Sports.title: Bayern Munich confirm Harry Kane ‘out for next few months’ with ankle injury
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich have confirmed Harry Kane will be “out for the next few months” with ankle ligament damage sustained in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday.

Kane was substituted after 20 minutes of the Bundesliga game, having been left limping after a challenge from the Cologne defender Joël Schmied. The Ballon d’Or winner was substituted and the returning Bayern coach, Vincent Kompany, said that the injury would take “months” rather than weeks to heal.

A club statement on X said: “Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against Köln on Friday evening. This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months.”

The Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore fired the visitors ahead before Kane’s injury, but Bayern levelled when Nathaniel Brown scored before the break. Bayern also lost Michael Olise to injury for the second half, and Said El Mala missed an excellent late chance to earn Cologne’s first win at Bayern since 2009.

The 33-year-old may face a race to be fit for the Nations League quarter-finals, the first leg of which takes place in Norway on 27 March – just over four months away. The Bayern sporting director, Max Eberl, said on Friday that club doctors were “discussing whether or not to recommend surgery” for Kane’s injury.

Part of Kane’s recovery period will come during the Bundesliga’s winter break from 20 December to 8 January. He will, however, miss Champions League games away to Lille next week and at home to Slavia Prague next month, as well as the January trip to Manchester United and the league phase finale at home to Real Betis.

View image in fullscreen Bayern Munich’s coach, Vincent Kompany, returned with his arm in a sling after dislocating his shoulder last month. Photograph: Heiko Becker/Reuters

Kane’s setback adds to an extensive Bayern injury list, with Olise also going off during Friday’s game with a foot contusion. Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and Manuel Neuer were already unavailable, leaving Kompany short of options for a busy month of fixtures.

Kompany returned from his own month-long absence for Friday’s game with his arm in a sling, having dislocated his shoulder when he collapsed on a training pitch in October. The Belgian was taken to hospital for meningeal irritation treatment after his collapse, and has been recovering at home.

“I think this result was fair and Cologne deserved the point,” Kompany said after the game. “We have other worries now, I have to honestly say. We will all try together to make something strong out of this situation. FC Bayern does that time and again, and that’s what we want to do now too.”

Cologne took a surprise lead with 12 minutes gone when Moore started and finished an excellent break. The teenage winger pounced on a mislaid Olise pass and drove forward, finding Linton Maina who laid off for El Mala, whose no-look backheel pass allowed Moore to round keeper Jonas Urbig before sliding the ball home.

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane stays down holding his lower leg after a challenge from Cologne’s Joël Schmied. Photograph: Heiko Becker/Reuters

Kane was then brought down in the Cologne box from behind by Schmied, who got the ball first but clattered into Kane’s left leg in his follow-through. Kane’s penalty appeals were waved away, but he was left visibly limping and received treatment on his ankle before being replaced by Tom Bischof on the 20-minute mark.

The hosts levelled 17 minutes later when full-back Brown sliced a low shot into the bottom-right corner, but suffered another blow just before the break when Olise went down. The France star did not return for the second half and was seen leaving the stadium shortly after on crutches – but it appears unlikely he will miss a significant amount of time.

Just before the hour mark, El Mala and Maina forced a spectacular double save from Urbig. El Mala, recently called up by Germany, then had a golden chance to put Cologne in front with eight minutes to go when one-on-one with Urbig – but he cut his close-range shot inches wide of the post.

Now a point behind Bayern, Borussia Dortmund can move into outright first place if they win at bottom club Mönchengladbach on Saturday. Freiburg can also move level on points with Bayern if they can defeat promoted Elversberg.

This month Kane signed a new deal with the Bundesliga giants until June 2029, which is reportedly worth in excess of £400,000 a week, making him the highest-paid player in Europe before bonuses.

Since arriving from Tottenham three years ago, Kane has scored an incredible 156 goals in 163 appearances, helping Bayern win a league and cup double last season.

Sports.title: Elon Musk’s lawyer joining Tom Brady in buying Chelsea stake
Sports.content:
Elon Musk’s lawyer is joining Tom Brady in buying a stake in Chelsea. The Guardian revealed on Friday that the much-decorated former NFL player is in discussions about purchasing a minority shareholding at Stamford Bridge and can now disclose that Alex Spiro of the New York law firm Quinn Emmanuel is also seeking to buy a stake by investing in Chelsea’s majority owners, Clearlake Capital.

Brady and Spiro, who is representing the planned Fifa investor Joshua Kushner in a legal battle against Uefa, would become limited partners in Clearlake with no voting rights at Chelsea if the transactions are completed.

Clearlake have been seeking additional investors since agreeing to buy the shares of their former partners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter for around £1bn in September, a deal that is due to be completed by the end of the year.

Clearlake will own 86.5% of Chelsea after buying out Boehly and Walter, who both held stakes of 12.9%, with the proposed investments of Brady and Spiro understood to be considerably smaller. As part of that transaction Boehly and Walter’s partner, the Swiss philanthropist Hansjorg Wyss, chose to stay at Chelsea by buying 12.9% of Clearlake’s shareholding.

Any other future investors such as Brady and Spiro would follow the same model.

Spiro has represented Musk since 2018 and advised on his $44bn (£33.6bn) purchase of Twitter (now X) in 2022, as well as working for other celebrity clients, including Alec Baldwin, Kim Kardashian and Jay-Z.

In 2019 he successfully defended Musk in a notorious defamation trial relating to comments he made about the rescuer of junior football players from a Thailand cave, while in 2024 his defence helped Baldwin’s acquittal on charges involuntary manslaughter after a cinematographer died on the set of his film Rust, when a prop revolver discharged a live round.

Last summer Spiro was also appointed to represent Kushner, whose company Thrive Capital was the lead investor in Gianni Infantino’s $4.2bn World Cup sell-off scheme, in a legal challenge from Uefa.

Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared, is facing court claims in the United States from Uefa’s lawyers to disclose all communications relating to Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise plan. Last week a New York court rejected a motion by two Fifa subsidiaries to dismiss Uefa’s claim, but the courts have yet to rule on the disclosure filing.

View image in fullscreen Lawyer Alex Spiro (left) alongside the actor Alec Baldwin, whom he helped acquit of involuntary manslaughter charges in 2024. Photograph: Ramsay de Give/Reuters

Brady owned a 3.3% stake in the Championship club Birmingham City until this month, with sources involved in his decision to sell those shares telling the Guardian that he was paving the way to invest in Chelsea.

The seven-time Super Bowl winner was a guest of Chelsea when they won the Club World Cup in New Jersey last year and has a good relationship with the Clearlake’s main power broker, Behdad Eghbali, who has led discussions on behalf of the club.

Brady bought into Birmingham in August 2023, less than a year after his second and final retirement from the NFL, following the club’s takeover by Tom Wagner’s Knighthead Capital.

The 49-year-old was appointed chair of the club’s advisory board and had a prominent role in the 2025 Amazon Prime documentary Built in Birmingham: Brady & the Blues, which made headlines when he questioned the “work ethic” of Wayne Rooney, who was the manager. Brady also owns a minority stake in the NFL team the Las Vegas Raiders, which he bought alongside Wagner.

Chelsea declined to comment.

Sports.title: Pochettino the connector: will human touch lift Manchester United?
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino celebrated his 50th birthday in style. It was March 2022, he was in charge at Paris Saint-Germain and the venue was a stunning boutique hotel; the kind that many capitals have but only Paris truly does. Pochettino’s family and friends were there. So were his inner coaching circle, who are basically family. There were lots of people from PSG. And a good time was had by all.

For Pochettino, it was emotional. As everybody knows, the new Manchester United head coach is the kind of guy to well up when the speeches start, so imagine how he felt when he looked up at the big screen and a video montage of well-wishers started to roll.

Pochettino’s PSG players were at the party. There was no need for anything from them. But there were loads from those he had coached at his previous clubs: Espanyol, Southampton and Tottenham. One by one, the faces flashed up; too many to mention. And, of course, there were the jokes about how old he was getting. But the tone was of pure affection; appreciation, too. Some of the players laid it on thick. They could not help it. They know what Pochettino has done for them.

This is what total buy-in looks like and this is how Pochettino gets you when he finds out which buttons to press. It might be a third-choice goalkeeper. Or a global superstar – for example, Kylian Mbappé, who Pochettino had at PSG. There is a story from those days that is worth sharing. Pochettino was due to give an interview and told the TV crew he would get Mbappé along to speak to them as well.

Everybody knows this is not how it works, that it would not be possible because Mbappé, well … he has his time and commitments tightly managed. They appreciated the sentiment from Pochettino, though. When the hour came, Pochettino took out his phone and messaged Mbappé. “Come to the media centre.” Five minutes later, there he was. A line from one of the production staff was gold. “Err, we’ve got Kylian Mbappé outside.”

This kind of thing is not confined to the dim and distant past. Remember when Pochettino left Chelsea in 2024 and the tributes some of the players paid to him on social media? One stood out because it came from Nicolas Jackson, who Pochettino had punished for getting too many silly yellow cards by ordering him to sprint around the training ground, reducing him to a face-in-the-ground mess when it was over. “Love you coach,” Jackson wrote. “Thanks for the advice and support. You’re a true lion and a fighter.”

It is easy to feel Pochettino has signed up for his biggest fight because it is not only that United have one Premier League win, a place in the relegation zone, no confidence, questionable fitness levels and a trip to Liverpool on Sunday which has the makings of root canal surgery without the anaesthetic.

Hanging heavy over everything is the fan fury towards the Glazer family, who have owned the club since 2005. It is obviously not a new thing. The diehards were passionately against them even before the takeover. But we are going through another period where the frustration has spiked and the malevolence can be heard in the chants. It is the insoluble problem, with the efforts of the minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the director of football, Jason Wilcox, making it worse. They have also been targeted by the Stretford End.

Pochettino knows managers do not tend to enter clubs when everything is rosy. There are reasons why the vacancies arise and they are almost always bad. He has told himself this. What he intends to do is what he has always done: create connections, starting with the players; inject his trademark positivity into every pore; build belief.

The Argentinian is obsessed with what he calls energia universal. It is a guiding life force that influences everything, which touches on concepts such as karma and what these days would probably be called manifestation. He once said it helped to explain, for example, why the London-born Harry Kane usually scored for Spurs in London derbies.

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino is obsessed with what he calls energia universal, a guiding life force that influences everything, touching on concepts such as karma. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images

Pochettino wants to release the pressure from United’s beleaguered squad and his early messaging has come from his tried and trusted playbook. He will treat each player as a human being, first and foremost, with individual needs. And, if necessary, individually tailored programmes. At Southampton, he put one together for Luke Shaw, then an emerging player. He has been reunited with the left-back at Old Trafford.

Pochettino talked at his media conference on Friday of having had three hours of one-on-one meetings with the players on Thursday; trying to understand what was happening with them on and off the field. Previously, in his opening address to the United fanbase via the club’s in-house channels, he stressed the importance of everybody “connecting together”.

“The responsibility I feel is energy, it’s excitement,” he said. “To connect with the game we need to feel free. The players need to express their talent and we need to create the environment for them to perform. That is the priority.”

Pochettino has been close to the United job before – most notably in the summer of 2022 when he left PSG. It was either him or Erik ten Hag to take over from the interim Ralf Rangnick, who had declared that United needed “open-heart surgery”. What do they need now?! The club went for Ten Hag.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Pochettino was in United’s thoughts when they looked for a successor to Louis van Gaal in May 2016; he had lunch with Sir Alex Ferguson at Scott’s in London that month. It was believed Ferguson was pushing him as a candidate. United appointed José Mourinho. There was also the period after Mourinho’s dismissal in December 2018 and the interim hire of Ole Gunnar Solskjær when Pochettino was tipped to go to Old Trafford. In the end, Solskjær earned the role on a permanent basis.

Why are United turning now to a manager they have previously overlooked? Pochettino is not about to dwell on that because he is in dream-come-true territory. He will love how the United support stand behind their manager, especially in troublesome times. He will love the pageantry and event glamour of Old Trafford. And he will love having Ferguson in the crowd for the matches.

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino had a good relationship with Kylian Mbappé when he was in charge at Paris Saint-Germain. Photograph: Enric Fontcuberta/EPA

Pochettino first encountered him in January 2013 when, in his second Southampton game, he went to Old Trafford to face Ferguson’s United, who won 2-1. Pochettino has mentioned that this week. And the meal at Scott’s. And how he was at the Camp Nou for Ferguson’s finest hour: the 1999 Champions League final victory against Bayern Munich. Pochettino was an Espanyol player at the time, together with Toni Jiménez, who is part of his coaching staff, and they watched the first half from so-so seats before blagging their way into the directors’ box for the second period.

When Solskjær scored his iconic late winner, Pochettino and Jiménez celebrated wildly. They were caught up in the moment. It was the first time Pochettino felt a connection to United and he began to pay more attention to them. And Ferguson. Pochettino described him this week as “the best coach in the history of the sport” but it was not a soundbite of convenience. He has always maintained this and said so on the record after the lunch at Scott’s.

How can Pochettino position himself in terms of the Glazers and Ratcliffe? The first thing to say is that he does have experience of unpopular and/or difficult owners. At Spurs, Daniel Levy was forever maligned by the fans, and Pochettino had problems with the American ownership at Chelsea. Between times, the Qataris at PSG were not easy. Pochettino worked to build a relationship with Levy, regularly saying nice things about him in the press and famously including him on a staff-bonding trip to Argentina.

It featured white-water rafting and ended with Pochettino having to fish Levy out of the Manso River. A repeat of the adventure with Joel Glazer feels unlikely but Pochettino’s starting point at United has been to stress unity; the need to create chemistry with everyone, including “the directors and the owners”.

And so to Anfield, where Pochettino first managed with Southampton in September 2013 when his team won 1-0. He has not tasted victory in his eight subsequent trips; seven with Spurs, one with Chelsea, the record shows two draws and six defeats. No United fan expects anything this time but Pochettino considers it a great game to have. He will certainly learn a lot about his players.

Sports.title: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet
Sports.content:
Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.

He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session.

“We’ll do maybe two days on, one day off, and then three days on, one day off,” says Peters. “We’ve been doing that for just over a year now. It’s full-on. It’s pretty much as if you were at a club.”

Dele rose as a teenager to a level of stardom few experience and, used to media attention, doesn’t mind that his absence from football draws scrutiny. But he disagrees with the suggestion that choosing to stream on Twitch is a sign he has lost interest in the game that made him wealthy enough to never need to work again.

View image in fullscreen Dele celebrates scoring for Spurs against Arsenal in 2018. Photograph: Alex Morton/Getty

To a modest Twitch audience, he sometimes plays video games, sometimes just talks. He has a knack for creating viral content, sharing a phone call with Harry Kane and playing a game of EA Sports FC with IShowSpeed, one of the most famous online influencers. When he lost that game – and a bet – he wore an Arsenal shirt, apologising to Spurs fans before burning it. When TalkSport pundits claimed Dele was wasting his potential by becoming a streamer, Dele responded in a live stream, pointing out he was recording himself in his spare time and if he was out at nightclubs, it would be worse. Even then he was polite.

“When people see him online streaming or whatever he does in his private time, the initial thought is: ‘He’s done with football, then,’” Peters says. “He’s been training for a year and a half by himself. If he was done with football he wouldn’t be doing that. His actions show that the hunger is still there. A lot of people would come out of the game and then stop and lose the hunger for it, but he’s still chipping away every day, trying to get back and get to somewhere that he’s happy with.”

Dele broke through at MK Dons as a slight but devilish defensive midfielder, dominating League One midfields full of hardened professionals, before being scouted by Tottenham. Mauricio Pochettino attended MK Dons’ 4-0 League Cup win against Manchester United in 2014 and saw enough to leave early and convince Daniel Levy to pay £5m.

By the time Dele turned 21, his statistics were superior to Cristiano Ronaldo’s at the same age: 26 goals and 14 assists to Ronaldo’s 14 and 13. His 40 goal involvements equalled Frank Lampard, Steven Gerrard and David Beckham combined at the same age.

“He’s scored more in his first 50 league games than Steven Gerrard, Wayne Rooney and Frank Lampard,” Pochettino wrote in his book Brave New World. “He may go on to be better than all of them because he has the quality; now he just needs consistency.”

But there were, perhaps, warning signs of what would happen at Spurs. One source who worked closely with Dele describes him as a “cheeky chappy”; charming and universally popular.

View image in fullscreen Dele Alli during his time with Como. He made one appearance, off the bench against Milan, and was sent off nine minutes later. Photograph: Paolo Bruno/Getty Images

He wasn’t one to miss training, but there were concerns he wasn’t leading the pristine lifestyle of many elite players, and tabloid stories about his private life trailed him. Pochettino was concerned when he saw Dele’s WhatsApp photo, a cartoon of a boy surrounded by people wanting a piece of him, believing he needed support from the right people. John McDermott, the head of coaching and development, said: “When the trough is full, the pigs come from all over to feed.”

When Dele voluntarily liquidated one of his companies this month, documents showed an estimated surplus after costs of £7.6m, suggesting the 30-year-old has not squandered the millions he earned at his peak in wages and sponsorship agreements, including a five-year deal with Adidas. He also owns a property portfolio worth more than £1.5m.

In the early days Pochettino warned Dele about the danger of not giving maximum effort in matches and training, a sentiment later shared by José Mourinho when he became Spurs manager. “I think one day you will regret, if you don’t reach what you can reach,” Mourinho told Dele in his office as Amazon Prime’s cameras rolled.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Although Dele formed a formidable relationship with Kane on the pitch, and was twice named the Professional Footballers’ Association’s men’s young player of the year while playing behind the striker, he was closer to Eric Dier off it. And perhaps it was those anchors – Pochettino and Dier – that Dele lost later in his career.

His time with Pochettino was fondly remembered. For the Argentinian’s 50th birthday celebrations, Dele recorded a heartfelt video for his former manager. “The message was beautiful,” says one party-goer.

In almost five years since leaving Spurs, he has made one league start at Everton and 10 at Besiktas, before a loan at Como, where Cesc Fàbregas tried to rediscover the player he once was. He came off the bench once and was sent off nine minutes later.

Dele, according to those close to him, is biding his time to get his next move right. He will be 31 in April and wants a suitable contract. He has spoken to a host of clubs, with interest from the Premier League and the Championship, and from the Middle East, where he has been tempted by the riches of the Saudi Pro League, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar. There has also been interest from Major League Soccer and he has held talks with clubs in Brazil and Japan. It is believed he will join a club this season.

View image in fullscreen Dele on debut for England, a Euro 2016 qualifier against Estonia in October 2015. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

In preparation, Peters is also guiding Dele’s nutrition, though he does not require much guidance. “Del’s a weird one, because he doesn’t snack, he doesn’t eat unhealthily, he doesn’t have a Sprite or a Coke or whatever. He’s never really been that kind of guy. All he does is drink coconut water, and he’ll have a small lunch, or his cheat day will be a Nando’s or something.”

Happiness is his priority. He spoke candidly on Gary Neville’s The Overlap in 2023 about his struggles with mental health and an addiction to sleeping pills after revealing abuse as a child. “Because he’s had such a long time out, he’s like: ‘What’s another few months if it means that I’m going to find something I’m actually happy with?’” Peters says. The aim is to “carry on for as long as possible”.

For the time being, Dele’s days are simple. When not training, he goes for coffee or a swim, and he has taken up padel. “He’s very much a person that’s happy with the little things,” Peters says. “He’s always the person that’s positive, the one that, if the group’s down or whatever, is going to pick everyone up. He’s happy with what he’s doing. His main happiness is playing football, and that’s what he wants to do.”

Sports.title: Three players Arsenal tipped to sell in clearout to future-proof squad
Sports.content:
Three players Arsenal tipped to sell in clearout to future-proof squad

Arsenal have been urged to cash in on Viktor Gyokeres, Martin Zubimendi and Eberechi Eze while they still can.

The Gunners have moved to secure the long-term future of a number of key players, with Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber and David Raya all closing in on new contracts.

5 Viktor Gyokeres was Aresnal's top scorer in the 2025/26 campaign

talkSPORT understands Rice and Timber have agreed long-term contract extensions at the Emirates, following in the footsteps of Bukayo Sakaand manager Mikel Arteta.

Goalkeeper Raya is set to be the next of Arsenal’s title-winning heroes to extend their stays, alongside captain Martin Odegaard.

With the quartet all established senior players, their new deals are expected to take them into their late twenties and early thirties respectively.

They form part of a growing number of Arteta's core group who are tied down at the club into their senior years.

Influential centre-back Gabriel is also contracted at the Emirates until 2029 - at which point he will be 31 - and it's a similar story for 2025 summer transfer window star signings Gyokeres, Zubimendi and Eze.

The trio were the Gunners' three most expensive arrivals last year - costing a combined £178.7million and all signed long-term deals.

However, all three now face uncertain futures, with Gyokeres being tipped to leave after struggling for game time this term, while Zubimendi and Eze have both had to settle for bit part roles too.

'Big name departures'

With Arsenal at risk of having too many senior players tied down on long-term, talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook has urged them to consider cutting their losses.

He said on talkSPORT: “There's something to be said for keeping your best players, particularly at a time when teams around you are weaker - in the case of Manchester City, they're probably going to be hit with a points deduction.

“But they need to regenerate as well.

5 Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice are both set to commit their futures to Arsenal Credit: Getty

5 Eberechi Eze joined Arsenal in a mouth-watering £60million deal, but this season has proved a mixed bag Credit: AFP

"Alex Ferguson was always so good at that when Manchester United were at their pump. Knowing when to move players on and when to bring in fresh blood.

"I think there will be a couple of big name departures next summer. At the moment, I think Victor Gyokeres’ career lies elsewhere.

"Zubimendi might try and get away as early as January from what I'm hearing. And maybe Eze as well might decide elsewhere.”

Despite netting 20 goals in all competitions last season, Gyokeres has failed to convince as Arsenal's first-choice striker.

This term he has played second fiddle to Kai Havertz, starting just six of his 14 appearances - only one of which has come in the Premier League - and scoring twice.

Meanwhile Zubimendi enjoyed a memorable debut season with the Gunners, making 57 appearances in total as he lifted the Premier League title, but has fallen down the pecking order this term.

5 Zubimendi's future at Arsenal is in doubt - just a year after his £55million from Real Sociedad Credit: Getty

The Spaniard has been less of a presence this term, starting just twice following the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes in the summer.

Eze has also experienced a drop-off this term, starting six of the 14 games he has played in, and was brutally hooked at half-time in Arsenal's win at Nottingham Forest in October.

Arsenal's contract situations worried Crook's co-host Sam Matterface who said: “The fact is that Rice, Raya, Gabriel, Eze, Gyokeres, Ezri Konsa, Guimaraes and Zubimendi are all going to be contracted into their 30s on what you would suggest is big wages.

"Could that leave Arsenal in a difficult selling position? Because it's alright saying they'll want to move Eze next summer. Or they want to move on Zubimendi.

“Those players are not going to go unless they can get value out of their contracts.”

While fellow presenter Gabby Agbonlahor agreed it is important for Arsenal to secure their key players, he admitted the club can't afford for everyone to stay.

5 Mikel Arteta may have to make some ruthless calls Credit: Getty

On the trio Crook tipped to leave, Agbonlahor argued: “They've not been performing. Especially Zubimendi - he lost his place. What is he now? Third, fourth choice now in midfield.

“Gyokeres isn't the answer. It's not worked out. So those players you'll get money for.

“But your Gabriels, your Konsas - players like that, they're going to be key to Arsenal for many years. I don't see Konsa slowing down into his 30s.”

Sports.title: Mikey Moore recall clause clarified as Tottenham loanee announces himself in Bundesliga
Sports.content:
Mikey Moore has arrived in the Bundesliga.

The 19-year-old winger scored his first goal for FC Köln in the 1-1 draw against Bayern Munich on Friday and was named Man of the Match.

3 Mikey Moore got his first Bundesliga goal for Koln in the 1-1 draw away to Bayern Munich Credit: Getty



It has been a difficult start to life in Germany for the Tottenham Hotspur loanee who had just one assist in eight appearances entering the match against the Bundesliga leaders.

But Moore took full opportunity to shine in front of the Allianz Arena crowd and share the pitch with fellow former Spurs academy product - and Moore's idol - Harry Kane, albeit for just 20 minutes.

This is because the 2026 Ballon d'Or winner's night was cut short after suffering a torn ligament in his left ankle which required surgery.

In the 12th minute, Moore and Köln teammate Said El Mala combined on the counter attack with the Englishman calmly slotting the ball past goalkeeper Jonas Urbig for the early 1-0 lead.



Bayern equalised before half time through summer signing Nathaniel Brown, but neither team was able to find a winner in the second half.

"It was a really good feeling," Moore said of scoring his first goal for the club.



"We combined really well, and then I tried to stay calm at the end. I hadn't scored yet, so I was afraid I might panic in front of goal."

Moore fought his way into the game, and contested more duels than any other Cologne player (11) while he also covered more ground than anyone else, running 12.5 kilometres.



"It's great that Mikey capped it off with a goal. It's a step in the right direction," Köln director of football Thomas Kessler said, via Kicker.

"We can take a big dose of confidence from this game. It was a very good, courageous performance. We need to build on that."

3 Moore has had a difficult start to life in Germany with just one goal and one assist in nine Bundesliga appearances Credit: Getty

3 Moore now believes he has fully settled, amid speculation his loan could be terminated Credit: Getty



Moore to stay in Bundesliga

After a poor start to life in the Bundesliga - a stark contrast to his - previous loan spell at Scottish Premiership giants Rangers - speculation was growing that Moore's loan spell could be terminated in January.

However, there is reportedly no clause in Moore's agreement that would allow Tottenham to recall him prematurely.

Although Moore admitted that his start to life in Germany had been 'up and down', he believes that he has now fully settled in and is optimistic that this "can translate to the pitch."

Therefore, it is expected that the teenager will see out the rest of the 2026/27 season at RheinEnergieStadion.



As for what he hopes to achieve during the remainder of his spell at Koln, that's simple for Moore.

"Just to help the team get as high up the table as possible," he stated. " I want to be a good player on the pitch, help the team off it too, and be a big part of getting us up the table and finishing in a really good position in the league."

After 10 games, Köln remain in 14th place in the league on 10 points, just four points above the relegation zone.

Sports.title: Why Erling Haaland’s goal had to be disallowed as explanation emerges
Sports.content:
Why Erling Haaland’s goal had to be disallowed as explanation emerges

The Premier League have explained why Erling Haaland's equaliser against Fulham was disallowed, in a decision which left the Norwegian furious.

With Manchester City trailing 1-0, Haaland thought he had levelled things in the 25th minute after Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno failed to gather his initial effort.



5 Haaland couldn't believe it when his equaliser was chalked off Credit: Getty

5 The Norwegian bundled the ball home, and Credit: Getty

City's talisman was on hand to stab the ball home, but his effort was quickly ruled out by referee Tom Bramall.

The match official ruled that he had kicked it out of Leno's hands, which left Haaland visibly furious.



Replays showed Leno appeared to have both hands on the ball, although there were questions over whether the Fulham stopper was actually in control of it.

But the Premier League Match Centre have now cleared things up by providing an explanation for the decision on social media.



A post on X read: "The referee’s call of free-kick to Fulham and no goal to Manchester City was checked and confirmed by VAR – with the goalkeeper deemed to be in control of the ball.

"VAR: 'The ball is in control between both hands and then is played out of that possession by the attacker, and then into the back of the net.'



Rules expert Dale Johnson also backed up the decision, insisting the referee was left no choice given that Leno had the ball in his hands.

He tweeted: "Erling Haaland's goal had to be disallowed.

"Bernd Leno had the ball between his hands when Haaland made first contact with the ball. It's an automatic free-kick.

"The 'level' of the goalkeeper's control is irrelevant."

5 The Premier League Match Centre insisted Leno was in control of the ball when Haaland poked home Credit: Getty

The controversy came after Rodrigo Muniz had given Fulham a shock 16th-minute lead at the Etihad.



This saw City's recent woes continue, who headed into the lunchtime clash off the back of three successive Premier League defeats.

Before the international break, the Citizens were 3-1 by strugglers Nottingham Forest, which followed back-to-back losses to Brighton and Aston Villa.

The poor run of form has seen Enzo Maresca's side lose ground in the title race, who now sit third in the table, six points off leaders Arsenal.

And while defeat to Fulham would deal a major blow to City's title hopes, they later grabbed an equaliser which was allowed to stand.



In the 57th minute, Elliot Anderson volleyed home superbly from the edge of the box to bring his side level, with this his first Premier League goal since his £116million summer arrival.

5 Rodrigo Muniz put Fulham 1-0 up with his second goal in two games Credit: Getty

5 Elliot Anderson eventually grabbed Man City's equaliser in the second half Credit: AFP

With Arsenal not in action until 5:30pm when they travel to Newcastle, victory for City would close the gap on the league leaders to three points.

Sports.title: Duncan Ferguson sent off for first time in managerial career – moments after team score
Sports.content:
Duncan Ferguson sent off for first time in managerial career – moments after team score

Du ncan Ferguson was sent off as his unbeaten start as Glentoran manager came to an end in dramatic circumstances.

The Everton great suffered his first defeat as Glentoran boss as they were edged out 3-2 by Cliftonville in an Irish Premiership clash.



3 Duncan Ferguson returned to management with Glentoran after a two-year hiatus Credit: Getty

Ferguson was appointed to take charge of the Belfast club in October, and had enjoyed an unbeaten start in his first three games.

However, it all came to an end on Friday night, and he wasn't even on the touchline when the final whistle blew on his first defeat.

Fiery Ferguson sees red

After picking up nine red cards in his playing career - including a joint-record eight in the Premier League - Ferguson was given his marching orders for the first time as a manager.



In the first-half, he lost his temper in the aftermath of his side falling behind, having been left furious at Cliftonville's opener.

Ferguson angrily protested after believing there was a foul on defender Jarlath O'Rourke in the build-up from Liam McStravick, who then set up Joe Sheridan to score the opener.



The fiery Scot was so incensed that he continued to argue while his side equalised just a minute later through Cal Weatherup.

But an equaliser was unable to calm Ferguson, who was subsequently shown a straight red card by referee Ben McMaster for his outburst.



Without their manager in the dugout, Glentoran ultimately slumped to defeat in dramatic circumstances.

They fell behind to a Brian Healy strike in the 67th minute before equalising again through James Douglas with four minutes left.

However, Cliftonville took the three points thanks to a second goal of the night from Sheridan in the 88th minute.

3 Glentoran are the third club Ferguson has managed on a permanent basis in his career



The defeat ended Glentoran's eight-game unbeaten run in the league and leaves them well off the pace in pursuit of their first league title since 2009.

This was their fifth league defeat of the campaign, and they now sit 14 points behind leaders Linfield.

With Ferguson being given his marching orders in the first-half, it fell to his assistant Gary Bollan to take charge for the rest of the game.

And Bollan was also left to handle media duties afterwards, where he admitted Ferguson's red card had a major impact on the game.



He said: "I think the manager got frustrated because it was a foul. It changes the dynamic [the sending off].

"He's a leader, I've then got to step in and fill his boots and it's a big set of boots to fill."

3 Ferguson worked alongside Carlo Ancelotti during their time together at Everton Credit: Getty

Ferguson took charge Glentoran in October as he succeeded Declan Devine in the dugout.



It marked a return to management after a two year hiatus following the end of his spell with Inverness Caledonian Thistle.

Ferguson has previously managed Forest Green Rovers and had a brief role as interim manager at Everton after working on the coaching staff under Carlo Ancelotti.

As a player, Ferguson scored 68 Premier League goals — the most by a Scottish player — across two spells with Everton and one with Newcastle.

He was also part of the Everton side that won the club's most recent major trophy, the 1994/95 FA Cup.

Sports.title: Premier League clubs put on red alert as Jamal Musiala release clause revealed amid Bayern concerns
Sports.content:
Premier League clubs are expected to be on red alert amid fears at Bayern Munich that Jamal Musiala’s wages are no longer feasible.

The 23-year-old was diagnosed with a fainting condition in the summer after collapsing on the pitch twice in just a few days.



3 Musiala reportedly has a release clause that activates in the summer Credit: Getty

Musiala has appeared in eight matches this season, but has currently been out for the last two months with a muscle injury.

Speaking on Friday evening, Former Bayern chief Karl-Heinz Rummenigge told Sky Germany: “(Musiala) has a health-related issue. It's also well known that he has a contract involving very substantial sums of money. As a club, we have to consider how to deal with that situation. I think that's responsible and perfectly normal.

“What we know unfortunately suggests it will be difficult for him to get back to the level he has often shown here in this stadium.”



Rummenigge continued: “[We need to] talk to the player, to the family and, above all, to the agency, because, with all due respect, those sums are then no longer feasible.”

“I think we’ve handled the player’s situation very carefully, and we all want him to return, ideally in the best possible shape.



“But what happens if that doesn’t work out? Then, of course, we’ll also have to continue taking the financial implications into account.”

Musiala contract

The Germany international is currently under contract at Bayern until 2030 and earns a reported £20.9m-a-year.



Reports in Germany claim that this contract includes a release clause that will become active in 2027.

Musiala has long been linked to a move to the Premier League, with Man City often touted as a destination. He was previously seen as a successor to Kevin De Bruyne.

Arsenal and Liverpool have long-term interest, meanwhile Chelsea, his former youth club, have also been linked.

3 Musiala [right] was a star in Chelsea's academy and won the league with the Under-18s Credit: 2019 The Arsenal Football Club Plc



talkSPORT verdict

European football expert Kevin Hatchard joined talkSPORT on Friday evening to talk about Musiala - and said the decision makers still back the player.

He said: “Jamal Musiala has had a horrible time in the last year and a half. A couple of summers ago, he had that clash with Donnarumma.

“Donnarumma dived for a ball that was on the floor and he kind of came through Musiala's leg to get there. That's not me blaming Donnarumma. That's just what happens sometimes.

“It's just really unfortunate. That was a break of the leg and there was some ankle damage there as well. So that was a really complicated injury.



“He's been out for the last eight weeks with a muscle tear. But in the middle of all that, it's emerged that he's been dealing with this neurological condition, which has caused him to have a couple of fainting fits. That's just what we know about. So he's on medication for that.

“Uli Hoeneß is the honorary president and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who's a Bayern legend as well, and was the CEO for a long time. What they say still carries weight, even though they haven't got official admin positions per se.

3 Musiala also featured four times for Germany at the World Cup Credit: Getty

“They've both said that they're concerned that Musiala won't be able to regain his best form and that if that's the case, maybe he shouldn't be getting 25 million euros a year.



“That's a contract they've committed to and Max Eberl, thankfully, who is the senior sporting director there, he's come out and said, look, this is a human, first of all, that we like very much and that we respect very much. And he's still a very talented player.

“The people that matter and have the most important voices at Bayern are still in his camp and are still very locked into getting him back to where he was.

“There's no doubt that since the injury, he's not been the player that we know. But the kid's 23. So I think we can cut him some slack. He's shown already what he's capable of.

I still believe he can get back to where he was.”

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho immediately shuts down JJ Gabriel question with blunt reply
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho refused to discuss Real Madrid's pursuit of JJ Gabriel, insisting he has 'nothing to say'.

Sixteen-year-old sensation Gabriel confirmed his departure from Manchester United on Tuesday in a social media post.



3 JJ Gabriel has been branded a star of the future, but that will lie away from Old Trafford Credit: Getty

It brought an end to a long-running saga after it was first announced in September that Gabriel had asked to leave the Red Devils.

The youngster is now understood to be on the brink of finalising a switch to Real Madrid.

A move to a foreign club has been permitted since Gabriel turned 16 last month despite being registered to United, although there could be further fall-out if it is found out that he was approached illegally.



But with a move to Spain now appearing just a matter of time, Real Madrid boss Mourinho was asked for an update on this.

Mourinho coy on Gabriel

Despite Gabriel looking destined for the Santiago Bernabeu, Mourinho shut down any talk of this in his press conference on Friday.



When asked about Madrid’s pursuit of Gabriel, The Special One shook his head and said: "I have nothing to say."

After being reminded that Gabriel had visited Madrid’s training complex during the international break, Mourinho replied: "No, no, not with me.



"I have a good feeling about my players. I have a good rapport with the players who I work with every day.

"I have a good feeling about the players who are available to me.

"I have no feelings for players who don’t work with me."

3 Jose Mourinho refused to be drawn on Gabriel and his links to Real Madrid Credit: Getty

Earlier this week, Gabriel confirmed his departure from United by posting a farewell message to the club on social media.

The teenager requested to be de-registered with the Red Devils in September after being left unhappy at a lack of first-team opportunities.



In an Instagram video, he said: “You gave me moments I will always treasure. To every coach and every member of staff, to my teammates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

“As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything, JJ.”

Despite bidding an emotional farewell, Gabriel is currently still registered with Man United.

And United are understood to be considering legal action against any club trying to sign him while still on the club's books.



3 Gabriel departs Man United having never made a first team appearance Credit: Getty

Berrada: United pushed to keep Gabriel

While Gabriel's future away from Old Trafford is all but sealed, Man United CEO Omar Berrada has insisted the club 'did everything' to keep the teenager.

Berrada told Sky Sports: "We did everything. Absolutely everything. Let's not forget with JJ, he's a very young boy with a lot of media attention around him. Our primary concern is his well-being...

"Credit to the academy and people that have been here for many years, they helped him in his development. We still think this is the best place for him to continue his career and to grow.



"This club has a very rich history and tradition of developing young players and giving them the opportunity, as we're seeing this season with Shea Lacey. Obviously, Kobbie Mainoo has been doing well for us for a few years now - we're not afraid of giving young players opportunities.

"Obviously, him and his family have taken the decision to leave. We can only wish him the best.

"We want players that want to be here, that feel being at Manchester United is a privilege."

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino built £157m Premier League phenomenon with win at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino will be aiming to achieve a 13-year first when he takes charge of his maiden Manchester United match this weekend.

The Red Devils travel to Anfield to take on Liverpool on Sunday, with kick-off at 4.30pm.

4 Pochettino takes United to Anfield in his first match as manager on Sunday Credit: Getty

It marks the first match of Pochettino's tenure after he replaced Michael Carrick as manager on a two-and-a-half year deal.

However, the Argentine will have to overcome his poor personal record at Anfield as a manager.

Pochettino is winless in eight visits and has claimed victory away against Liverpool just once in nine meetings.

His only previous triumph came with a Southampton side which went on to earn the club over £150million in transfer fees.

Pochettino's famous Anfield win

Just eight months into his reign with the Saints, Pochettino masterminded a 1-0 victory over Liverpool on September 21, 2013.

Dejan Lovren's second half goal proved to be the winner as he headed home Adam Lallana's corner.

The pair were amongst four members of the matchday squad who would later be bought by the Reds.

Meanwhile, of the 14 players used by Pochettino that day, Southampton fetched an initial £157.5million in the transfer market.

With add-ons, those fees rose to roughly £164.5million as 11 players were sold and a further three departed for free.

Unused substitute Calum Chambers was also sold to Arsenal for £16million in 2016.

4 Lovren scored the only goal as Pochettino's Southampton beat Liverpool in September 2013 Credit: Getty

His departure takes the overall value of the 18-man matchday squad to £173.5million before factoring in potential add-ons.

Those sales include Nathaniel Clyne and Rickie Lambert's moves to Liverpool from the Saints.

They joined Lovren and Lallana, who were both part of the Reds side which beat Pochettino's Tottenham Hotspur to win the Champions League in 2019.

Elsewhere, United themselves swooped to sign Luke Shaw and Morgan Schneiderlin, with the former still at Old Trafford today.

Southampton also secured fees for James Ward-Prowse, Jay Rodriguez, Victor Wanyama, Jose Fonte and Jack Cork upon their exits.

The only players to leave for nothing were free transfers Artur Boruc and Steven Davis as well as Dani Osvaldo, who had his contract terminated in 2015.

4 Southampton made £157.5million in transfer fees from the side which beat Liverpool Credit: Getty

Transfer Fee Breakdown (Players Who Featured)

Player Role in 2013 Match Sold To Year Reported Fee (Initial) Luke Shaw Starter (LB) Man United 2014 £30m James Ward-Prowse Sub (on 76') West Ham United 2023 £30m Adam Lallana Starter (AM) Liverpool 2014 £25m Morgan Schneiderlin Starter (CM) Man United 2015 £24m Dejan Lovren Starter (CB) Liverpool 2014 £20m Jay Rodriguez Starter (FW) West Bromwich Albion 2017 £12m Nathaniel Clyne Starter (RB) Liverpool 2015 £12.5m Victor Wanyama Starter (CM) Tottenham Hotspur 2016 £11m José Fonte Starter (CB) West Ham United 2017 £8m Rickie Lambert Starter (FW) Liverpool 2014 £4m Jack Cork Sub (on 89') Swansea City 2015 £3m Artur Boruc Starter (GK) Bournemouth 2015 £0 Dani Osvaldo Starter (FW) Contract terminated 2015 £0 Steven Davis Sub (on 66') Rangers 2019 £0 Total £157.5m

As for Pochettino, he would guide the Saints to an eighth place finish in the 2013/14 season, their best performance for 11 years.

It ultimately earned him a move to Spurs at the end of the campaign following 18 months in charge at St. Mary's.

However, he has failed to replicate his maiden win at Anfield since.

In eight visits with Tottenham and Chelsea, Pochettino has picked up just two draws and suffered six defeats,

The most recent trip came in January 2024, with his Blues side beaten 4-1 by Liverpool.

United's recent Anfield record

United's own recent record at Anfield is equally concerning for supporters.

4 United have only won one of their last 11 trips to Anfield Credit: Getty

The Red Devils have won just one of their last 11 trips in all competitions.

Those visits include a 7-0 thrashing in March 2023 as well as a 4-0 defeat the previous season.

However, United have avoided defeat in their three most recent away matches against Liverpool.

Under Ruben Amorim, meanwhile, they won 2-1 in this fixture last season thanks to a late Harry Maguire goal.

As for their opponents, Liverpool have only won one home Premier League match this season.

Their 2-0 victory over Brighton last month is their only Anfield triumph in seven home league outings dating back to May.
