Sports.title: Erling Haaland sees Man City equaliser DISALLOWED in controversial circumstances - with fans and pundits split over whether Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno had both hands on the ball after fumbled strike
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland saw a first half equaliser controversially disallowed against Fulham, as Enzo Maresca's side only managed to fight back to earn a disappointing draw.

Haaland latched onto a beautifully bent cross from Iliman Ndiaye to bundle home from less than eight minutes after Rodrigo Muniz had given the visitors a shock lead at the Etihad.

But despite Bernd Leno appearing to fumble the ball over the line and the referee's watch flashing to signify a goal, the man in the middle ruled the equaliser out for a foul on the Cottagers goalkeeper.

The decision has left both fans and pundits torn over whether the decision was harsh or whether it was the right call.

Former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Karen Carney said her mind changed after having watched a replay of the incident.

Speaking on TNT Sports from the Etihad, she said: 'My initial reaction was I thought the goalkeeper didn’t have control of it, and it should've been a goal, but then when you slow it down, (you can see it).

Erling Haaland has the ball in the back of the net, but it’s ruled out! ❌



📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/sKqY8Q7a9Z — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 21, 2026

Erling Haaland has a first half equaliser for Man City chalked off against Fulham

'People are going to shout at me through the TV. But I think the referee made the right decision.'

Tottenham legend Glenn Hoddle, also on punditry duty in Manchester, felt the same.

He said: 'I don’t know whether he had control of it, but I don’t think that comes into it. I think that’s the right decision, but it’s a very tough call. It could have gone either way.'

The Premier League Match Centre clarified why the decision was made by Tom Bramall and the VAR team in Stockley Park.

A statement on social media read: 'The referee’s call of free-kick to Fulham and no goal to Manchester City was checked and confirmed by VAR – with the goalkeeper deemed to be in control of the ball.'

They added that the VAR said: 'The ball is in control between both hands and then is played out of that possession by the attacker, and then into the back of the net.'

The laws of the game state that a goalkeeper is believed to be in control of the ball when the ball is 'between their hands/arms or between their hand(s)/arm(s) and any surface'.

Not all fans, of a Manchester City persuasion or not, felt that the right decision was made. Some believed that both Haaland and City should feel hard done by.

Haaland was left in disbelief by the referee's decision with many fans feeling the same

An Arsenal fan made their stance clear: 'Even as a rival, I honestly think this Haaland goal should’ve stood for Manchester City. Would’ve been p***** off if a Gyokeres goal like this for Arsenal was cancelled.'

A different fan added: 'Manchester City has been robbed. Haaland scored a clean goal here. The ball went in even before Haaland had contact with the keeper.

Not everyone agreed, though, with many X users taking the opposite stance.

One said: 'It’s explicitly a foul under the Laws. Don’t blame the ref if you don’t like the laws.'

Another user wrote: 'I am also an Arsenal fan but the ball is still in two-palm contact. If you allow it, you will encourage outfield player challenging the save attempt And a foot to hand challenge will much more often lead to a broken wrist or thumb. That is an unfair advantage to outfield players.'

City did go on to equalise in the second half, with Elliot Anderson bagging his first Premier League goal for the club by smashing home a sublime volley in the 57th minute.

Sports.title: Harry Brook fireworks eclipsed by brilliant Nikhil Chaudhary as England squander chance to inflict more misery on Aussies in dramatic MCG finish
Sports.content:
England blew a golden chance to inflict more misery on Australian cricket when they lost the first T20 at the MCG by three wickets – after a Harry Brook special had threatened to take the game out of reach.

Australia were in desperate need of a good-news story after a fortnight in which the resurrection of Sandpapergate has dominated the headlines, on front and back pages and across continents. To make matters worse, they then lost the three-match ODI series to their oldest rivals after going 1-0 up.

And their second-stringers looked there for the taking when England, asked to bat, raced to 110 for two in the ninth over, with Brook in full flow and a total of 200 on the cards.

But he was caught behind for 65 off 28 trying to nudge Nikhil Chaudhary’s leg-breaks to third man, and England lost momentum.

With Tom Banton falling in the next over for a 22-ball 39, and Sam Curran chewing up 20 deliveries for his 21, Australia clawed their way back. In all, the last 11 overs and one ball produced an anaemic 77 runs and seven wickets.

Chaudhary, the first Indian-born male cricketer to represent Australia for over 60 years, was central to the fightback, taking two for 21 in only his fourth T20 international, then masterminding Australia’s chase of 188 in front of a crowd of nearly 40,000 that included his parents, who had flown over from India.

England blew a golden chance to inflict more misery on Australian cricket in the wake of the Sandpapergate scandal

Chaudhary, the first Indian-born male cricketer to represent Australia for over 60 years, was central to the fightback

With wickets falling regularly, he hit a classy 66 off 38 balls to take his side within 20 of victory, engaged in a verbal spat with Curran – ‘I think he was mad I got his wicket’ – before flicking Jamie Overton to Aneurin Donald at deep square leg. Jack Edwards then finished the job with a ball to spare.

And England’s mood was not helped when vice-captain Will Jacks had to leave the field in the 19th over with blood pouring from his right hand after dropping a tough chance off his own bowling.

Jacks is supposed to take over the captaincy for the fifth and final T20 in Canberra when Brook leaves early for the Test series in South Africa, but a glance at his injury suggested he may struggle. Asked who would take the armband if Jacks doesn’t make it, Brook said he didn’t know.

Banton, Curran and Phil Salt, who had begun the game with his seventh golden duck in T20 internationals, must all be in the mix.

This was only the fourth T20 defeat under Brook’s captaincy in 27 completed matches, and it highlighted a potential weakness with the seam attack. Henry Crocombe would have bowled only two overs on T20 debut had Jacks not hurt his hand, while 6.5 overs between Overton and Curran cost 81 runs.

The spin of Liam Dawson and Adil Rashid, back in the white-ball side after missing the last six ODIs, looked England’s best bet, and Jacks briefly raised hopes by removing Lachlan Shaw and Joel Davies in the 17th over. But, as Brook conceded later, their own total felt at least ten runs short.

At least his own performance gave England a reason to be cheerful. Dropped on two and three during an unusually error-strewn fielding performance by the Australians, he had managed just seven off his first nine balls before he stepped on the gas.

Brook hit six of his next 16 deliveries for six, starting with three in a row off Riley Meredith, the last a majestic swat over wide long-on as he advanced at the bowler with murderous intent. After it hit a boy in the crowd, Brook handed over a pair of batting gloves by way of apology.

England’s captain needed this innings, if only to start winning round a sceptical Australian public who were yet to see the best of him. Ten previous white-ball innings in this country had produced just 92 runs, while the locals still remember his antics during last winter’s Ashes, when he kept finding ways to self-destruct.

By the time he fell to Chaudhary, his record since moving to No3 in February was a ridiculous 597 runs at 74, with a strike-rate of 203. But it wasn’t enough, and England must regroup quickly before Tuesday’s second game on the Gold Coast.

Sports.title: Inside Diego Gomez's remarkable rise to Premier League's king of the wondergoal: Plucked from a rural Paraguayan village at 13, doing Lionel Messi's running for him at Inter Miami and starring as Brighton's aggressive machine
Sports.content:
Inside Diego Gomez's remarkable rise to Premier League's king of the wondergoal: Plucked from a rural Paraguayan village at 13, doing Lionel Messi's running for him at Inter Miami and starring as Brighton's aggressive machine

Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.

Diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream. While it is a script that has been read many times before, like an old movie or a classic song, it is also one that never gets old.

In this particular iteration, it begins on the dirt tracks of Mburika Reta, which literally translates to the ‘land of donkeys’ in Paraguay’s native Guarani, before winding through the country's capital, Asuncion, and briefly stopping among the palm-lined suburbs of Miami alongside Sergio Busquets and Lionel Messi. It is now gathering pace on England’s south coast, where Brighton find themselves in the unfamiliar territory of hunting down the Premier League champions.

Gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s machine: energetic, aggressive and relentlessly forward-thinking. It is through this collective sense of selflessness that the Seagulls are second in the table, having already defeated both league leaders Arsenal and Manchester City this season. And for Hurzeler’s versatile midfielder, every performance and goal is a reminder of the moments that forged him.

‘He always told me to play forward and, when I have the ball, to have no fear,’ the 23-year-old said last year of his former team-mate Messi.

Cue a spectacular goal from the halfway line against Crystal Palace last month, the Amex crowd growing feverish as the ball sailed over Walter Benitez before crashing into the back of the net.

Diego Gomez pictured as a young teen playing for Libertad (left), is now thriving for Paraguay (right) and one of Brighton's most important players

Gomez is congratulated by Pascal Gross after scoring a brilliant goal against Brentford

Another quickly followed against Brentford last weekend, with Gomez barely bringing the ball under control before hooking it into the net from 25 yards out with his supposedly weaker left foot, leaving half of his team-mates clutching their heads in disbelief.

Inevitably Gomez’s rise has not been without its setbacks. It was his mistimed tackle on Desire Doue, stretching out a leg to topple the French winger in the penalty area, that led to the heartache of Paraguay’s World Cup elimination this summer, after Kylian Mbappe slotted home the resulting spot-kick.

Yet rather than be defined by this mistake, Gomez returned home to a hero’s welcome, mobbed by locals as he was paraded through the streets of the usually sleepy San Juan Bautista in an open-top car.

‘He has the right attitude towards football,’ Hurzeler said shortly after his arrival. ‘He loves to play. You can feel his passion in every talk with him.’

Across his 10 appearances this season, Gomez has won 66 duels, more than any Brighton player. His 35 aerial duels won, second behind only Croatian centre back Luka Vuskovic, point to his impressive spring, and he has won 10 tackles, again more than any other Brighton player.

At the other end of the pitch, meanwhile, he has taken the most touches in the opposition box and has scored two goals and recorded two assists this season.

While Gomez’s physique gives the impression of a battering ram, he is surprisingly speedy, recording Brighton’s fastest top speed of the season against Chelsea at 21.01mph.

But who is this kid who was plucked out of nowhere? Who, at the age of 13, moved four hours away from his rural village to the capital to play football, navigating the bus networks as a child to get to training at FC Libertad before a move to join David Beckham’s glitzy side arrived seven years later?

Gomez, seen with his partner Geraldine Villagra, has taken an unusual route to the top

In this case, it was Inter Miami who did the plucking, with Gomez identified by Brighton’s scouting network while he was playing in the MLS in 2024. Gomez formally joined the club as a 21-year-old in a deal worth £11million in January 2025, having agreed the move six months earlier.

Former Brighton centre back Gordon Greer is now the club’s pathway development manager and spoke regularly to Gomez during this time, travelling to Florida to see him during the latter stages of the MLS season. It’s fair to say he liked what he found.

‘We knew that he would do well because of his application,’ Greer says. ‘He was just a really talented, young, hungry footballer. You could see that he had raw potential, and I think Brighton do that really well. They sign players who have got room to improve.

‘The one thing about Diego that is really impressive is his attitude, his work rate. He’s a really driven character and he’s such a humble kid. You can ask Diego to do certain things and he’ll give it his all, no matter what you ask him to do, whether he’s good at it or not. As a coach, it must be amazing to have someone like that in your team.’

During his six-month wait for the move, Gomez undertook regular English lessons, tuned in to Brighton’s games on television and spoke to Hurzeler about the areas he could improve before making the switch. All of that left him with a couple of weeks’ head start, which in Premier League terms is massive.

Meanwhile, Brighton’s plethora of South American footballers at the time, most notably Julio Enciso, who played alongside him at Libertad, helped him settle quickly. So too did Gomez’s girlfriend, Geraldine Villagra, who moved to Brighton to live with him, while his family regularly visit from Paraguay.

Gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s energetic machine for the Seagulls

Spending 18 months alongside Messi, Busquets and Luis Suarez was also another important step in Gomez’s development, despite his understandable initial nerves. He forged a strong understanding with Messi on the pitch and was the engine that enabled the Argentine genius to thrive. Much like at Brighton, though, that did not stop Gomez from producing moments of magic of his own.

‘The fact that he had these superstars in the team probably helped him,’ Greer says. ‘We don’t have any superstars in our team like Messi, but everyone gives their all.

‘At Inter Miami, Messi was by far the best player, but Diego did a lot of the running for him and had a fantastic season in which he contributed a number of goals and assists. He just worked away at it. Regardless of the kind of environment you put him in, he finds a way through it.’

The audacity of Gomez’s two recent goals, the strike against Palace that inevitably won the Premier League Goal of the Month award for October and the Brentford one which is firmly in contention for November, almost contradicts that industrious nature. Has Greer been surprised by them?

‘He scored some really good goals for Inter Miami, but not as good as the ones he’s scored of late for us,’ he says. ‘He wants to achieve big things. It’s no surprise... well, it is a surprise when you see him stick one in the top corner with his left foot!’

Gomez endeared himself to many when he broke down during a pre-World Cup press conference while speaking about the privilege of representing his country, and he remains deeply aware of where he has come from.

Earlier this year, Brighton chose to extend their UNICEF partnership to Paraguay, with Gomez becoming an ambassador for a programme that aims to develop young people's skills and confidence through sport and will reach thousands of children across the nation, a role he regards as a great honour.

After Paraguay’s elimination from the World Cup, Gomez attended one of the events in Asuncion, where he first plied his trade and where UNICEF will soon roll out the programme.

‘During his personal time, after coming back from the World Cup, he could have done lots of other things and chose instead to do that,’ Anna Easthope, Brighton’s head of marketing, adds. ‘He realises the impact of meeting kids, giving them inspiration and letting them know that sport is for everyone.’

If a hero’s welcome followed World Cup elimination, imagine the reception a Premier League title would bring to Misiones.

Sports.title: Harry Kane's injury blow: Ballon d'Or winner sends upbeat message from hospital amid England concerns captain will be out for MONTHS after tearing ligaments
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich fear Harry Kane will be ruled out for months after suffering an ankle injury in their Bundesliga draw against Cologne - with the striker revealing he will only return for 'the business end of the season'.

Kane was forced off just 20 minutes into the match at the Allianz Arena following a challenge from Joel Schmied.

The defender had won the ball but caught Kane with his follow through on his ankle.

Kane had initially tried to play on after treatment, before eventually needing to be replaced.

The Ballon d'Or winner was upbeat on Saturday morning however, sharing a message with his fans that stressed his readiness to come back better than ever.

'The highs and lows of life!' Kane captioned a picture of himself wearing a protective boot. 'Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going in 2027.

Harry Kane was forced off during Bayern Munich's draw against Cologne on Friday night

Bayern confirmed the England captain is set to be out for months following the injury

But despite his injury, Kane was upbeat as he spoke to fans for the first time on Saturday (Source: Harry Kane/X)

'I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!

'"Tough times don't last, tough people do" - my guy (Julian Edelman) told me this one!' Kane added, quoting the NFL icon.

'Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut (red heart emoji, strong arm emoji).'

Speaking post-match, Bayern sporting director Max Eberl revealed that Kane has suffered ligament damage.

A Bayern club statement confirmed the blow, reading: 'Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against 1. FC Köln on Friday evening.

'This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department.

'The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months. Get well soon Harry.'

Kane's absence will be a major blow for Bayern, with the Ballon d'Or winner having scored ten goals in 16 matches so far this season.

Bayern, who are already without Luis Diaz, Saibari and Serge Gnabry, also saw Michael Olise come off at half-time.

The German giants later confirmed Olise had suffered a 'contusion of the forefoot', with the Frenchman set to undergo treatment in the coming days.

It remains to be seen whether Kane - who became England's most-capped player last week when making his 126th appearance in the 2-1 win over Croatia - is at risk of missing the Nations League quarter-final against Norway in March.

Vincent Kompany, who was back in the dugout for the first time since his collapse last month, admitted other players will have to step up for Bayern in the absence of star names such as Kane.

'These are world-class players, you can't replace them, but we have the mentality and we have to bring that now,' Kompany said, as per Bild.

'We need incredible performances from players who may not yet be used to this pressure at FC Bayern.

Bayern were held to a 1-1 draw by Cologne on Vincent Kompany's return to the touchline

'We will all try together to make this situation a positive one for ourselves. FC Bayern does this time and time again, and that's what we want to do now too.'

Bayern were ultimately held to a 1-1 draw by Cologne, with Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore giving the visitors a shock first half lead at the Allianz Arena.

Nathaniel Brown drew Bayern level before half-time, but the hosts were unable to find a winner on Kompany's return.

The draw gives Borussia Dortmund the chance to move to the top of the Bundesliga table on Saturday.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta clamps down on Arsenal stars' use of Fantasy Premier League after Christos Tzolis 'leaked' team news in his side 'Tzatziki FC' before Gunners beat Liverpool
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta clamps down on Arsenal stars' use of Fantasy Premier League after Christos Tzolis 'leaked' team news in his side 'Tzatziki FC' before Gunners beat Liverpool

Mikel Arteta has clamped down on Arsenal stars' Fantasy Premier League (FPL) exploits after 'Tzatziki FC', Christos Tzolis' team, 'leaked' team news.

The Arsenal manager admitted he has 'taken measures' to ensure opponents are not given an advantage by his players' selections on the popular game.

Tzolis picked himself as captain of his FPL side prior to the Gunners' 1-0 victory over Liverpool, a clear indication that he would start after recently coming back from injury.

Arteta then caught wind of the situation and Tzolis removed all Arsenal players from his fantasy team for their next game against Hull.

X account FPL Focal identified 'Tzatziki FC' as the Greek winger's team and screenshots of his teams from both game weeks showed how his picks changed.

On Friday, speaking about this issue, Arteta said: 'With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well. Constantly they are asking me about line-ups as well, because they want to know.

Christos Tzolis picked himself in Fantasy Premier League before starting the Liverpool game

Tzolis' team, seen here before the Liverpool clash, is called 'Tzatziki FC' and was identified as his side by X account FPL Focal

'It’s a topic, you know. These are the kind of things that are happening in our society right now and it’s something new.

'We haven’t dealt with it [before] and we need to put new things in place. Obviously confidentiality is something critical because it’s about trust and about what you are trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret. We’ll take measures to make sure it doesn’t happen.'

Arteta then confirmed that those measures had already been taken.

Tzolis is a known obsessive of the game, which puts him among 13 million other players who participate every year.

He even quipped after providing an assist against Coventry earlier in the season: 'I will take the three points', referring to the FPL score for doing so.

Chelsea had a similar issue this season, with their players indicating that Joao Pedro was out injured, removing the Brazilian from their FPL teams before his absence was confirmed by the club.

Teams are taking the matter seriously and are keen to ensure any possible advantage their opponents might have regarding team news is nipped in the bud.

Five years ago, Aston Villa stopped their players from participating in FPL after a number of them took Jack Grealish out of their line-ups, notifying eagle-eyed competitors that he was injured.

Mikel Arteta has cracked down on FPL use and 'taken measures' to ensure there are no leaks

The potential impact of players joining the global GTA 6 mania is another concern for Arteta, with a number of top-flight players already sharing how gripped they will be by the new game.

Bryan Mbeumo posted the loading screen at midnight on Thursday, indicating that he was having a late-night gaming session just days before the Liverpool clash, while Alexander Isak has said he will be hunkering down to play the game.

Declan Rice has previously spoken about how he often games into the early hours after matches when adrenaline is still coursing through him.

And his manager noted: 'We’ll try to find out how much exposure we have to these kinds of games and make sure it’s the right one to be able to perform and focus on what we have to do.'

Sports.title: Pat Cummins to REMAIN captain despite Sandpapergate claims after Cricket Australia's unanimous vote of confidence - as board seeks to draw a line under re-emerged scandal
Sports.content:
Australian cricket is closing ranks on the sandpaper affair, with the board expressing their ‘unanimous support’ for Pat Cummins’s captaincy, and former coach Darren Lehmann insisting: ‘I didn’t know sandpaper was being used.’

It had been obvious all week that Cricket Australia had no appetite the relitigate the events of their team’s Test series in South Africa eight years ago, but on Saturday they formally gave Cummins the green light.

CA chair David Boon said the board had learned from the events of 2018, and were ‘proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered’.

That followed Wednesday’s announcement by Boon and chief executive Todd Greenberg of an ‘independent forum’ to allow the players a ‘safe space’ to discuss Sandpapergate.

Boon added: ‘We unequivocally reject any implication that Pat’s integrity has been compromised.’

Usman Khawaja’s recently published autobiography set the ball rolling by claiming that the whole team knew about the plot to rub sandpaper on the ball at Port Elizabeth and Cape Town. His claims were subsequently backed up by Chadd Sayers, 12th man during the two Tests, and – explosively – by Cameron Bancroft, who carried out the plan.

Australian Test captain Pat Cummins will remain skipper of the team after a 'unanimous' vote of support from the Cricket Australia board

It followed almost a fortnight of speculation about the Sandpapergate scandal after retired batter Usman Khawaja claimed in a newly released autobiography that the entire Australian team knew about the planfor ball tampering in South Africa in 2018

Cummins said the backing, expressed during a meeting with Cricket Australia chair David Boon (right) and chief executive Todd Greenberg (left) on Friday, 'meant a lot'

But Cummins met Boon and Greenberg in Sydney on Friday, before the board issued a statement expressing its ‘unanimous support for Pat Cummins as captain given ongoing speculation about his position’.

A relieved-sounding Cummins admitted: ‘It meant a lot to speak with David and Todd on Friday. Being Australian captain carries with it an awesome responsibility. I have and never will take that lightly.

‘David and Todd have a very tough job navigating cricket through all of this and I commend them for reaching out to me and to many of the players and staff from 2018.

‘I support the forum 100 per cent. I will be there. All of the players and staff I have spoken with are very keen to go and to have their say. There will be a lot of difficult conversations but that is what’s needed.

‘Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth will be my focus and priority.’

That first Test against New Zealand starts on December 9. And despite CA’s latest show of support for their captain, there will be no avoiding more awkward questions when Cummins addresses the media the day before the game.

Lehmann, meanwhile, said in a 25-minute radio interview before the first T20 between Australia and England in Melbourne that ‘my version stays the same: I didn’t know sandpaper was being used’.

He added: ‘I was coach at the time, I’ve got to take that responsibility. It was the best job in the world. I’m sorry for what happened. It’s my fault it went too far.

‘I can’t remember David Warner raising the possibility of using sandpaper. There are a whole load of conversations that go on – some that you’re privy to, some that you’re not.’

Pictured, Khawaja and Cummins during day five of the Third Test match in the series between Australia and India at Melbourne Cricket Ground in 2018

Cummins said on Saturday that he would be in attendance of the CA's forum, which has been set up to allow players and staff to share their experiences

During his excoriating 4,500-word tell-all for the West Australian, Bancroft claimed that Lehmann shouted into his walkie-talkie to substitute Peter Handscomb to ‘get the f****** sandpaper off Bangers now’ after the giant screens at Cape Town revealed his skulduggery.

But Lehmann said: ‘That was all after the fact. It was already played out on TV. So that’s Cameron’s take on it. Again, I’m not going to talk about Cameron. My view is different.’

He continued: ‘I went to a really dark place. I think people say, “Well, you probably should.” But I went to as dark a place as you can think about, and it took me probably three or four years to actually get back to some sort of normality, and to the stage where we are now.

‘I’m not going back to that dark place, mate. I’m trying to move forward. I’m not going back. There’s things I remember, not remember. It’s eight and a half years ago. It’s a traumatic time. None more so for my family, and without the support of family and friends back then, I don’t know where I’d be.’

Both Khawaja and Warner have been ‘rested’ from their punditry duties by Fox Sports, in a bid to prevent them being a distraction.

‘We think it is increasingly difficult to focus on the game while the situation continues to unfold and think it is unfair on both commentators to put them in that position,’ said Fox Sports managing director Steve Crawley.

Earlier on Saturday, fellow cricketer Josh Hazlewood had spoken out in defence of Cummins amid suggestions his captaincy might not survive the Sandpapergate saga.

The 35-year-old warned Code Sports that removing Cummins would divide the squad and described how there had been a 'bit of a pile on the last few days from different people'.

Looking ahead to Australia's first Test against New Zealand, he suggested that if the team turned up Cummins wasn't the captain, then there could be fractures, saying: 'Honestly, I don't know how that would go.'

On Friday, former Australian fast bowler Mitchell Johnson suggested Cummins's 'personal brand' and role as captain may not survive the scrutiny he has faced.

'I believe Bancroft's account. It comes across as real and I could feel the words as he was saying them,' he wrote in the West Australian.

'The pressure on Cummins is now immense. I think he will still try to stand by what he has said. But I think the public pressure for Cummins to stand down as Test captain now will be too much.

'I just can't see how his captaincy and personal brand survives this.'

Cummins has repeatedly denied having prior knowledge of the plan to alter the condition of the ball during the 2018 Cape Town Test.

When he fronted the media on November 13, he also directly challenged Khawaja's claim that the team knew.

'When he says "We all knew", if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out in the field, he's 100 per cent wrong,' Cummins said.

Cummins, Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon had previously addressed what they knew during the Cape Town Test in a joint statement issued on May 18, 2021.

The four said they 'did not know a foreign substance was taken onto the field to alter the condition of the ball' until they saw the images on the big screen at Newlands.

Sports.title: RIATH AL-SAMARRAI: The grubby antics of JJ Gabriel's entourage threaten to derail his career before it's begun. Man United insiders tell a revealing story about his acrimonious exit
Sports.content:
RIATH AL-SAMARRAI: The grubby antics of JJ Gabriel's entourage threaten to derail his career before it's begun. Man United insiders tell a revealing story about his acrimonious exit

Riath Al-Samarrai Chief Sports Feature Writer

We should start with the video. It’s something to behold. Opening with a scene that depicts a young footballer being ushered through a crowd of faux reporters, there is a promise within the first five seconds of ‘epic news’ and ‘a rare discovery’.

It’s a little on-the-nose, but the messaging will only escalate. Soon we find ourselves staring at what appears to be a Ballon d’Or replica, before the director cuts to a moody shot of the footballer from behind as he stares at a wall of photographs.

Those images are showing a few of the staging posts in his brief career to date – signing for Manchester United aged 10, posing with a ball and, then, one of him preparing to come on as a substitute. A pair of Nike boots find their way in.

Finally, the lad shows himself and delivers a single line to camera: ‘I am epic.’

This came out at the start of the week. Our epic footballer? That would be JJ Gabriel, aged 16 years and one month, still in braces, and potentially the best you’ve not yet seen.

As you have likely heard, he really is that good. And as you will also know, the mechanisms of his exit from United ahead of an imminent deal with Real Madrid have been ugly.

JJ Gabriel, aged 16 years and one month, still in braces, and potentially the best footballer you’ve not yet seen

The video Gabriel released this week announcing his exit from Manchester United includes signing for the club at the age of 10 alongside Cristiano Ronaldo Jr (Source: Instagram/Jjnr10)

Finally, the lad shows himself and delivers a single line to camera: ‘I am epic’ (Source: Instagram/Jjnr10)

But let’s momentarily keep to that bizarre video, which has been watched almost two million times on Gabriel’s Instagram page, and from there we can raise the question of whoever thought it was a good idea.

This is where we should introduce Ali Barat, the owner of Epic Sports. He’s a big fish in the world of football agencies and the 31-second clip was advertising their latest coup: Gabriel had joined his group, which is timely because a move to Real is imminent and that will follow other big deals brokered by Barat.

They include Moises Caicedo to Chelsea for £115million, Noni Madueke to Arsenal for £52m and Dean Huijsen to Bournemouth for £12.6m, then on to Real Madrid for £50m more. He’s a significant figure with a changeable definition of what it means to be understated. Here’s an example from his company’s website: ‘While some agents seek the spotlight, Ali Barat is quietly reshaping the transfer market.’

Amusingly, it then goes on to describe Barat as a ‘super-agent’ twice in the same paragraph while declaring he is ‘not just closing deals, he is building careers, guiding legacies, and setting the standard for a new era of football representation’.

The ‘quiet’ part was possibly lost along the way. But ‘legacy’ is the word among that salad most worthy of fixation, because Gabriel has been steered to a series of pivotal decisions at an incredibly young age.

He is yet to play a single minute of competitive senior football but he is clear on what he wishes to become. Earlier this month, his handlers felt it prudent to place him in an interview with the Madrid-based newspaper Marca and Gabriel said: ‘My dream is to win a Ballon d'Or.’

Fair enough. He’s a teenager aiming high. Is it wise to say so? Maybe not, but he’s 16. Barat, the super-agent, has no such excuse. He’s 30 years older than his client and saw no harm in a video that invoked the Ballon d’Or to peddle an academy kid.

There’s less ambiguity in the wisdom of what Barat has done there. It reeks. It carries the stench of an agent who evidently doesn’t mind so much if the labels attached to Gabriel today stick for the remainder of his career.

Earlier this month, his handlers felt it prudent to place him in an interview with the Madrid-based newspaper Marca and Gabriel said: ‘My dream is to win a Ballon d'Or’

Gabriel's representative Ali Barat, who is 30 years older than his client and saw no harm in a video that invoked the Ballon d’Or to peddle an academy kid

I can remember when Mauricio Pochettino once made the blunder of placing Marcus Edwards, a Tottenham wonderkid, into the same sentence as Lionel Messi. His point was that he had some similar movement patterns, but the fact the lad was named mini-Messi in training didn’t help – it was a tag that endured.

Thankfully, Edwards has carved out a respectable career at Burnley via Sporting in Portugal, but Pochettino regretted the words as soon as they left his mouth.

That’s different to designing and releasing a video, of course. That’s different to a process involving some level of sign-off. That’s different to the grubby act of hyping a very young guy to a standard reached by only five Englishmen in history.

A question at this stage: where was Gabriel’s family when this was being decided? That’s somewhat loaded because there is chatter about how much of the United separation has been driven by Gabriel’s father, Joe O'Cearuill, formerly a professional himself for Brighton, Barnet and the Republic of Ireland.

I’d add that many of those noises have originated from within Carrington. It might simply be the bitter discourse of the jilted. But a recurring sentiment among some United staffers is that the father became difficult during the breakdown in relations.

These are lines we have heard before in football. But for once, United do not appear to have done much wrong. There was genuine care for the player. And if there is one thing they can guarantee, it is that young talents get a good chance, though evidently not enough to please Gabriel’s camp.

A demand for minutes against Azerbaijani side Sabah in the Champions League was a bad look; similar might be said with less force around reports that he changed his name from Joseph Junior Andreou O'Cearuill for commercial reasons, feeding one of those blurry conversations about where the athlete ends and the product begins.

Gabriel’s early days with Epic and Barat and his content wing do not serve much encouragement on that front.

Gabriel's father Joe O'Cearuill was briefly in Arsenal's reserves before going on to play for Brighton, Barnet and the Republic of Ireland

United do not appear to have done much wrong. There was genuine care for the player. And if there is one thing they can guarantee, it is that young talents get a good chance

It is worth stating that the teenager at the heart of it all is not considered to be a bad sort. Far from it.

None of his ascent was accompanied by the worrying noises that followed another prodigy in Ravel Morrison – once described by Sir Alex Ferguson as having 'as much natural talent as any youngster we ever signed', but who made all of three League Cup appearances for United before a journeyman career through the Championship, Italy, Mexico, Sweden, the Netherlands, the US and the UAE.

One source has suggested Gabriel even cried when he said his goodbyes back in September.

It might be over-reaching to claim he has left the club against his own better judgment, but there is no doubt he has gambled hugely on Real Madrid.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is pretty handy and has found it tough there; Martin Odegaard is a far closer parallel to Gabriel having moved to Madrid aged 15, and he played 11 games in three seasons.

If the pathway was blocked at United, then what is it at a club who employ Vinicius Junior, Rodrygo, Yan Diomande, Arda Guler, Endrick, Brahim Diaz, Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe in Gabriel's positions?

A new language and surroundings are large hurdles for a young player, especially one whose ambitions are so public and grand. It won’t be a quiet arrival by any definition, even those found in the quirky dictionary of Ali Barat, and the pressure will be significant.

Hopefully such factors don’t impact upon an exciting trajectory. That would be an epic shame.

If United's pathway was blocked, then what is it at a club with (L-R) Vinicius Junior, Jude Bellingham, Rodrygo, Kylian Mbappe and plenty more in Gabriel's positions?

A new language and surroundings are large hurdles for a young player, and hopefully such factors don’t impact upon an exciting trajectory. That would be an epic shame

Welsh Rugby Union's 20,000 reasons to be ashamed

Among the joys of this job is being present at rare moments of sporting greatness. The Welsh win over the All Blacks last weekend was one such occasion and, for me, it was compounded by a subsequent email from a lovely chap named John Evans, aged 87 and from Tredegar in Blaenau Gwent.

John had watched the game on television, but was part of what must be a dwindling group who could say they were there the last time Wales had beaten New Zealand, at the Arms Park in 1953.

After detailing how he, ‘a small-bottomed outside-half’, had left himself with no view of the pitch at the back of the stand, John went on to recall that the crowd around him and a friend ‘decided to pass us over everyone’s head back down to the front’. He landed just in time to see Ken Jones score the winning try. His excitement in sharing a memory from 73 years ago was spelled out in block capitals.

One of the consequences of the ongoing shambles at the Welsh Rugby Union is that there were 20,000 empty seats at the Principality Stadium last weekend, mainly due to a combination of apathy and protest. Accordingly, there will be 20,000 fewer people with a great story to tell decades from now. While the WRU ponder their next blunders, they might wish to consider some of the above.

Sports.title: Ismaila Sarr opens up on failed Liverpool transfer and reveals fresh talks
Sports.content:
Ismaila Sarr opens up on failed Liverpool transfer and reveals fresh talks

Liverpool saw a £50million bid for Ismaila Sarr rejected by Crystal Palace in the summer transfer window before the Reds eventually moved on to their top target, Bradley Barcola

View 2 Images Crystal Palace want to give Ismaila Sarr a new contract (Image: Ahmad Mora/Getty Images)

Ismaila Sarr has confirmed that he's in talks over a new contract with Crystal Palace after putting Liverpool's interest 'behind him'. Sarr, 28, was keen on a move to Anfield before Palace turned down Liverpool's £50million bid.

‌



‌



The Reds were looking for alternatives to Bradley Barcola before ultimately coughing up Paris Saint-Germain's £123m asking price. Despite the disappointment, the Senegal international maintains that he's happy at Palace and is open to extending his stay.

‌



Sarr told BBC Sport: "Liverpool is one of the biggest clubs in world football and, when a club like that shows an interest in you, of course it's something you take seriously.

‌



"I don't think any player would be indifferent to that kind of opportunity. It was an interesting possibility, and naturally, I considered what it could mean for my career.

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"Today, that chapter is behind me. I've always believed that you can't move forward if you're constantly looking in the rear-view mirror.

"I'm a Crystal Palace player, I'm proud of what we've achieved together, and my focus is on getting back on the pitch and helping the team."

‌



On his future at Selhurst Park, the ex-Watford star added: "Yes, there have been discussions with the club. For now, I prefer to let those conversations happen privately and concentrate on football."

Sarr will have a new manager when he returns from a groin injury, as Thomas Frank has replaced Pierre Sage. Frank's reign begins away to Coventry on Saturday, and Sarr is confident that the former Brentford and Tottenham boss can change Palace's fortunes.

‌



Should Liverpool go back in for Ismaila Sarr? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Ismaila Sarr is willing to commit his future to Crystal Palace (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

‌



"Of course, it's a difficult moment for everyone at the club," the winger acknowledged. "After everything we achieved last season, nobody expected us to be in this position.

"But I know the quality of this squad. We have very good players, a strong group and the ability to turn things around. The arrival of Thomas Frank is an opportunity for a fresh start, new energy and a different approach.

Article continues below

"We all have to take responsibility, work together and fight for every point. I'm confident we can overcome this difficult period and achieve our objectives this season."

Sports.title: Goalkeeper involved in tragic death of Jesus De Miguel makes emotional return to his club
Sports.content:
Goalkeeper involved in tragic death of Jesus De Miguel makes emotional return to his club

Jesus Owono has made his first public appearance since the tragic collision that claimed the life of CD Tenerife striker Jesus De Miguel

View 3 Images Jesus Owono made a public appearance on Friday as he watched this side from the stands (Image: Movistar Plus)

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who was involved in the collision that resulted in CD Tenerife striker Jesus De Miguel's death, has made his first public appearance since the incident. Owono was in the stands as his team faced CD Leganes on Friday.

‌



‌



Tragedy struck on November 2, when Owono and De Miguel competed for a bouncing ball in second-half stoppage time during a LaLiga Hypermotion clash. The goalkeeper attempted an aerial clearance as he sprinted out of his area, but ended up colliding with De Miguel's chest.

‌



De Miguel, 30, collapsed and suffered cardiac arrest on the pitch. He was treated at the scene and taken to University Hospital of Nuestra Senora de Candelaria by ambulance, but passed away the following morning from "accidental chest trauma." Owono was sent off for the challenge; the game was abandoned at 2-2, and the goalkeeper was later handed a 12-match ban and financial fines.

‌



FC Andorra played their first home match since the tragedy on Friday and a minute's silence was held pre-game. Players placed a bouquet in the centre circle whilst wearing De Miguel's No. 9 shirt, and play was stopped in the ninth minute for a minute of applause. Owono, who had not been seen publicly since the collision, watched on.

Because of his ban, which was issued by the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) Competition Committee on November 13, Owono could not play for FC Andorra. This 12-game sanction is the maximum penalty permitted under Article 102 of the RFEF disciplinary code for violent conduct or excessive force resulting in serious injury.

View 3 Images Owono was in attendance for FC Andorra vs CD Leganes and appeared to say a prayer pre-match (Image: Movistar Plus)

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Still, Owono attended the match at the Nou Estadi a Encamp as an onlooker. The 25-year-old appeared emotional during the period of silence, and it seemed as though he said a prayer when the referee blew his whistle. The game ended in a 3-1 defeat for FC Andorra.

‌



Owono has reportedly been stricken by grief since the ordeal and may never play football again. Ana Maye, a close friend of Owono and a general coordinator of the Equatorial Guinea men's national team, told Mundo Deportivo: "No matter how much we tell him, he's deeply saddened.

"He's very affected, especially for Jesus De Miguel's one-and-a-half-year-old child and for his widow. He doesn't know how to handle all of this."

‌



On the day after De Miguel passed away, Owono released a statement through FC Andorra: "These are the most difficult days of my life. I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to process what has happened.

View 3 Images De Miguel passed away on November 3 (Image: Getty)

‌



"I feel enormous pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many questions to address.

"I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus."

Article continues below

Spain's National Police opened a routine judicial inquiry into potential involuntary manslaughter following the incident. This is a standard mandatory step under Spanish law following any non-natural death.

FC Andorra officials have confirmed that Owono is receiving psychological support and faces no pressure to return even after he has served his ban. He missed Equatorial Guinea's AFCON qualifiers against Zimbabwe this month.

Sports.title: NFL legend Tom Brady in talks to buy Chelsea stake after Birmingham City exit
Sports.content:
NFL legend Tom Brady in talks to buy Chelsea stake after Birmingham City exit

Tom Brady recently left the ownership group in charge of Birmingham City and has already moved his focus to another English club, holding talks to become a minority stakeholder in Chelsea

View 2 Images Tom Brady wants to continue his football journey (Image: Michael Owens/Getty Images)

Tom Brady is set to buy a stake in Premier League club Chelsea less than a month after leaving Birmingham City. The NFL legend has been in talks to join the Clearlake Capital vehicle that controls Chelsea, where he'd serve as an adviser but have no voting rights at the club.

‌



‌



Brady, 49, sold his minority share in Birmingham earlier this month, and it's understood that he made the decision in order to pave the way for an investment at Stamford Bridge. The seven-time Super Bowl winner has a good relationship with Clearlake co-founder Behdad Eghbali.

‌



Clearlake now owns 86.5 per cent of Chelsea after Todd Boehly and Mark Walter sold their shares in September. Brady was previously a guest of Chelsea when they won the 2025 Club World Cup final, celebrating with their players after the Blues beat Paris Saint-Germain 3-0 in New Jersey.

‌



Brady made his first foray into English football in August 2023, becoming part of Birmingham's ownership group. The ex-quarterback was appointed chair of the club's advisory board and was the subject of an Amazon Prime documentary, Built in Birmingham: Brady & The Blues.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



One moment saw Brady make headlines, as he questioned then-manager Wayne Rooney's work ethic. "I'm a little worried about our head coach's work ethic," he admitted. "I mean, I don't know, I don't have great instincts on that."

Appearing on the Stick to Football podcast, brought to you by Sky Bet, in June, Brady said of his time at Birmingham: "I love it. I love the competition we had.

‌



"Our first season was terrible - we had four different manager changes. We hired a good manager in our second year, Chris Davis. We had an awesome season, then the championship is tough, and we got to the championship this year.

Where will Chelsea finish this season? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Tom Brady was a guest of Chelsea at the 2025 Club World Cup final (Image: Stephen Nadler/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

"A lot of change in personnel, the quality of the player has been better, we just could never quite get on a run with the right momentum. This championship is tough. It's really tough."

‌



Birmingham announced that Brady was leaving last Monday, saying: "Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the Club over the last three years.

"It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom's experience and passion associated with the Club, and the Club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community."

Sports.title: 12 players could be missing from Liverpool vs Man Utd in Mauricio Pochettino's first game
Sports.content:
12 players could be missing from Liverpool vs Man Utd in Mauricio Pochettino's first game

Mauricio Pochettino faces injury concerns ahead of his first game as Manchester United boss against Liverpool, with Andoni Iraola also providing updates

View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of his first Manchester United match against Liverpool (Image: MUTV)

Mauricio Pochettino faces several injury headaches ahead of his first match as Manchester United manager. The Argentine confronts one of the most challenging possible debuts on Sunday against Liverpool, who will also be without at least three players.

‌



‌



Whilst United's rivals haven't exactly set the world alight so far this campaign, they have made steady strides under Andoni Iraola and occupy fourth spot in the Premier League table - though they sit nine points adrift of pacesetters Arsenal.

‌



No one needs reminding of the situation Pochettino has walked into and his new side could be rooted to the bottom of the table by kick-off if Sunderland and Crystal Palace claim victories in their fixtures. United entered the international break with numerous injury concerns and the picture remains mixed as they gear up to resume action.

‌



With the trip to Anfield on the horizon, Mirror Football takes a look at all the players who could miss Sunday's game, both for United and their bitter rivals.

Mauricio Pochettino confirms Bruno Fernandes decision after private talks with Man Utd captain READ MORE :

Man Utd chief sends JJ Gabriel clear message after departure triggers potential legal action READ MORE :

Manchester United

Harry Maguire has been nursing a back problem that saw him withdrawn against Aston Villa, whilst Patrick Dorgu wasn't considered fit enough for international duty with Denmark, though both have participated in training this week.

View 3 Images Dorgu is a doubt (Image: Getty)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

However, Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford have stayed on the treatment table and appear doubtful. Among the longer-term casualties, Carlos Baleba remains some distance from a comeback with his hamstring complaint, whilst fellow midfielder Manuel Ugarte is likely to miss the remainder of the season with the injury he sustained at the World Cup.

‌



In attack, Benjamin Sesko continues to be unavailable with his shin problem and isn't anticipated to return until early in the New Year. Reserve goalkeeper Karl Darlow is also sidelined.

Pochettino told MUTV: "There are some injured players and another player that we need to assess. Tomorrow [Saturday], we will have a better idea of the squad that will be available to travel to Liverpool."

‌



Players who could/will miss the match: Maguire, Dorgu, Shaw, Rashford, Baleba, Ugarte, Sesko, Darlow

Liverpool

Liverpool have received a welcome boost with the news that Virgil van Dijk and Jeremie Frimpong are likely to be fit, whilst Ryan Gravenberch remains a doubt. Iraola said: "I think, if everything goes to plan, they should all be available for the game.

‌



View 3 Images Van Dijk is fit to play (Image: Getty)

"[With] Ryan Gravenberch, it's a matter of pain. He's managing the situation a little bit, but he has been training with us the last two days, so I hope he is available.

‌



"Jeremie is recovering. The international break sometimes helps with these things. We have introduced him with the rest of the group and he also should be available. And Virgil also is fine to go."

Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni remain on the treatment table, though both have returned to training. Striker Hugo Ekitike has yet to resume training following the Achilles injury he sustained in April.

Article continues below

Players who could/will miss the match: Gravenberch, Bradley, Leoni, Ekitike.

Sports.title: Harry Kane out for MONTHS as Bayern Munich confirm England captain's major injury blow
Sports.content:
Harry Kane out for MONTHS as Bayern Munich confirm England captain's major injury blow

Harry Kane had to be substituted in the 20th minute of Bayern Munich's 1-1 draw with Koln on Friday night and tests have confirmed that the 33-year-old has suffered a serious ankle injury

View 2 Images Harry Kane will be sidelined until 2027 (Image: Getty)

Bayern Munich have confirmed that Harry Kane will be ruled out for a 'few months' after the England captain tore his ankle ligaments. Kane, 33, was forced off after just 20 minutes as Bayern drew 1-1 at home to Koln in the Bundesliga on Friday.

‌



‌



The striker had his ankle caught by Koln defender Joel Schmied, who won the ball before making contact. Kane winced in pain as he received treatment but managed to walk off the pitch before being replaced by Tom Bischof.

‌



After Bayern's medical staff assessed Kane's injury, however, it was found that he'd torn his syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle. A statement released after full-time confirmed that he'll be out of action until the new year.

‌



Bayern posted on social media: "Harry Kane sustained a syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle during this evening's home match against 1. FC Köln. This was confirmed by an examination carried out by FC Bayern’s medical department. The 33 year-old will be sidelined for the next few months. Get well soon, Harry!"

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Reports from Germany suggest that the exact timeframe for Kane's recovery will be three months. That would see him return in time for England's Nations League quarter-final fixtures against Norway on March 27 and March 30.

Unfortunately for Bayern, a full three months on the sidelines would see the Ballon d'Or winner miss a total of 16 games - 18 if Vincent Kompany's side reach the DFB Pokal quarter-finals. That period includes Bayern's game away to Manchester United in the Champions League on January 20.

‌



The German giants also lost Michael Olise to injury at half-time on Friday but say that it's only a bruise, meaning that the French winger could be back for Wednesday's journey to Lille. Bayern had to come from 1-0 down against Koln after Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore scored his first goal for the club in the 12th minute.

Is Harry Kane the best striker in the world? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Harry Kane suffered the injury after a tackle by Joel Schmied (Image: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images)

Kane's replacement, Bischof, set up with the equaliser, which was scored by summer signing Nathaniel Brown. But Bayern couldn't find a winner, as Koln earned a valuable point in Munich to pull further away from the relegation zone.

Article continues below

"I think we didn't get off to a bad start, we were really in the game and had some pace," Kompany said post-match. "But then Harry Kane and Michael Olise suffered injuried of course. However, no excuses."

Sports.title: Meg Jones makes demand to Red Roses team-mates after losing 41-match unbeaten record
Sports.content:
Meg Jones makes demand to Red Roses team-mates after losing 41-match unbeaten record

The Red Roses were 41 matches unbeaten until they were beaten by Canada last month.

View 2 Images Megan Jones of England breaks a tackle against Canada (Image: 2026 Tim Austen)

Red Roses captain Meg Jones wants the world champions to become ‘unpredictable’ after losing their unbeatable status – calling their battles against World Cup final opponents Canada exactly what they want.

‌



Jones’ side saw their 41-match unbeaten streak ended by consecutive defeats to the Canadians in the WXV Global Series across the Atlantic.

One year after the 2025 Rugby World Cup final at Allianz Stadium, when England were crowned champions against the North American side in front of a world record crowd, the rivalry has levelled up the standard of the international game.

The Commonwealth Games bronze medallist and PWR finalist this summer with Trailfinders Women is embracing the challenge and wants to play in more matches like their Canadian showdowns.

View 2 Images Meg Jones during the Nations Championship 2026 match between England and Japan at Allianz Stadium on November 14, 2026 in London, England. (Image: Peter Nicholls)

“To have Test matches like we had against Canada is exactly what we want: competitive, the unions developing their game just as much as we are, putting the time and effort in, and wanting to see a genuine development of the game,” Jones said.

“We want competitive rugby, and we want it to be a good product for people to come and watch. We just want to keep the game growing.

“I just want to see us become unpredictable, to show our characters that we have. We are some amazing rugby players and their skill set is phenomenal.

“I'd love to keep showing a product of rugby where we don't differentiate between men and women. It's just a good game of rugby.

“[Growing the game] is our main legacy as a group of individuals. You want to see the game grow, you don't want it just to stay where it is. You want it to evolve.

“You also want to see the product, which is an entertainment product at the end of the day, develop.”

The Women’s Rugby World Cup winner was speaking at Allianz Stadium, where there was a giant Allianz Kick Start T1 Rugby Zone as part of a rugby programme run by Allianz UK and England Rugby.

Allianz Kick Start is a six week programme designed to introduce children to T1 Rugby, an exciting, inclusive and non-contact version of the game. Through fun activities, enjoying learning resources and practical sessions, children discover the fundamentals of the sport while developing life skills including teamwork, respect, communication and confidence.

Joined by Saracens and England legend Owen Farrell, she watched as children got active as part of the programme which Allianz have launched to support over 5,000 primary school pupils by 2028.

“The Allianz Kick Start programme in essence is to make it accessible, reduce the barriers to playing and help children learn all the basics of rugby," the centre said.

“It's a non-contact sport, T1 Rugby. Non-contact allows you to be free, have a chuck about with your friends, make friends, build teamwork, build a sense of belonging.

“I don't think I saw as many schools get involved in rugby when I was growing up. Particularly being from a state school, it's not something you see daily.

“It's special to me because I want to see the game grow, the women's game's given me so much.

“It's built my character, my sense of belonging, I've been able to work in teams my whole life, which I think is a super strength and is also giving me leadership qualities, which I think is favoured in this society.”

Allianz UK and England Rugby aim to introduce rugby to children in 5,000 schools through the Allianz Kick Start programme. Link to Allianz Kick Start Landing Page.

Sports.title: Edwin van der Sar claims he 'saw a light' before brain haemorrhage that changed his life
Sports.content:
Edwin van der Sar claims he 'saw a light' before brain haemorrhage that changed his life

Legendary Ajax and Manchester United goalkeeper Edwin van der Sar has reflected on his final memories before being rushed to intensive career with a bleed on the brain

View 2 Images Edwin van der Sar survived a health scare three years ago (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United legend Edwin van der Sar has recalled "seeing a light" as he suffered his life-changing brain haemorrhage. The Dutchman, 56, was rushed to intensive care via helicopter after falling ill on holiday in Croatia in July 2023.

‌



‌



He spent around three weeks in hospital, returning to his native Netherlands where he underwent a rehabilitation program. He's since made a full recovery, although he leads a much calmer life than before.

‌



Van der Sar credits the quick thinking of his wife, Annemarie van Kesteren, who herself suffered a brain haemorrhage 14 years prior. Recalling the ordeal to FourFourTwo, he said: "Annemarie knew what was happening.

‌



"I had this strange feeling that something wasn't right. Then before you know it, you see the light and the light hurts your eyes. I had pain in my head.

"From that point onwards, you just let yourself go, and hope the ambulance and the people around you take care of you. You have to put your faith, your life, into the hands of people who are trained for that and who specialise in it."

‌



At the time, Van der Sar had not long stepped down from his role as CEO at Ajax after seven years. He was glad of that timing, with no stress about a job he was needing to return to.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images The Manchester United legend won 26 major trophies during his career (Image: Getty Images)

Van der Sar's life now is a million miles away from the day-to-day running of a football club. He previously told Gazzetta dello Sport: "My phone was always ringing and I had to make important decisions and support the team and manager. Now I enjoy time with my family, travel, play padel and go cycling."

Article continues below

His success with Ajax brought repeated links with a return to Old Trafford, twice holding talks with his former club. But after what he's been through, there's no interest in a boardroom comeback, although he has since been back out on the pitch for charity matches such as Soccer Aid.
