The NUJ chairman in Akwa Ibom, Nsibiet John, pledged the union’s support but called for a broader approach that would address the behaviour of both men and women.

He urged the committee to extend preventive education to boys, focusing on emotional intelligence, self-control, peer pressure, drug abuse and cultism.

He also condemned relationships involving significantly older men and underage girls, insisting that cultural justifications should not excuse abuse.

Mr John said rejection by women should never be used to justify violence or sexual assault.

“Prevention is better than going after them. I don’t know how many people you are going to jail before they realise that this particular battle is not even supposed to be left for you. It is supposed to be everybody’s affair,” he said.

The 340 reported cases present a difficult question for the state: whether its existing interventions are sufficiently preventing abuse or merely responding after victims have suffered.

As the 16 Days of Activism approaches, the effectiveness of the state’s response will depend not only on public awareness campaigns but also on survivors’ access to protection, willingness to report abuse, and the consistent prosecution of alleged perpetrators.

World.title: Delta targets offsetting N6.8bn pension arrears by 2027
World.content:
The Delta State Government is targeting the clearance of outstanding N6.8 billion pension arrears by 2027, following a N10 billion intervention to improve retirees’ welfare.

The Director-General, State Bureau for Pension, Eddy Gbegbaje, disclosed this after the agency’s 2027 budget defence before the House Committee on Special Duties on Friday in Asaba.

Mr Gbegbaje said the government remained committed to regular pension payments and securing additional funds to settle outstanding liabilities.

He commended Governor Sheriff Oborevwori for his continued support to pensioners, describing the N10 billion intervention as a significant relief.

According to him, the bureau is working to clear existing pension obligations while making provisions for workers retiring into the system.

He explained that pension liabilities continued to evolve because workers retired regularly, creating fresh obligations even as the government settled existing arrears.

“Just as babies are born every day, people also retire daily. So, as you clear the outstanding liabilities, more people enter the retirement system,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The director-general expressed optimism that additional government funding would accelerate the settlement of outstanding obligations and strengthen pension administration.

“Our expectation is that more funds will be released so that we can clear the outstanding liabilities and also prepare for more retirees,” he said.

Similarly, Edafe Emakpor, chairman, House Committee on Special Duties, expressed optimism that the state would clear the outstanding N6.8 billion pension arrears by the end of 2027.

Mr Emakpor said the N10 billion intervention had reduced the pension debt to approximately N6.8 billion, adding that sustained government funding would facilitate its eventual clearance.

He said the state had also made significant progress in reducing its overall debt profile since the present administration assumed office in 2023.

According to him, the state’s debt declined from N467 billion in 2023 to about N67 billion, following repayments of approximately N400 billion.

He added that the government planned on offsetting the remaining debt of about N60 billion by the end of the first quarter of 2027.

Mr Emakpor expressed optimism that offsetting the outstanding debt would free up resources to address other financial obligations, including pension payments.

READ ALSO: Oborevwori approves special allowances for Delta health workers

“Once this is done, funds will be released. If you can afford to pay N60 billion within three months, getting the state to clear N6.8 billion is achievable,” he said.

He expressed hope that additional resources would be made available from the second quarter of 2027 to accelerate the settlement of pension arrears.

The lawmaker clarified that the reduction in the proposed 2027 budget would not affect pension payments, noting that the state’s N500 million pension subvention had remained unchanged.

He described the proposed N1.2 trillion 2027 budget as generally satisfactory, compared with N1.7 trillion in 2026.

(NAN)

World.title: 2027: NDC supporters shut down Onitsha for Obi/Kwankwaso
World.content:
Thousands of supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) shut down the commercial city of Onitsha, Anambra State, on Friday in solidarity with the Peter Obi/Rabiu Kwankwaso presidential ticket.

The crowd of supporters, who went on a road show from the First Niger Bridge down to the Holy Trinity area of Odoakpu, Onitsha, caused a traffic gridlock along major streets and link roads in the Onitsha metropolis.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Mr Obi and some party chieftains were in Onitsha for an executive meeting of the party’s campaign council.

Mr Obi, who addressed party supporters at the premises of the All Saints Anglican Cathedral, Onitsha, expressed appreciation for their massive show of love and solidarity.

He said he and Mr Kwankwaso were running for the presidency to liberate Nigeria from slavery, poverty and banditry that had plagued the nation over the years

“Kwankwaso and I have formed a formidable force that will liberate Nigeria from slavery, poverty, and the menace of banditry.

“We are ready, mark my words, anything I say here, we will do. We share a common belief that Nigeria must be free so that its citizens can, for once, enjoy the dividends of democratic government.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We are ready for the work ahead, and we equally know that with your support, and the support of all well-meaning Nigerians, we will get there,” Mr Obi said.

The NDC presidential candidate observed that Nigerians have suffered enough and implored the citizenry to make sacrifices by going to cast their votes on election day.

According to him, the quest for a new Nigeria demands all hands to be on deck in the party’s determination to sweep the polls at the 2027 general elections.

‘We’ll not allow anybody to rig this election’ – Obi

Mr Obi urged party supporters and every eligible voter in Nigeria not to be afraid of anybody, saying that the NDC was fully prepared to ensure that nobody rigged the elections.

“We want to assure you that our commitment to the task of enthroning a new Nigeria is total. We will not allow anybody to rig this election, never will that happen,” he said.

In a goodwill message, renowned human rights activist, Aisha Yesufu described the Obi/Kwankwaso ticket as a perfect match for the rebirth of the nation.

She urged all Nigerians to rally support for the NDC, as the party sets its sights on winning the 2027 presidential election.

“This election is not just about Peter Obi, it is about all of us. It is about a new Nigeria free from bad governance.

“I am determined to contribute my quota and this is why when I stand, I stand to fight for a just society.

“So, I want to urge every Nigerian who is eager for a better Nigeria to rise up and fight for it.

“We cannot remain slaves in our country, thank God that today, we have a man who is ready to deliver that new Nigeria to all of us,” Ms Yesufu said.

Also speaking at the event, Senator Victor Umeh, who represents Anambra Central at the Nigeria Senate, noted that the Obi/Kwankwaso ticket represents the hope of all Nigerians for a secured future.

READ ALSO: Police invite local council chairman over attack on NDC secretariat

“My stand on this coming election is that Mr Peter Obi alongside his running mate, Alhaji Rabiu Kwankwaso are the best candidates for the presidency.

“If you ask me, they represent a secured future for Nigeria. A future where our country will become great again.

“So, I want to appeal to the people of the South-east to be united in the task ahead of us.

“We have a responsibility to give the Obi/Kwankwaso presidential ticket the needed foundation to triumph in this coming election.

“We must put our votes together to deliver the NDC as a party,” Mr Umeh said.

(NAN)

World.title: Anambra CityBoy Movement threatens mass defection over leadership crisis
World.content:
The Anambra chapter of the CityBoy Movement (CBM) has threatened mass defection from the All Progressives Congress (APC) over an unresolved leadership crisis.

The State Secretary of CBM, Wilson Ekwerekwu, issued the warning in a protest letter addressed to the movement’s national leadership, which was made available to the News Agency of Nigeria on Friday.

Mr Ekwerekwu, who is also the leader of the Coalition of Igbo Youth Leaders in South-East Nigeria, called for urgent intervention over the alleged imposition of parallel executives in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He warned that failure to resolve the crisis could prompt him and other aggrieved members to reconsider their membership of the movement and allegiance to the APC.

“Aggrieved CBM executives and political followers sharing these concerns are equally considering their continued participation in the movement and allegiance to the APC,” he said.

Mr Ekwerekwu urged the national leadership to clarify the recognised leadership structure in Anambra and explain the basis for introducing new executives without adequate consultation with existing state leaders.

He also called for an urgent reconciliation involving affected executives and a framework to promote inclusion and prevent parallel leadership arrangements.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Other demands included clear communication on the movement’s strategic direction, mobilisation plans and expectations of state executives ahead of the 2027 elections.

“Let me be unequivocal: this situation cannot continue indefinitely,” he said.

Mr Ekwerekwu said members joined the movement with commitment, political networks and grassroots mobilisation capacity, rather than merely seeking leadership positions.

“We are asking for leadership, not favours; consultation, not imposition; and inclusion, not exclusion,” he said.

He stressed that grassroots contributions deserved recognition, adding that the movement’s cohesion depended on members’ confidence and commitment.

He expressed willingness to engage constructively with the national leadership but urged it to act swiftly to resolve the crisis and prevent further divisions in the Anambra chapter.

World.title: 2027: Reset your mind, align with people’s choice, Oshiomhole tells Makinde
World.content:
Adams Oshiomhole

By Adeola Badru

Senator Adams Oshiomhole, former Governor of Edo State, has urged Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, to reconsider his political position ahead of the 2027 general elections, saying the country needed leaders committed to sustaining progress.

Oshiomhole, who spoke in Ibadan on Saturday during President Bola Tinubu’s rally at the historic Mapo Hall, challenged Makinde to align himself with the wishes of the electorate, insisting that the governor must first reconsider his own position on Tinubu’s re-election bid.

The former Edo governor, who expressed support for Tinubu’s second-term ambition, described the forthcoming election as a decisive moment for Nigeria and questioned whether Makinde’s call for a reset was intended to reverse policies he said had benefited ordinary Nigerians.

“This coming election is a decisive factor. We have a leader, the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.

Oshiomhole said he had questions for Makinde over his position on Tinubu’s continuation in office, particularly regarding the administration’s student loan scheme, infrastructure development, and improved welfare for university lecturers.

He asked whether Makinde’s opposition to the president’s re-election was connected to the federal government’s decision to provide financial assistance to students from poor backgrounds through the student loan scheme.

“Is Seyi Makinde angry because Tinubu is giving loans to the children of poor people in our universities? Is that what Makinde wants to reset?” he asked.

The senator also questioned whether the governor intended to reverse the federal government’s infrastructure projects, particularly the coastal highway linking Lagos to Calabar, which he said would improve connectivity and make movement easier for Nigerians.

“The President is creating massive infrastructure to connect Lagos to Calabar so that our people can move. Is that what Makinde wants to reset?” he said.

Oshiomhole further challenged Makinde’s position on the welfare of university lecturers, citing the University of Ibadan as an example of an institution that had previously experienced repeated disruptions to its academic calendar due to industrial action.

He recalled that university lecturers had, in the past, frequently embarked on strikes, disrupting academic activities and delaying students’ graduation.

“For this city has the most outstanding university in Africa, the University of Ibadan. For a long, long time, the lecturer will teach you for two days and then will go on strike for three days. Is that not true?” he said.

The former governor said the Tinubu administration had deliberately prioritized the welfare of university lecturers, whom he described as critical to developing the country’s future workforce.

He argued that improved remuneration for lecturers would strengthen the education sector, encourage qualified academics to remain in the profession, and ensure that students could complete their studies without repeated interruptions.

“I just want to deliver this message. Now, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has deliberately decided that those who make the manpower of tomorrow are the lecturers in our universities.”

“And he has increased their pay substantially so that for four years, your academic calendar has not been interrupted,” he said.

Oshiomhole asked whether Makinde intended to reverse the policy, allow strikes to return to the university system, or reduce lecturers’ salaries.

“Does Makinde want to reset this policy? Does he want the strike to return? Does he want to reduce the salaries of lecturers?” he asked.

He maintained that improved remuneration for university lecturers would encourage more intelligent minds to return to the teaching profession, which he described as one of the noblest professions.

“When you pay lecturers very well, intelligent minds will go back to the teaching profession, which is the most noble profession,” he said.

Oshiomhole, who repeatedly challenged Makinde’s call for a reset, urged the governor to reconsider his position and align himself with the aspirations of the electorate ahead of the 2027 elections.

He said Nigeria needed political leaders who would prioritize the country’s development and sustain policies aimed at improving the lives of citizens.

“When you go back, tell the man in Ibadan he is for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.

The senator concluded by urging Makinde to reconsider his position before the election, stressing that the country’s progress should remain the priority of political leaders.

“The governor needs to reset his own mind before the election. We want Nigeria to progress. Thank you and God bless,” Oshiomhole said

World.title: Oyo rally: Tinubu assures Nigerians of improved electricity supply
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu

President Bola Tinubu has assured Nigerians of improved electricity supply, stressing that his administration is working round the clock to boost the power sector.

The president stated this on Saturday in Ibadan during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign held at the historic Mapo Hall.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the event also featured the formal presentation by President Tinubu of Sen. Sharafadeen Alli as the APC’s governorship candidate to the party’s supporters in Oyo State.

Tinubu commended Oyo State for the overwhelming votes delivered to him in the 2023 elections and urged the citizens to see the party as their own.

“For the sake of progress, development, your children’s future, and prosperity for our country, I urge you to stay the course.

“For our children and grandchildren to benefit from the hope of Nigeria, we must give them the right education and invest in agriculture.

“For Oyo State, we just signed an agreement with Yutong Automobile of China to reopen the old Leyland Automobile factory in Ibadan.

“This aims to start production of commercial vehicles and commence general automobile assembly plant.

“We will continue to bring in more industry, and, in addition, I guarantee you improvement in electricity supply,” he said.

The president, while commending the support of traditional rulers and leaders of the party in the state, urged supporters not to be deceived by other parties that allegedly come to dupe them.

Earlier, in separate goodwill messages, the governor of Ekiti State, Mr. Biodun Oyebanji, on behalf of the 31 progressive governors, and the Anambra and Osun governors, urged the electorate in Yoruba not to trade their votes.

This, he said, was necessary to let the president continue his reforms and good works, such as student loan initiatives, infrastructural development, and various transformational moves in other sectors.

Also, the Senate Leader, Sen. Opeyemi Bamidele, said that splitting the APC votes for different parties across different political offices in Oyo State would not profit the party maximally.

He stressed that votes for the presidential, governorship, and national and state assemblies should be for the APC.

Bamidele added that the achievements of the president in the last three years should be the template for the campaign.

Also, Sen. Adams Oshiomhole said that the coming election remained a decisive factor, as various initiatives and reforms of the president were already resetting Nigeria and should not be a campaign slogan for any other candidate.

NAN reports that the campaign was attended by both former and serving governors, their wives, members of the Senate and House of Representatives, and party leaders, among others. (NAN)

World.title: Zelensky reaffirms Ukraine’s wish to join NATO
World.content:
Zelensky

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky on Saturday reiterated his country’s determination to join NATO, following proposals to provide Kyiv with security guarantees similar to those of the military alliance.

“Of course Ukraine very much wants to be in NATO,” Zelensky told reporters, judging that membership of the alliance was one of the “most obvious security guarantees” for his country.

The issue of Ukraine joining NATO, ruled out by Washington since 2025, resurfaced in recent days during fresh talks to end the war nearly five years after Russia’s invasion.

At a meeting with Kyiv’s allies in Berlin on Thursday, US envoy Jared Kushner said Washington could be ready to grant Ukraine a security guarantee similar to that provided under Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty.

That clause – the cornerstone of NATO – states that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all allies.

On Friday, the French presidency said offering Kyiv “Article 5-type” protection would in practice amount to bringing Ukraine into the alliance.

The same day, two Russian missiles and a suspected drone landed in southeastern Poland, a NATO member bordering Ukraine.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte denounced violations of Polish airspace, calling them “clearly dangerous”.

Vanguard News

World.title: Outrage as Defence Ministry publicises APC campaign rally
World.content:
Photo Credit: Defence Ministry/X

By Ayobami Okerinde

The Ministry of Defence has come under criticism on social media after its official X account published details of preparations for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in support of President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid.

In a post on Saturday, it announced that the rally was scheduled to hold at Mapo Hall, Ibadan, Oyo State, on November 21, 2026, with Tinubu and key party officials expected to attend.

It also disclosed that the Minister of Defence, retired General Christopher Musa, had visited the venue on Friday night to assess security arrangements and other preparations ahead of the event.

“Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), OFR, Friday night conducted an on-the-spot inspection of the venue as part of strategic preparations ahead of the upcoming presidential campaign rally in the state,” the post reads.

“During the visit, General Musa toured the premises and surrounding perimeters to evaluate security readiness, crowd management logistics, and overall infrastructural preparedness. President Bola Tinubu GCFR, and key party officials would be on ground for the rally.”

Defence Ministry/X

Defence Ministry/X

The post, which was accompanied by photographs of the minister’s inspection, was followed by criticism from several Nigerians, who questioned the use of an official government platform to publicise the activities of a political party.

One of the critics, Kunle Adebajo, described the development as “political psychosis so deep it’s ridiculous even by Nigerian standards”.

Another X user, N6, questioned the ministry’s apparent involvement in partisan activities, asking, “How is the Ministry of Defence handle clearly being Partisan. Have you lost it?”

Similarly, a user identified as Dollarain2000 said, “Is this really the official handle of Nigeria’s Defence Ministry? Or the Security Directorate of the APC Presidential Campaign Council?” the user asked.

Another critic, Emmanuel Doji, expressed concern over what he described as the blurring of boundaries between government responsibilities and involvement in partisan political activities.

He wrote, “So what exactly is the meaning of this? The official Twitter handle of the Ministry of Defence is now publishing a political party’s campaign schedule and updates on preparations for its rally? Where exactly do we draw the line between government business and party politics?

“A whole Ministry of Defence is now a publicity arm of the APC. Will it also publish the activities and campaign schedules of other political parties? This is completely inappropriate and should be condemned. Government institutions should not be turned into platforms for partisan political activities. This is not how things should be done.”

Another user, Benjamin, wrote, “Defence handle of the nation doing this! No, no, no, no! This is preposterous! This is no more Democracy!”

Josephu_o also criticised the development, he wrote, “Imagine the Ministry of Defence, an institution funded by Nigerian taxpayers and entrusted with the security of over 200 million citizens, using its official platform to publicise a political party’s re-election rally.

“Is this a Ministry of Defence or an APC campaign publicity office? State institutions belong to Nigerians, not political parties,” the user added.

Another user, HonShield, questioned whether the ministry would extend the same publicity to opposition parties, asking, “Dear Ministry of Defence, will you also do this for other political parties? Do you now belong to the APC to be tweeting for their campaign? What’s going on in this country for God’s sake?”

World.title: Haaland in VAR controversy as Man City held by Fulham
World.content:
Manchester City’s Norwegian striker #09 Erling Haaland reacts at the final whistle during the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Fulham at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on November 21, 2026. (Photo by Oli SCARFF / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE. No use with unauthorized audio, video, data, fixture lists, club/league logos or ‘live’ services. Online in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No video emulation. Social media in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No use in betting publications, games or single club/league/player publications. /

Erling Haaland was controversially denied a crucial goal as Manchester City’s spluttering Premier League title challenge suffered a fresh blow in a 1-1 draw against Fulham on Saturday.

Enzo Maresca’s side trailed to Rodrigo Muniz’s early opener at the Etihad Stadium before Haaland’s equaliser was contentiously ruled out.

The City striker kicked the ball out of the grasp of Fulham keeper Bernd Leno on the goal-line.

But Leno barely had two hands on the ball when Haaland made contact, giving City reason to feel aggrieved with the decision.

Elliot Anderson saved City from a fourth successive league defeat as the England midfielder equalised in the second half with his first top-flight goal since signing from Nottingham Forest in the close-season.

But it was another frustrating afternoon for third-placed City, who could not find a winner and were booed off at full-time.

Leaders Arsenal can extend their lead over City to eight points if they win at Newcastle later on Saturday.

After making a blistering start to the season with seven successive league wins, City are winless in their last four top-flight matches.

It was the first time in 15 years and 21 games that City had failed to beat Fulham.

Still waiting to discover the result of their appeal against the guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules, City have looked increasingly distracted in recent weeks.

Maresca has claimed City are not bothered by the “noise” around the financial scandal, which is likely to include a huge points deduction if the appeal fails.

But his team’s lethargic performances of late suggest otherwise, with tricky tests against Napoli on Tuesday and Arsenal next weekend threatening to extend their slump.

– Slumping City –

City needed a fast start to ease their anxiety and Erling Haaland almost delivered it when his looping header was cleared off the line.

But Maresca has failed to fix the defensive problems that ailed City in their previous three games.

Fulham took full advantage of City’s flaws to snatch the lead with an incisive counter in the 16th minute.

Former City winger Oscar Bobb pounced on a wayward pass and accelerated down the right flank before picking out Muniz’s run into the penalty area.

With City’s defence in disarray, Muniz kept his composure to curl a fine finish into the top corner.

Maresca turned away in disgust and his frustration only increased when City were denied a leveller in the 26th minute.

Iliman Ndiaye’s cross reached Haaland inside the six-yard box but the Norway striker’s weak volley was saved by Leno.

Haaland’s momentum carried him into Leno and he kicked the ball over the line as the Fulham keeper struggled to get hold of it.

But Haaland’s celebrations were curtailed by VAR’s decision to disallow the goal for a foul on Leno.

Haaland squandered a golden opportunity to drag City level when he blazed wildly over from Phil Foden’s defence splitting pass.

Enduring one of his more profligate days, Haaland scuffed wastefully wide from Nico O’Reilly’s pass.

Out of sync for so long, City finally found some rhythm after the break and their pressure was rewarded in the 58th minute.

Fulham failed to clear a corner and Anderson pounced, drilling a fierce volley past Leno from the edge of the area.

Anderson was inches away from putting City ahead moments later with a low drive that fizzes just wide.

It was that kind of day for City, whose season is in danger of spiralling out of control before they even discover their appeal verdict.

World.title: 2027: Tinubu takes swipe at Makinde, urges Oyo voters to choose APC
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has told the people of Oyo State not to mind Governor Seyi Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), and urged them to vote for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) from top to bottom.

The president spoke on Saturday at the APC presidential rally in Ibadan, the Oyo state capital.

Apparently referring to the governor, the president said, “There is a party out there parading themselves. Please don’t mind them and don’t listen to them. They are only interested in clearing what you have. Vote for APC from top to bottom.”

Tinubu said he would not speak at length. “I will not be able to speak much to you. I just want to greet you. This is our party. It is your party. Is that clear?

“You voted overwhelmingly for the APC last time. You must stay the course for the sake of progress, the prosperity of our country and the development of your children and great-grandchildren,” he said.

Before addressing the rally, the president asked the gathering to observe a minute of silence for the victims of the boat accident in Bayelsa State. “Our condolences go to the people of Bayelsa State and the bereaved families. May God grant the people of Bayelsa peace and happiness and prevent a recurrence of such an incident. We will support them,” he said.

Tinubu also announced an investment for Oyo State. “For your state, we have just signed an agreement with China’s Yutong to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport vehicles and establish an automobile assembly plant there. We will continue to bring industries. You will see progress and development,” he added.

Speaking on behalf of the APC governors, the governor of Ekiti State, Mr Biodun Oyebanji, urged the Yoruba to turn out for the President.

“We are appealing to the Yoruba people, particularly our sons and daughters, to come out and support the presidential candidate, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. On January 16, let us all come out and vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Senator Sarafadeen Ali of the APC. When the time comes, we will also support our candidates contesting for the Senate, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly.

“I appeal to the Yoruba people not to allow this opportunity to slip away. Let us stand together and ensure that our party succeeds in Nigeria,” Oyebanji said.

World.title: Diallo present as African football boss Motsepe reiterates support for Infantino
World.content:
Confederation of African Football (CAF) President Patrice Motsepe (3rd L, lower row)), and Federation Internationale de Football Association (FIFA) Gianni Infantino (2nd L, lower row), sit among other delegates during the CAF 48TH Ordinary Assembly, in Abuja on November 21, 2026. African football supremo Patrice Motsepe said Saturday that all 54 members of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) support Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president. Motsepe made the declaration in Abuja, where CAF is holding its ordinary general assembly and at which one of Infantino’s two rivals, French football chief Philippe Diallo is present. Former Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima is the other candidate. The trio will learn whether they have been successful on March 18 next year in Rabat — the winning candidate must obtain a majority of the 211 associations. (Photo by Light Oriye Tamunotonye / AFP)

African football supremo Patrice Motsepe said Saturday that all 54 members of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) support Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president.

Motsepe made the declaration in Abuja, where CAF is holding its ordinary general assembly and at which one of Infantino’s two rivals, French football chief Philippe Diallo is present.

Former Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima is the other candidate.

The trio will learn whether they have been successful on March 18 next year in Rabat — the winning candidate must obtain a majority of the 211 associations.

CAF’s support for Infantino comes hours after another of his steadfast supporters South American football’s governing body CONMEBOL gave him their “unanimous” backing.

CAF has been consistently behind Infantino — who is seeking a fourth and final term — even after the furore he stirred up in July with his shortlived FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Morocco is co-hosting the 2030 World Cup.

“Gianni, you have our support on behalf of the 54 nations in Africa to be our candidate,” Motsepe said.

“I have a report from all 54 member associations in Africa to say that we are unanimously supporting Gianni.”

Infantino has faced multiple calls to step down and lost the backing of European football’s governing body UEFA, whilst CONCACAF has also been strident in its criticism of the 56-year-old Swiss lawyer.

Motsepe though has been a vocal supporter and Infantino said such loyalty was reciprocal.

“You will always find, in me and in FIFA, a trusted partner,” Infantino told the assembly, announcing cash inflow of $25 million to each member of CAF, starting January 2027 for development projects.

On Wednesday, UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister told AFP that Diallo, a 63-year-old lawyer whose Senegalese-born father boxed for France at the 1960 Olympics in Rome, should not be seen as solely a European candidate.

“He is a francophone, which is an important asset in lots of CAF countries,” she said.

McAllister, who in 2023 became the first woman to be elected a vice-president of UEFA, noted though that confederations do not vote as a bloc.

“There is a soft space which Philippe can exploit and convince some federations within each confederation to support a reform agenda,” the 61-year-old said.

“There is a lot of discomfort around the behaviour of Gianni Infantino and a desire to challenge the concentration of power in his hands.

“This applies everywhere in world football. This is not about Europe, the same rules apply globally.”

World.title: Tinubu inaugurates UI medical hostel, promises 50,000 bed spaces in federal varsities
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has pledged to deliver additional 50,000 bed space hostels across federal tertiary institutions by the end of 2027 to tackle accommodation challenges confronting students

Tinubu made the pledge on Saturday at the inauguration of Block E of the College of Medicine hostel, University of Ibadan (UI), located at Alexander Brown Hall, University College Hospital.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the hostel block was donated by the Chagoury family.

The President, represented by the Minister of Education, Dr Maruf Alausa, said that the 50,000 bed space hostels would be delivered through the ₦400 billion Student Hostels Programme, implemented via the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) and Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs).

He said the initiative was aimed at providing students with safe and decent accommodation to support their education.

“The accommodation shortage at the College of Medicine has become a critical challenge following the 2020 directive of the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) requiring clinical students of medicine and dentistry to reside within the University College Hospital (UCH) premises for accreditation purposes.

“The college faced a shortfall of 490 bed spaces, representing 44.5 per cent of its accommodation requirement, leaving many students exposed to insecurity and difficulties attending essential clinical sessions,” the president said.

According to him, the shortage also prevented the college from fully utilising its annual admission quota for the Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) programme.

Tinubu said his administration was prioritising education funding and reforms through initiatives such as the Nigerian Education Sector Renewal Initiative, Nigeria Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), TETFund and the Student Venture Capital Grant.

He added that more than 36 universities had benefited from the Renewed Hope Energising Education Programme, with power installations ranging from 2.5 megawatts to 12 megawatts.

The President also said that the government had completed 20 compressed natural gas (CNG) conversion centres and maintenance facilities in some universities, with 40 additional facilities expected by the end of 2028.

Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor of UI, Prof. Peter Olapegba, said the inauguration of Block E marked another milestone in efforts to provide adequate accommodation for medical students and meet accreditation requirements.

Olapegba expressed appreciation to the benefactors, Ambassador Gilbert Ramez Chagoury and his brother, Ronald Chagoury, for their contribution to medical education.

“The hostel, named the Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR Block, provides accommodation for 192 medical and dental students in 48 rooms, with four students per room.

“The building also has four reading rooms, each measuring about 71 square metres, as well as rooms equipped with toilets, showers and kitchenettes,” Olapegba said.

The immediate past provost of the College of Medicine, Prof. Olayinka Omigbodun, said the hostel project was initiated to address the accommodation deficit that threatened the college’s ability to meet accreditation requirements.

Omigbodun, represented by Prof. Fatai Adeniyi, said the college required 1,101 bed spaces for clinical students but had only 611, resulting in a shortfall of about 500 beds.

She said the deficit had previously constrained the college’s ability to admit students up to its annual quota.

The Provost, College of Medicine, Prof. Temidayo Ogundiran, expressed appreciation to stakeholders and supporters who contributed to the realisation of the project.

According to him, the various contributions of the President Bola Tinubu-led administration had repositioned the education sector. (NAN)

World.title: Abia APC to Tinubu: Gives Us a Minister
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Boniface Okoro in Umuahia

The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Abia State has appealed to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to appoint a minister from the state to represent it in the Federal Executive Council (FEC).

The Chairman of Abia State APC and Coordinator of the Presidential Campaign Council in the state, Hon. Chijioke Chukwu, made the appeal while addressing a grand rally organised by the party to flag off the campaign for the re-election of President Tinubu in Abia held at the Umuahia Township Stadium.

Chukwu noted that Abia State currently has no representation in the Federal Executive Council following the resignation of Rt. Hon. Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, who previously served as Minister of State for Labour and Employment.

Onyejeocha resigned to contest for the Isuikwuato/Umunneochi Federal Constituency seat.

According to Chukwu, Abia deserves a ministerial position in the Tinubu administration.

He therefore appealed to the President to consider appointing Onyejeocha’s replacement from Abia, “in the interest of fairness, inclusiveness and adequate representation of Abia State at the federal level.”

Chukwu also reaffirmed the commitment of the Abia APC to the re-election of President Tinubu, assuring him that the party would mobilise its structures and supporters across the 17 local government areas to deliver overwhelming support in the January 16, 2027 presidential election.

He expressed confidence that the APC in Abia State will secure over 90 per cent of the total votes cast in the state for President Tinubu.

Similarly, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu, while addressing the rally, assured Tinubu that the APC in Abia has the numbers to deliver him in the January 16, 2027 presidential poll, urging him not to beg anyone for 25 per cent votes in the state.

Kalu said Abia has about 2.3 million voters and 162,000 APC members. He said each member had been charged to bring 10 voters, which would deliver 1,620,000 votes, about 75 per cent of registered voters. “Nobody should convert you to a beggar of 25 per cent. Your sons and your daughters in Abia, we will give you 75 per cent,” Kalu said.

Kalu equally announced a donation of 100 branded buses fitted with public address systems to be shared across the 17 local government areas to preach the gospel of Tinubu, adding that they would be presented on December 7, at another grand rally to be held at Enyimba International Stadium, Aba. He appealed to Tinubu, who had chosen Enugu for the region, to consider coming to Abia on that day to see the strength of the party.

World.title: Kwara: Hospital Project as a Symbol of Malice
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

By Quadir Olatunde Adebayo

As thousands of Kwarans gathered in several locations across the state on Saturday, November 14th, 2026 for the 14th memorial prayers in remembrance of one of their heroes and benefactors, Dr. Abubakar Olusola Saraki, they all lamented about one common issue in the aftermath of the prayers. The issue is how the incumbent Governor Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq demolished the popular Ile Arugbo (Old People’s Home). Ile Arugbo was the place the late politician established as a centre for catering to the needs of old people, particularly aged women.

The late Saraki had held possession of the piece of land on which Ile Arugbo was located, opposite his residence in the GRA on Ilofa Road, for decades. His children, particularly former Senate President, Dr. Abubakar Bukola Saraki, and former Minister of State, Ministry of Solid Minerals, Senator Gbemisola Ruqayat Saraki, have sustained the legacy of caring for the elderly after their father’s demise.

However, in December 2019, barely six months after Governor Abdulrazaq assumed office, he ordered the forceful takeover of the piece of land on which Ile Arugbo was located. The government claimed that the land belonged to it and that even though it was allocated some time ago to the late Dr Saraki, there was no record that he perfected the documents.

The Ile Arugbo and the old Civil Service Clinic next to it were demolished despite protests from beneficiaries and many other residents. To create a justification for his action, the governor’s aides announced that the landed property was needed for a public purpose – that is, the building of a government hospital.

While the matter became a subject of litigation, the government went ahead to commence the construction of a conference centre and a hospital on the stretch of land that had hitherto hosted both Ile Arugbo and the Civil Service Clinic.

Many Kwarans believed the decision to build a hospital around the area was a mere attempt at justifying a politically motivated plan. They noted that the real aim was to demolish a major plank of the legacy of one of the widely acclaimed biggest philanthropists that the people of the state have ever seen.

Some of the people gathered at the Saturday prayer sessions questioned the need for another government hospital when the existing general hospital and other public health facilities remain unattended to, in terms of equipment, personnel, and funding.

Other commentators spoke about the fact that if the government truly wanted a new health facility, there are many areas of the state capital and other parts of the state with abundant land and space that could have hosted bigger facilities. The space in other places would have created enough room for vehicular traffic and parking than the present location.

“The target was Ile Arugbo. The projects – hospital and conference centre – only fit into the bigger grandiose idea of concentrating development in only one street and one area. That is Ahmadu Bello Way, Ilorin. This hospital, if it must be built in the government’s pathological belief in brick and mortar as the sure signs of development, can be located in other more spacious areas of Ilorin or other towns in the state”, said Mr. Mohammed Bashir, a public policy analyst.

He added that though the late Saraki was not above the law, the purpose he and his family used Ile Arugbo to serve deserves that the state government discretionally engage them on how they can formally perfect the process for the allocation of land. He added that a strict instruction that the property could only be used for the purpose for which it was allocated should then be issued.

“If Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq has good advisers, he should have been counselled to allow the Saraki family to pay necessary charges and continue using the land for the noble and philanthropic purpose of helping the growing population of old people in the state. He can even allocate another piece of land to them in other areas of the state. However, when the intention is not pure and Godly, the action cannot be considered right”, he added.

Ile Arugbo was used by the late politician to share money, clothing, food items and other necessary household materials like battery-powered torch lights, umbrellas, and utility necessities which the old people found useful to provide comfort for them in their respective homes. Also, free medical checks were provided for the old women who gathered at the place in their thousands every month during the late politician’s visit to Ilorin or in his absence.

Popularly known as ‘Oloye’ (Chief) by his supporters and admirers, the late Saraki was the biggest patron of the then Civil Service Clinic. The old women who needed medical attention were referred to the Clinic while the Oloye picked the bills. Doctors were also organised to visit the homes of the sick among the old women once information reached Dr. Saraki that any of them was indisposed and needed medical attention.

Even after the demolition of the Ile Arugbo, late Saraki’s son and former Senate President, Bukola, created a makeshift venue for the old women to gather around his father’s residence for the purpose of regularly receiving the provisions of money, food items, and other materials.

To further cement the narrative that the hospital project was an afterthought and that the aim was borne out of malice, many commentators believe the idea of a civil service clinic or a public health facility being established in the Government Reservation Area (GRA) where the rich people in the town reside and which is definitely out of reach of most of the common people, is ill-conceived.

The GRA is mostly occupied by rich people who can afford medical attention in private clinics and even travel to Lagos, Abuja, and other bigger cities in the country and abroad for medical attention. Those who mostly patronise public health facilities are the common people and the less privileged lower-class people. At best, such facilities get patronage from the middle-class people whose ranks have been seriously depleted due to the general economic situation. To put a government hospital in an area reserved for the rich is not just a misplaced priority; it is a misallocation of the resources of a state. It should have been sited where the people who need it can easily access it.

The facility as it is will not have enough vehicular parking space. It will only worsen the traffic situation along the mostly residential area. That is why a new government hospital, if it must be built to satisfy the fancy of a governor, will be more suitable in other parts of town where there is room for more space for parking facilities and future expansion.

It is also necessary to weigh the benefit of the hospital in Ilofa Road against the current situation of the 35 other government health facilities in the state. One writer, Adeniyi Isola in an article titled ‘The Real Cost of Kwara’s Elephant Projects’ published in October lamented that some of the money being wasted in constructing grandiose projects with little or no economic value like this hospital in the GRA could have been deployed to “equip and fully staff primary healthcare centres across the state, reduce maternal and infant mortality rates that continue to define health outcomes in Kwara”. He continued that “it could have provided MRI machines to state hospitals, ending the heartbreaking reality of Kwarans travelling to other states for basic diagnostic services at higher costs and greater risks”.

An earlier article by the same writer had identified that Kwara State had just 362 medical doctors while only 99 of them are on the government’s payroll. That is an average of one doctor to 11, 767 people in a state said to have 4.2 million people. The state-owned premier health facility, the Kwara State University of Teaching Hospital (KWASUTH) is said to consistently experience power outages, lack of water supply, inadequate staffing, and acute shortage of basic surgical equipment. In the hospital, patients are tasked with the purchase of fuel to power generators and water supply. All these result in delayed treatment for patients, avoidable complications, and preventable deaths.

The Harmony Advanced Diagnostic Centre (HADC), in the Oko Erin area of Ilorin, which used to serve patients from across the North-central and South-west parts of the country has been deliberately allowed to deteriorate and go down because it was one of the achievements of the past governments. Now, the Centre that used to have the most modern medical diagnostic equipment in the country can no longer boast of a single functional MRI machine. As of February, no single functional MRI machine is in the entire state. And this is because the Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq government wants to build a new diagnostic centre.

This shortage of equipment, personnel, and other basic amenities/ necessities in the 45 health facilities owned by the state government is what should be the priority of a government that plans, that is honest, patriotic, and has good intentions. Not the construction of another building that will suffer the same deprivation as the existing ones. However, when the aim is malicious, when the motivation is to settle scores, when the purpose is to destroy the legacy of a past hero and justify that action by appearing altruistic, the judgement will be clouded and the outcome will be warped. All these are what the grandiose new clinic and convention centre being built on the property that once hosted Ile Arugbo are afflicted with.

*Adebayo writes from Ilorin, Kwara State.

World.title: NRS Pushes For Simpler Tax Rules To Unlock Nigeria’s Creative Economy
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

.Says clarity, formalisation, investment and partnership critical to sector’s growth

By Emmanuel Jonathan

The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has called for simpler, clearer and business-friendly tax rules to unlock the investment potential of Nigeria’s creative economy, stressing that tax administration must facilitate enterprise growth, innovation and prosperity.

The Service said the emergence of digital business models, intellectual property-driven enterprises and cross-border transactions required tax system creators, entrepreneurs and investors could easily understand and navigate.

The Executive Chairman of the NRS, Dr. Zacch Adedeji, made the call at a high-level dialogue on taxation and investment in the creative economy at the Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) event in Lagos. He was represented by the Executive Director, People, Stakeholders and Communication, Mr. Obinna Ihedioha.

Adedeji described Nigeria’s creative economy as one of its most promising economic assets, noting that the country’s greatest resource was the minds and talents of its young people.

He said the sector had evolved beyond entertainment into a major economic enterprise capable of generating jobs, earning foreign exchange, attracting investment and expanding economic opportunities.

According to him, digital platforms and emerging business models had changed how value was created, with creative entrepreneurs building businesses around copyrights, designs, brands, digital products and audiences.

He said the development required a corresponding shift in tax administration to ensure that fiscal policies did not discourage innovation, investment or business expansion.

“Government needs sustainable revenue to invest in education, security, technology and infrastructure. But how we tax matters as much as what we collect. It shapes whether businesses start, whether investors come, and whether enterprises grow or stay small,” he said.

Adedeji stressed that taxation should not be pursued at the expense of enterprise but should support the expansion of prosperity through a productive economy, noting that growing businesses would ultimately strengthen government revenue and its capacity to deliver public services.

He said the new tax laws provided an opportunity to reset the system around clearer rules, fewer burdens for small businesses and an administration built on service, understanding and support.

He identified clarity, understanding and value as critical pillars of an effective tax system for the creative economy, adding that formalisation should provide businesses access to finance, contracts, investment, larger markets and protection.

The NRS, he said, participated in CANEX as a partner in enterprise through a high-level dialogue, an Investment and Tax Advisory Hub for creators and investors, and the Creative Economy Tax and Investment Initiative (CETII), designed to sustain engagement beyond the event.

The Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musa Musawa, underscored the importance of the creative sector to Nigeria’s economic diversification agenda, describing it as a major opportunity for job creation, wealth generation and youth empowerment.

Musawa said the sector had continued to expand even before the establishment of a dedicated ministry, adding that government policies should enable creative entrepreneurs to earn more from their talents and intellectual property.

She identified intellectual property protection, digital infrastructure and access to funding as priorities, noting that Nigeria could draw lessons from countries such as South Korea, which had transformed its creative industries into major drivers of economic growth.

The Executive Director, Finance and Corporate Services, Mr. Muhammed L. Abubakar, addressed concerns surrounding income earned abroad, explaining that tax residency status and double taxation agreements between Nigeria and other countries were important considerations in determining applicable tax treatment.

Similarly, the Executive Director, Policy and Compliance, Mr. Shettima Tamadi, said tax simplification required identifying practical difficulties businesses encountered under existing rules.

He said understanding taxpayers’ challenges was essential to making the system more efficient and responsive.

“For entrepreneurs in the creative sector, simpler rules can make it easier to understand their tax obligations and plan for them as their businesses grow,” Tamadi said.

During a panel discussion, tax policy expert, Mr. Simeon Onyegbula, examined provisions in the tax framework that could support creative enterprises, including income tax relief for qualifying small companies, changes to minimum tax provisions and the implications of recovering Value Added Tax paid on qualifying business equipment for cash flow.

Mr. Mustapha Akaje said tax incentives were designed to encourage investment and promote economic development, explaining provisions relating to the zero per cent Company Income Tax rate applicable to qualifying small companies.

Speaking on business formalisation, Mr. Kazeem Lawal stressed that formalising creative enterprises was essential to their growth, credibility and sustainability.

He said operating business transactions through personal accounts could constrain expansion, while proper business registration and structures gave enterprises a distinct legal identity, improved record-keeping and compliance, and strengthened their ability to attract investors, strategic partners and access local and international markets.

In his closing remarks, Ihedioha said the dialogue had underscored the need to move the relationship between tax administration and the creative economy from apprehension to understanding, and from compliance as a burden to formalisation as an opportunity.

Drawing on the story of Kenneth Nnebue, the Onitsha trader whose use of unsold videotapes to produce Living in Bondage in 1992 helped lay the foundation for Nollywood, he said the creative economy demonstrated how ideas could transform circumstances and create entire industries.

He noted that although the tools of creative production had evolved from videotapes to laptops, digital platforms and global audiences, the ingenuity driving the industry remained the same.

Ihedioha said interactions at the NRS Investment and Tax Advisory Hub revealed that uncertainty, rather than unwillingness to comply, was a major concern among creative entrepreneurs.

He recounted the experience of a young animator who had earned income from international clients for two years without filing tax returns but feared registering her business because of possible penalties for past non-compliance.

According to him, NRS officials provided guidance on registration, tax obligations, provisions supporting small businesses and digital channels for compliance, with the aim of replacing fear with clarity and enabling entrepreneurs to enter the formal economy with confidence.

He identified three lessons from the engagement: clarity was an incentive in itself; formalisation must deliver tangible value; and sustainable growth of the creative economy required partnerships among government, creators, investors, financial institutions, regulators and development partners.

“Uncertainty is a tax nobody collects but everybody pays,” Ihedioha said, emphasising that creators and investors were more likely to formalise, invest and grow when tax rules were clear, predictable and accessible.

He said the NRS regarded CANEX WKND as more than a one-off engagement, noting that the Investment and Tax Advisory Hub had demonstrated the value of direct engagement with creative entrepreneurs.

He added that CETII would provide a continuing framework for collaboration on tax education, business formalisation, investment facilitation and policy dialogue.

Ihedioha commended the Minister, the Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment, Afreximbank, speakers, panellists and other stakeholders for their contributions, reiterating the NRS’s commitment to creating an enabling environment for creative businesses to formalise, grow, attract investment and contribute to national development.

The Group Director, Corporate Communications and Stakeholder Engagement (GD-CC&SE), Mrs. Yinka Akpata, was among the stakeholders from the NRS that participated at the event to ensure the successful outing of the 2026 edition of CANEX WKND.

*Emmanuel Jonathan is a Communications Expert and Head of Editorial Unit, Corporate Communications Department, Nigeria Revenue Service, and writes from Lagos.

World.title: FG Tackles High Transportation Cost at UNILAG, 3 Others with 4 New CNG Stations
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

*Minister vows reduction in students’ fares in 3 months

*Facility now exists at 11 institutions nationwide, says MDGIF

Peter Uzoho

The federal government yesterday inaugurated four new Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) daughter stations and vehicle conversion centres at the University of Lagos (UNILAG), University of Ibadan (UI), Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA), and Federal University Oye-Ekiti (FUOYE), in a major push to cut high transportation costs for students and staff under the Project SPROUT.

The facilities were inaugurated live at UNILAG, with simultaneous remote inauguration at UI, FUTA and FUOYE.

The project, funded by the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF) and delivered by Femadec Energy Limited, brings the total number of campus CNG stations now in operation nationwide to 11.

Speaking at the ceremony in Lagis, the Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, said the initiative, known as the Special Palliative Relief on University Transportation (Project SPROUT), was designed to directly address the cost of getting to class, a major concern repeatedly raised by students.

He said the programme was designed to reach 20 federal universities, beginning with a pilot phase of one tertiary institution from each of the six geopolitical zones, adding that with the inauguration of the four institutions, government was well on its way to achieving its objective.

Alausa said for most students who make several trips a day between accommodation, lecture halls and laboratories, even a modest saving on each journey can make a difference.

He urged university managements and transport operators to work together to ensure that students share in the savings through affordable fares and dependable shuttle services.

As part of the intervention, he said UNILAG will receive 10 CNG buses to ease campus transportation, while UI, FUTA and FUOYE will each receive five buses.

The minister also announced that 1,000 faculty members, academic and non-academic staff at UNILAG will get discounted conversion of their cars from petrol to CNG.

Explaining the savings, Alausa said a trip to Ibadan that costs about N10,000 on petrol would cost only about N2,500 on CNG, representing just 25 per cent of the cost.

“If you don’t see reduction in three months, I need to know. Then I’ll have a meeting with your vice chancellor,” he vowed.

He added that government plans to deliver another 40 conversion centres to federal tertiary institutions, with the first batch of 20 already being finalised with MDGIF to ensure that by the end of the year, 60 federal tertiary institutions would have a CNG conversion centre.

He also said the centres will serve as practical training sites for engineering, technology and science students.

In his remarks, the Executive Director of MDGIF, Mr. Oluwole Adama, said the inauguration was a direct expression of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s directive that Nigeria’s gas resources must create opportunities ordinary Nigerians can see, touch and benefit from.

He said four locations, one shared ambition, had come together to bring useful gas infrastructure closer to institutions and communities, with UNILAG, UI, FUTA and FUOYE joining the class of institutions driving the President’s initiative on the use of CNG.

Adama listed the other joint venture stations with Femadec already inaugurated and operational as Yakubu Gowon University, Abuja; Federal University of Technology, Owerri; Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife; University of Uyo; University of Calabar; Federal University of Petroleum Resources, Effurun; and University of Nigeria, Enugu Campus.

He disclosed that within a few weeks, nine other stations, mostly in the North, would be unveiled.

He explained that under Section 52 of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA), MDGIF exists to turn viable gas investments into working infrastructure, with a portfolio of 31 projects made up of 205 infrastructure assets across the country.

In just two years, Adama said MDGIF has supported the delivery of 25 fully operational CNG stations nationwide, adding that the UNILAG facility was the 11th CNG station inaugurated in Lagos State alone, a clear signal that CNG was no longer a promise for tomorrow.

“But the figure that matters most to me is not the number of stations. It is the number of Nigerians who can put this infrastructure to productive use,” Adama said, urging students to study the technology, ask questions and build solutions for safer operations and smarter energy systems.

On his part, the Chief Executive Officer of Femadec Energy Limited, Mr. Fola Akinnola, said the event marked another defining milestone in Nigeria’s clean energy transition and a major chapter in a disciplined, nationwide 20-campus rollout.

He said the journey began with the first three pioneering stations at University of Abuja, Obafemi Awolowo University and Federal University of Technology, Owerri, followed days ago by four more at University of Uyo, University of Calabar, Federal University of Petroleum Resources, Effurun, and University of Nigeria, Enugu Campus.

With today’s inauguration, he said Femadec’s cumulative footprint has reached 11 tertiary institutions, while engineering teams were finalising six additional universities for commissioning before the end of the year, with the remaining three to be commissioned early next year.

Akinnola said each station was designed as a living laboratory and hands-on training and conversion hub, giving engineering and technical students direct exposure to gas infrastructure management, vehicle conversion, maintenance and international safety standards.

World.title: Tinubu Mourns Bayelsa Boat Victims
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

* Directs relevant disaster rescue agencies to ensure successful recovery and rescue operation

* Also directs his re-election campaign in Ibadan to hold with less fanfare as mark of honour to lives lost to the disaster

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has expressed deep sadness over the tragic incident on Friday in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha community, in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, where a boat carrying scores of people capsized, resulting in loss of lives.

The deceased were said to be mourners travelling to attend a funeral in the community where the incident happened.

The president, in a release issued on Saturday by his Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, stated inter alia that: “Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation.

“I have also directed that our Presidential Campaign Rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, this Saturday, November 21, 2026, be observed without much fanfare in honour of the lives lost and in sympathy with the relatives and families of those involved in the disaster.

“On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State.

“I particularly mourn with Governor Duoye Diri over this sad incident.

“I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families.”

World.title: Babcock Matriculates 4,860, Records Highest Postgraduate Enrolment
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Funmi Ogundare

President/Vice-Chancellor of Babcock University, Ilishan-Remo, Ogun state, Prof. Afolarin Ojewole, weekend advised newly admitted students of the institution to embrace discipline, academic integrity and responsibility, saying that success is intentional and requires diligence, focus and commitment.

Ojewole made this known at the institution’s 28th undergraduate and 17th postgraduate matriculation ceremon, where a total of 4,860 students were formally admitted into various academic programmes.

The figure comprised 3,380 undergraduate and 1,480 postgraduate students, with the latter representing the highest postgraduate enrolment in the university’s history.

Addressing the students, Ojewole urged them to approach their academic pursuits with determination, intellectual curiosity and a strong sense of purpose, stressing that admission into the university marked the beginning of a journey of growth, discovery and transformation.

He particularly challenged postgraduate students to undertake research that would advance the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) while providing practical solutions to real-life challenges.

“Success is intentional. It requires discipline, diligence and reliance on God,” he said.

The VC said the university remained committed to extending the frontiers of knowledge, nurturing responsible leadership and contributing to national development by producing graduates who are globally relevant, research-focused, competent and entrepreneurial.

He reminded undergraduates that gaining admission into Babcock goes beyond securing a place in an academic institution, noting that they had become part of a community committed to preparing individuals for service to God and humanity.

He urged them to develop intellectual curiosity by asking questions, reading beyond lecture notes and making effective use of the university’s academic resources, particularly its library.

He also warned against examination malpractice, manipulation, peer pressure and other forms of misconduct capable of undermining their academic and personal development.

“Above all, guard your character. Babcock is not just interested in producing graduates with degrees; we are committed to shaping citizens with character,” he said.

The VC further encouraged the students to prioritise their physical, emotional and mental well-being, assuring them of access to support through the university’s pastors, chaplains, faculty members, academic advisers, counsellors and student support centre.

He said the institution’s philosophy of education transcended the acquisition of certificates, emphasising the development of the whole person.

Welcoming international students, Ojewole described their presence as an important contribution to the university’s multicultural environment and global outlook, assuring them of opportunities to acquire knowledge, develop sound values and make positive contributions to their home countries.

He also emphasised the university’s modern laboratories, digital learning resources, recreational facilities, globally recognised faculty, mentorship programmes and opportunities for spiritual growth and community engagement.

The ceremony also celebrated outstanding academic performances among the newly admitted undergraduates.

Ayobami Adeoti emerged as the candidate with the highest Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) score, recording 359 points, while John Dada emerged as the highest-performing Joint Universities Preliminary Examinations Board (JUPEB) candidate with a perfect 16-point score.

Both students received presidential handshakes and were scheduled to receive awards and prizes from the university.

The ceremony also attracted the wife of the Special Assistant to the Ogun State Governor on Education, Hon. Daniel Idowu, among the newly admitted postgraduate students.

Ojewole expressed optimism that the matriculating students would graduate as academically accomplished, morally upright, professionally competent and socially responsible individuals capable of providing solutions to societal challenges.

“Our goal is not simply to produce graduates. We are committed to raising men and women of character, competence and purpose who will provide solutions to society’s challenges and positively impact their communities, nation and the world,”

World.title: WealthBridge Group Appoints Olawoyin, Tijani, Others to Subsidiary Boards, Charts Next Frontier of Growth
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

In a strategic move to strengthen corporate governance, deepen institutional expertise and advance the Group’s growth ambitions, WealthBridge Financial Services Holdings Limited has announced the appointment of four directors to the boards of two of its subsidiaries: WealthBridge Capital Partners Limited and WealthBridge Asset Management Limited.

WealthBridge Capital Partners, the Group’s investment banking and financial advisory subsidiary, has appointed Professor Adewale Adedamola Olawoyin, Mr. Adetoye Toriola and Mrs. Tairat Tijani as Non-Executive Directors.

Mrs. Tijani and Dr. Ganiyat Taiwo Olusesi have also been appointed Independent Non-Executive Directors to the Board of WealthBridge Asset Management Limited.

These appointments underscore the Group’s deliberate commitment to strengthening corporate governance and aligning institutional expertise with its strategic growth objectives.

Together, the appointments bring to the Group significant experience across corporate governance, law, investment banking, capital markets, corporate finance, financial management, strategic planning, risk oversight, regulatory affairs and business transformation, reinforcing the Group’s commitment to building institutions anchored on sound oversight, accountability and stakeholder confidence.

WealthBridge Capital Partners Limited — Board Appointments

Prof. Olawoyin brings more than three decades of experience in law, corporate governance, commercial transactions and banking-related matters.

A Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) and an academic at the University of Lagos, Olawoyin specialises in Shipping and Admiralty Law, Company Law, Commercial Transactions, Banking and Negotiable Instruments.

He has also been actively involved in corporate and institutional governance, as well as international commercial transactions.

Mrs. Tijani brings over 22 years of experience in the Nigerian investment banking and corporate finance sector, including service on the boards and board committees of institutions regulated by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX).

An active market operator, she has participated in several landmark transactions that contributed to the development of the Nigerian capital market.

Her expertise spans investment banking, capital markets regulation, financial planning, risk management, corporate finance, asset management and governance.

She is currently Head of Corporate Finance and Treasury at Rite Foods Limited, having previously served as Head of the Capital Markets Division at FBN Capital, where she oversaw deal origination and execution.

She is a director of Sterling Bank Plc and a former Board member of Central Securities Clearing System (CSCS) Plc. She holds an MBA with Distinction in International Business from the University of Birmingham and an honours degree in Accounting, Finance and Economics from Lancaster University.

She is a Fellow of the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (FCCA) and a member of the Institute of Chartered Secretaries and Administrators of Nigeria (ICSAN).

Mr. Toriola brings more than 20 years of executive experience across the FMCG, manufacturing and financial services sectors.

He has held senior roles with leading organisations, including Godrej Consumer Products West Africa, Unilever West Africa, Guinness Nigeria, British American Tobacco and First Bank of Nigeria.

His experience spans strategic planning, financial stewardship, performance management, audit and risk oversight, capital raising and operational transformation. He is a Fellow of the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) and the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN), and holds an MSc in Professional Accountancy from the University of London.

WealthBridge Asset Management Limited — Board Appointments

WealthBridge Asset Management Limited’s Board is further strengthened by the appointment of Mrs. Tijani as an Independent Non-Executive Director, whose profile is outlined above.

Dr. Olusesi is a Chartered Secretary and Administrator, legal practitioner and management professional with extensive experience in corporate governance, legal administration, institutional leadership and policy development.

She holds a first degree and a Master’s degree in Law from Olabisi Onabanjo University, as well as a PhD in Corporate Governance from Lead City University, Ibadan. She also holds an MBA from the European Institute of Management and Administration and is an alumna of the Policy, Strategy and Leadership Course 53 of the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies (NIPSS), Kuru, Jos.

Olusesi is a member of the Nigerian Institute of Management, where she currently serves as Registrar/Chief Executive. She is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Secretaries and Administrators of Nigeria (ICSAN) and belongs to several professional bodies, including the Nigerian Bar Association, International Federation of Women Lawyers, Chartered Institute of Taxation of Nigeria and Chartered Institute of Directors Nigeria.

She is also associated with the Nigeria-Britain Association and Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ). Her professional experience includes serving as an External Examiner with the Council for Legal Education, Nigerian Law School, between 2016 and 2019, and as a Faculty Member of the Encouragement Initiative Academy for NGO Training and Sustainable Development Goals, where she teaches the Legal Framework of Running Not-for-Profit Organisations.

The appointments come at an important stage in the Group’s evolution and align with its recently concluded three-year strategy session, themed ‘Charting the Next Frontier of Growth,’ held in Lagos.

The session brought together key leadership and stakeholders to assess emerging market opportunities, review the Group’s growth trajectory and establish strategic priorities for its next phase of development, focused on sustainable growth, business transformation, innovation, operational efficiency and enhanced value creation across the Group.

For WealthBridge Capital Partners, the strategy provides a clear roadmap for sharpening its competitive positioning, expanding its investment banking and financial advisory capabilities, pursuing new opportunities and deepening institutional relationships.

For WealthBridge Asset Management, the appointments form part of a broader institutional development agenda that places strong emphasis on corporate governance, accountability, effective risk oversight and the continuous strengthening of management and operational capabilities.

Commenting on the appointments, the Group Chief Executive Officer of WealthBridge Financial Services Holdings Limited, Ahmed Adekunle Lawal, said: “The appointments of Professor Olawoyin, Mr. Toriola, Mrs. Tijani and Dr. Olusesi to the Boards of our subsidiaries reflect our deliberate commitment to building strong institutions positioned for long-term relevance and sustainable growth.

“Their combined experience, expertise and depth of knowledge will strengthen our governance, strategic direction and capacity to create greater value for our clients and stakeholders.

“As we continue to advance our growth ambitions, we recognise that strong institutions are built on the quality of their leadership, the strength of their governance structures and the expertise guiding their decisions. We are confident that their contributions will further strengthen WealthBridge Capital Partners and WealthBridge Asset Management and create lasting value for our clients and stakeholders.”

He added that the repositioning of the Group’s subsidiaries extends beyond strengthening governance structures, describing it as part of a deliberate effort to build stronger platforms for growth, innovation and excellence across the Group.
