With strengthened Board leadership and a clear strategic direction, WealthBridge Capital Partners and WealthBridge Asset Management are focused on deepening their respective roles in Nigeria’s financial ecosystem and pursuing opportunities that support businesses, institutions and investors in creating and preserving long-term value.

World.title: AFASU Golden Awards 2026 Honour IHG Leaders
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Charles Ajunwa

In a ceremony attended by members of the Afro-Asian Union for Development, Tourism and Technology (AFASU), two prominent leaders of IHG Hotels and Resorts, Nasser Fadly and Maarten P. Drenth, were recognised

on the sidelines of the graduation celebration of 500 participants from the InterContinental Hotels Academy in Egypt.

The recognition which took place at the Al-Saraya Hall InterContinental Citystars Cairo,

formed part of the AFASU Golden Awards 2026, celebrating outstanding leadership, meaningful contributions to the hospitality industry, youth empowerment, human capital development, and the advancement of professional excellence across the hotel sector.

A key highlight of the ceremony was the presentation of an exclusive recorded message by H.E. Alain St.Ange, former Minister of Tourism and International Ambassador, and President of the AFASU Awards Sector, who also serves as the Chairman of the International Jury of the AFASU Golden Awards.

In his address, St.Ange presented the official justifications behind the two awards, explaining the professional, institutional, and impact-based criteria adopted by the International Jury in selecting the recipients.

His message emphasised that the AFASU Golden Awards are not merely recognitions of professional positions or prestigious titles, but rather an acknowledgment of genuine achievements, effective leadership, measurable contributions, and the positive impact individuals create within their industries and communities.

He highlighted the importance of recognising leaders who contribute to the sustainable development of tourism and hospitality, particularly those who invest in people, empower young professionals, and help shape the future of the industry.

His message represented a central moment of the ceremony, reflecting the credibility, international vision, and professional standards upon which the AFASU Golden Awards are founded.

Following the presentation of St.Ange’s message, Dr. Hossam Darwish, President of the Afro-Asian Union (AFASU), delivered an address welcoming the distinguished guests and congratulating the award recipients.

Dr. Darwish emphasised that AFASU’s philosophy in granting its international awards is based on recognising genuine achievement and positive impact rather than titles or positions alone.

He stressed that investing in people, developing human capabilities, and empowering young generations are fundamental pillars for the future of the global tourism and hospitality industry.

He also praised the contributions of both award recipients to strengthening hospitality operations, developing human resources, and promoting a culture of professionalism and institutional excellence.

Regional General Manager, IHG Egypt & Africa,

Maarten P. Drenth, was honoured in recognition of his outstanding leadership and contributions to the development of the hospitality sector, strengthening professional standards, and promoting excellence across IHG’s operations in Egypt and Africa.

Recipient of the Youth Hospitality Empowerment Leadership Award, Nasser Fadly, was recognised for his significant role in youth empowerment and human capital development within the hospitality industry, reflecting the importance of investing in emerging talent and preparing the next generation of professionals to lead the future of the hotel sector.

At the conclusion of the ceremony, Darwish personally presented the recipients with the prestigious AFASU Golden Awards trophies and official certificates of recognition.

The presentation took place in an atmosphere of appreciation and celebration, followed by commemorative photographs with AFASU members, IHG executives, and distinguished guests.

This distinguished recognition reflects AFASU’s ongoing international mission to support influential leaders, celebrate professional achievements, promote youth empowerment, and strengthen cooperation among international institutions operating in tourism and hospitality.

Through the AFASU Golden Awards, the Union continues to affirm its belief that developing people, empowering young talent, and recognising leaders who create meaningful impact are essential to building a more competitive, innovative, and sustainable future for the global tourism and hospitality industry.

World.title: DStv to broadcast Rassie watch-along party – Here’s how…
World.content:
SuperSport has announced that it will broadcast Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus’s watch-along party for South Africa vs Ireland on DStv Stream and its YouTube channel.

The Boks boss will stream his commentary about the match amid his World Rugby sanction, which has barred him from any match-day involvement with the national team.

The match kicks off on SuperSport Rugby at 18:30. Ten minutes earlier, viewers will be able to



SUPERSPORT TO BROADCAST RASSIE SPRINGBOK WATCH-ALONG PARTY

On Saturday, 21 November – just hours before kick-off – SuperSport announced that it would be broadcasting the Rassie Erasmus watch-along party on DStv Stream channel 245, exclusive to the platform.

It will also be broadcast on SuperSport’s official YouTube channel.

The streaming video of Rassie’s commentary of the Springboks match against Ireland will also be available on the Springbok coach’s YouTube channel.

The Springboks coach will be watching the game from his hotel, not the stadium, as per his World Rugby sanction.

According to a sign-up page, over 150 000 rugby fans from 89 countries around the world will be joining Rassie’s watch-along party.

SuperSport shared: “Erasmus will watch as a supporter. In line with the terms of his suspension, he will have no contact with players or team management during the match”



Banned from the box. Open on YouTube.



Watch along with Rassie tonight at 18:30 on SuperSport's YouTube page and channel 245 on DStv Stream 🏉#WatchWithRassieOnSS | #SSRugby pic.twitter.com/kWmEReWJfc — SuperSport Rugby (@SSRugby) November 21, 2026

TWO DEVICES REQUIRED

As it is a commentary video, not a broadcast of the Springbok game, rugby fans will need to have two screens running – one for the live match and another for Rassie’s stream. This means that viewers will need a TV and another device, like a laptop or smartphone, to watch both videos, or a smart TV that supports split viewing.

Rassie has shared that his video will intentionally lag by 10 to 30 seconds behind the live match broadcast. This is likely due to copyright protection and also adhering to the rules of his suspension.

Fans will also be able to post messages – which will be carefully moderated – showing their support for the Springboks or Rassie himself, which he will be able to read.

EVERYBODY GETS PREMIUM!

DStv’s support of Rassie’s watch-along video comes shortly after it announced that it would also make the Premium package available to all subscribers through its Open Time promotion, which runs from 25 November to 25 December.

This means that irrespective of package, subscribers will have access to every live channel at no extra cost.

World.title: How Scottland FC surrendered the Zimbabwe PSL title to newcomers
World.content:
Scottland FC’s hopes of retaining the Zimbabwe Premier Soccer League title ended on Saturday despite beating Triangle United 2-1 in their final match of the season.

The defending champions finished two points behind newly crowned champions Hardrock FC, who secured their maiden top-flight title after defeating FC Platinum 1-0 at Chahwanda Stadium.

Scottland went into the final round with 68 points, while Hardrock occupied top spot with 70.



The Kwekwe-based newcomers needed victory to guarantee the championship, regardless of what happened in the other match.

How Scottland’s title defence unravelled

Scottland’s campaign had already experienced setbacks, particularly on the continental stage.

The Mabvuku-based club’s CAF Champions League adventure ended in disappointment after they were eliminated by Angola’s Petro de Luanda in October.



Scottland had taken a 2-0 advantage into the second leg of their second preliminary-round encounter, with former Kaizer Chiefs players Khama Billiat and Knowledge Musona scoring in the first-leg victory at the National Sports Stadium.

However, Petro overturned the deficit with a 3-0 victory in Angola, advancing 3-2 on aggregate and ending Scottland’s hopes of reaching the group stages.

The club subsequently experienced changes in its technical department, with Peter Ndlovu taking over from Norman Mapeza on an interim basis.



Ndlovu collected seven points from his first three league matches, keeping Scottland in contention for the championship.

The defending champions also received important contributions from Billiat and Musona during their title chase. Both players featured in Scottland’s emphatic 4-0 victory over Herentals in the penultimate round, alongside Kwakhe Thwala and Kingsley Mureremba.

Billiat, who scored 12 league goals during the campaign, was, however, unavailable for the decisive encounter against Triangle after a family emergency.



Although Scottland secured a 2-1 victory, Hardrock’s result meant their efforts were not enough to retain the championship.

Who are Zimbabwe’s new champions, Hardrock FC?

Hardrock FC are a Kwekwe-based football club that secured promotion to the Premier Soccer League after winning the 2025 Central Region Division One championship.

The 2026 campaign was their debut season in Zimbabwe’s top-flight competition.



Under coach Kelvin Kaindu, the newcomers established themselves as serious title contenders, eventually finishing above established Premiership sides.

Hardrock play their home matches at Chahwanda Stadium and have now achieved a remarkable milestone by winning the league in their first season.

Their triumph makes them the third club to win Zimbabwe’s top-flight championship in their debut season, following Black Rhinos in 1984 and Scottland in 2025.



Hardrock’s achievement also brings an end to Scottland’s reign as Zimbabwean champions after just one season.

World.title: Brave or selfish? Viewers divided over Buzza’s mother on ‘Stars and Vows’
World.content:
Viewers of the much-anticipated wedding special Stars and Vows: Anele & Buzza were deeply divided after learning that Buzza’s mother, Mam’ Vuyi, and her children had spent 30 years navigating a strained relationship.

THE MGUDLWA FAMILY DRAMA

Stars and Vows is a four-part wedding docuseries that follows the wedding journey of seasoned broadcaster Anele Mgudlwa and her husband, Bonelela “Buzza” Mgudlwa, an attorney and prince whose father is Chief Mongezi Mgudlwa in the Eastern Cape.

The Netflix special debuted on 13 November 2026, and many parts of the story evoked mixed reactions from social media users.



The dynamics within the Mgudlwa family stood out to many viewers, especially after Buzza revealed that his parents divorced when he was 12.

Buzza explained that in his royal family, when a couple divorces, the children remain in the royal court, meaning his mother had to leave her children behind.

Despite Mam’ Vuyi’s attempts to reach out throughout the years, especially to her daughter Nangamso, the relationship remained strained.

Therefore, it was only natural for Buzza to wrestle with the idea of inviting his mother to his wedding, given that she had been barred from attending royal family events in the last 30 years.

‘SHE’S SO BRAVE’

Many viewers truly empathised with Buzza’s mother and respected her decision to leave an unfulfilling marriage, especially since she had married into royalty.

Hummingbird@TshegiMore: I’m so fascinated by Buzza’s mother. I feel like she’s so brave and has such an interesting lore. For her to sacrifice everything and brazenly choose freedom, something she’s been shunned for, I wish I could know more about her and what happened.



@Malaikadiva: Buzza’s mother is so beautiful, and I think she was a woman ahead of her time, who chose to leave when that wasn’t done. There’s something that happened that she’s not saying [it] to keep the peace. Whatever the story is, I just know I’m on her side.

Danilo@odedanilo: Buzza’s mom. Oh, they can never make me hate her.

@NalediMOfficial: Her absence may have hurt her kids, but part of it feels like she was kept away from them. Also – let’s pay attention to how Anele also vouches for Buzza’s mom, indicating that her departure wasn’t entirely her fault.

‘SHE’S A HORRIBLE HUMAN BEING’

Another group of viewers held no punches towards Buzza’s mother, arguing that she should have fought harder to remain in her children’s lives.

Her absence also sparked a broader debate about society’s double standards between mothers and fathers who neglect or abandon their children.

Many stated that if a man had been in the same situation, people would have been labelled a deadbeat father.

𝑺𝒖𝒏𝒔𝒉𝒊𝒏𝒆@_Thandiwe: Can we not forget that Buzza’s mom is a deadbeat? Thanks.

Helen of Troy@manzimalanga: Buzza’s mother ain’t sh*t. You guys are calling a woman who is still actively abandoning her kids a queen? She’s a horrible human being.

@_BafanaMthembu: You guys don’t hate deadbeats; you hate deadbeat fathers. The praise Buzza’s mom is getting for abandoning her kids for 30 years is crazy. Had it been a man, we’d be dragging him to hell and back.

@JayAsie: You can’t tell me you can’t see your kids because of their dad, I feel like she didn’t fight enough. There are emails now; there’s social media where she can reach out. Or even ask abantu abadala [elders] be family to intervene.

World.title: Sundowns coach Miguel Cardoso pleads with Chiefs to ‘keep it clean’
World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns head coach Miguel Cardoso hopes for a clean match when his side hosts Kaizer Chiefs in the semi-final of the Carling Knockout Cup clash.

The two giants of South African football face each other this Sunday afternoon at the Loftus Versfeld.

Last season, Downs defender Keanu Cupido was injured during a match against Chiefs following a dangerous tackle from Sphesihle Ndlovu.



The 28-year-old defender has been out since then.

“Yeah, I hope I don’t lose Keanu [Cupido] or a player like Keanu for a year because, from the last match, a very brutal action of a player from Kaizer Chiefs,” said Cardoso.

“We got a player who still cannot play. He’s severely injured and at risk of his career, and that should be stated here,” Cardoso added.

Cardoso wants a fair match between Sundowns and Chiefs

Masandawana and Amakhosi met this season aleady, with the match ending 1-1 back in August,

“So I just hope that everything that goes beyond playing a normal game, like the one we played in the championship, was a beautiful match,” Cardoso said.

Sundowns are facing a hard period going into Sunday’s match. The Brazilians got knocked out of the CAF Champions League before they lost 3-1 in the CAF Super Cup.



The Carling knockout is their last hope of salvaging something before the year ends. Two domestic trophies within three months will wipe their tears and encourage Cardoso to inspire Sundowns to another league title.

World.title: Richards Bay FC announce new head coach
World.content:
Richards Bay confirmed Dladla has put pen to payer on a one-season contract. The 48-year-old replaces the Bulgarian coach Dimitar Pantev.

The club known as The Natal Rich Boyz announced the appointment in an official statement on Saturday, 21 November 2026.

SIMO DLADLA RETURNS TO RICHARDS BAY FC

“Richards Bay Football Club is pleased to announce the appointment of Simo Dladla as the Head Coach. He has signed for One (1) season with an option to renew,” the club announced.



Dladla previously coached Richards Bay in the National First Division (NFD), where he guided the club to a promotion play-off position.

Richards Bay also appreciated his experience at Young Africans SC in Tanzania, where he was an assistant to his countryman Manqoba Mngqithi.

Dladla joined Yanga as an assistant coach before taking temporary charge following Mngqithi’s departure in October.



He recorded two victories in his two matches as caretaker coach, beating Mashujaa FC 2-1 on 27 October before securing a 4-0 victory against Kagera Sugar on 1 November.

However, Young Africans subsequently appointed Fadlu Davids as their new head coach, with Dladla agreeing to leave the club.

Richards Bay also confirmed that the returning coach holds a CAF A coaching licence.



“The 48 year old holds a CAF A License. The Club is delighted to welcome the Coach to Richards Bay Football Club and wishes him all the best,” the statement added.

RELEGATION FIGHT AWAITS DLADLA

Dladla takes charge of a Richards Bay side that has collected just three points from its opening nine Betway Premiership matches.

The club has recorded three draws and six defeats, leaving them at the bottom of the league standings without a victory in the 2026/27 campaign.



His appointment follows the departure of Pantev, whose tenure lasted only three matches. The Bulgarian suffered defeats against Mamelodi Sundowns, Sekhukhune United and Kruger United.

Dladla becomes Richards Bay’s third head coach this season after the club also parted ways with Ronnie Gabriel in September.

His first assignment is scheduled for 29 November, when Richards Bay travel to face Marumo Gallants.



The coach will have 21 league matches remaining to improve the club’s position and secure its Betway Premiership status.

World.title: UK's Princess Catherine explores life after cancer in 'personal documentary'
World.content:
Prince William's wife Catherine will explore life beyond a cancer diagnosis in a personal documentary, almost two years after she revealed she was in remission, her office said on Saturday.

The British future queen, 44, also known as Kate, announced in March 2024 she had been diagnosed with an unspecified cancer and was undergoing chemotherapy.

"Heal", described as a "deeply personal" documentary, will be broadcast by the BBC on November 29, the princess's Kensington Palace office said in a statement.

It will air internationally via NBCUniversal in the United States on November 30, Channel 9 in Australia on December 1 and CTV and Noovo in Canada on December 7, it added.

Catherine, whose formal title is Princess of Wales, has three children aged between eight and 13 with heir to the throne William.

She revealed she was in remission in January 2025.

The documentary "follows the princess on a personal journey through some of Britain's most spectacular landscapes" as she takes part in one of the UK's best-known endurance events, the Three Peaks Challenge, the statement said.

Participants in the challenge, which Catherine completed in June, climb the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours.

"Set against the backdrop of the challenge itself, the princess reflects on her own experience alongside individuals navigating their own health journeys," the statement said.

"Together they explore the profound impact serious illness can have on the whole person and the people, places and experiences that can help us heal," it added.

Catherine's father-in-law, King Charles III, was also diagnosed with cancer, which was revealed by Buckingham Palace on February 5, 2024.

Charles, 78, has returned to public duties but is still being treated for an undisclosed cancer.

All funds generated by the documentary's distribution will go to Britain's Royal Marsden Cancer Charity.

World.title: Diallo present as African football boss Motsepe reiterates support for Infantino
World.content:
African football supremo Patrice Motsepe said Saturday that all 54 members of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) support Gianni Infantino's bid for re-election as FIFA president.

Motsepe made the declaration in Abuja, where CAF is holding its ordinary general assembly and at which one of Infantino's two rivals, French football chief Philippe Diallo is present.

former Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima is the other candidate.

The trio will learn whether they have been successful on March 18 next year in Rabat -- the winning candidate must obtain a majority of the 211 associations.

CAF has been consistently behind Infantino -- who is seeking a fourth and final term -- even after the furore he stirred up in July with his shortlived FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Morocco is co-hosting the 2030 World Cup.

"Gianni, you have our support on behalf of the 54 nations in Africa to be our candidate," Motsepe said.

"I have a report from all 54 member associations in Africa to say that we are unanimously supporting Gianni."

Infantino has faced multiple calls to step down and lost the backing of European football's governing body UEFA, whilst CONCACAF has also been strident in its criticism of the 56-year-old Swiss lawyer.

Motsepe though has been a vocal supporter and Infantino said such loyalty was reciprocal.

"You will always find, in me and in FIFA, a trusted partner," Infantino told the assembly, announcing cash inflow of $25 million to each member of CAF, starting January 2027 for development projects.

On Wednesday, UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister told AFP that Diallo, a 63-year-old lawyer whose Senegalese-born father boxed for France at the 1960 Olympics in Rome, should not be seen as solely a European candidate.

"He is a francophone, which is an important asset in lots of CAF countries," she said.

McAllister, who in 2023 became the first woman to be elected a vice-president of UEFA, noted though that confederations do not vote as a bloc.

"There is a soft space which Philippe can exploit and convince some federations within each confederation to support a reform agenda," the 61-year-old said.

"There is a lot of discomfort around the behaviour of Gianni Infantino and a desire to challenge the concentration of power in his hands.

"This applies everywhere in world football. This is not about Europe, the same rules apply globally."

World.title: Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka to be laid to rest in eXesi
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka will be laid to rest in eXesi in the Eastern Cape on Saturday 28 November.

She passed away on Friday after complications from a medical procedure.

Mlambo-Ngcuka has been granted a State Funeral and her memorial service will be on Tuesday at the Our Lady of Lourdes Catholic Church in Rivonia, Johannesburg.

World.title: Finland detects drone attack on Russian cargo ship in Baltic
World.content:
Finland's military detected a drone attack on Saturday morning on a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea which caused the vessel to catch fire, the Nordic country's authorities said.

The Finnish defence ministry did not specify who was behind the drone strike, but Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said in a message on X: "War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity... Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor."

Fighting off a Russian invasion now in its fifth year, Ukraine has stepped up its long-range barrages against Russia far beyond the front lines.

"On Saturday morning, the Finnish Defence Forces detected a drone attack against a Russian cargo vessel west of Suursaari, in the eastern Gulf of Finland, in international waters," the ministry said in a statement.

According to Finnish border guards dispatched to the scene the ship caught fire and began drifting towards Finnish waters after the strike.

"The situation currently poses no danger to other vessels," the border service said in a press release.

Authorities gave no immediate details of the boat's crew.

Finland immediately informed NATO of the strike, the defence ministry said.

It said temporary restrictions were enforced in the airspace and maritime area of the eastern part of the Gulf.

The Baltic Sea has become a potential flashpoint in the wake of Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, with Western countries accusing Moscow of conducting a "hybrid war" in the strategic waterway.

Lying at the easternmost end of the Baltic along the coasts of Finland, Estonia and Russia, the Gulf of Finland is a key maritime passage for Russia, leading to the former capital, Saint Petersburg.

World.title: 'I'll be back': vows Kane after ankle surgery
World.content:
Bayern Munich's star striker Harry Kane pledged to return and help his injury-ravaged side for the "business end of the season" after undergoing surgery on his left ankle on Saturday.

Kane limped off after 20 minutes of Bayern's 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday, the club confirming the England captain had torn a ligament in his ankle.

Bayern issued a statement Saturday saying the Ballon d'Or winner had "successfully undergone surgery" on his left ankle.

"The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program," Bayern said, with the injury expected to keep Kane out for three to four months.

Kane posted a picture on social media from his hospital bed on Saturday, vowing to work his way back to fitness this season.

"The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027.

"I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season."

Kane shared a quote from three-time Super Bowl-winning wide receiver Julian Edelman: "tough times don't last, tough people do", while thanking his supporters for their messages of support.

Kane has a history of ankle issues although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023.

England coach Thomas Tuchel will be keeping a keen eye out on how England's most capped player's rehabilitation progresses.

England play Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in late March.

- Bayern's casualty ward -

The injury comes at a difficult time for Bayern, who are currently missing several players, particularly up front.

Bayern have been without Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer in recent weeks.

On Friday, Michael Olise -- one of Bayern's few remaining forwards -- went down after a tackle late in the first-half.

Despite continuing until the break, the France star did not return for the second-half.

World.title: Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka granted State Funeral
World.content:
Her official funeral will take place at the family home in eXesi in the Eastern Cape.

Mlambo-Ngcuka was, at the time of her death, Chancellor at the University of Johannesburg since 2022.

She served as deputy president under former president Thabo Mbeki from 2005 to 2007. She also served as Minister of Minerals and Energy from 1999 until 2005.

She also served deputy minister of trade and industry from 1996 until 1999.

Mlambo-Ngcuka is survived by her husband Bulelani Ngcuka and her five children.

Ramaphosa, who is currently in the US says he is looking forward to offering his condolences to the family upon his return.

World.title: Greek PM under fire over Grand Theft Auto post
World.content:
Greece's prime minister has come under fire for asking youngsters whether they'd like the mature-content Grand Theft Auto VI videogame for Christmas.

"Which of you will ask for Grand Theft Auto VI as a Christmas present from grandad and grandma?" Kyriakos Mitsotakis said in a TikTok post on Friday, with the game's logo briefly flashing on-screen.

"We all know that grandfathers and grandmothers rarely say no to their grandchildren," he added.

The post was designed to promote a 400-euro ($439) pension bonus from Mitsotakis' government, as it faces elections next year.

But it came under attack from critics calling it inappropriate to encourage minors to buy a mature game.

"The prime minister 'promotes' a video game that is banned for minors just to follow the trend," the main opposition socialist Pasok party said.

Leftist daily Efsyn called the move a "gaffe" while conservative newspaper Dimokratia said it was a "tragic" error.

Ironically, Mitsotakis' government has joined a growing number of countries imposing curbs on young people's use of social media.

World.title: Ruto defends IEBC, challenges rivals to present alternative policies
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [PCS]

President William Ruto has launched a scathing attack on opposition leaders over their demands on the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), accusing them of attempting to interfere with the electoral agency because they fear losing the 2027 General Election.

The President challenged opposition leaders to allow IEBC to prepare independently for next year's elections, saying they should instead focus on identifying their presidential candidate, developing a manifesto and presenting alternative policies to Kenyans.

Ruto accused his competitors of attempting to play the roles of both contestants and referees by seeking to influence decisions on the procurement of election materials and equipment.

He spoke a day after opposition leaders walked out of a meeting convened by IEBC, alleging bias by the commission.

“Please give IEBC a chance to arrange the elections next year. The people of Kenya will decide. You go and first look for your candidate, find your policies, agenda and plans and sell them to the wananchi. We shall meet at the ballot,” said Ruto.

Speaking during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto questioned why opposition politicians were concentrating on determining how IEBC should procure election materials instead of preparing to face voters.

“How can somebody who is in a competition want to decide where the pitch will be, who the referee will be and where the ball will be placed? Leave IEBC alone. Those who will vote are the citizens, and they are the ones who will decide,” he said.

The President accused his opponents of lacking a clear political agenda and capacity to deliver, claiming their campaigns were centred on slogans and personal attacks against him.

He challenged them to explain what they would do differently in agriculture, education, healthcare, infrastructure and employment rather than mobilising Kenyans around the slogan 'Kasongo Must Go'.

“The reason why my competitors cannot develop a plan is that they have no capacity. The reason why they have no agenda is that they have no knowledge. The reason why they cannot develop anything is that they know they have no capacity to deliver on anything that they will say,” he said.

His remarks were echoed by Kakamega Governor Fernandes Barasa and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, who rallied Western Kenya leaders behind his re-election bid and defended IEBC against what they termed unnecessary political pressure. President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [ Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Speaking in Butere, Barasa said the region's political leadership, including Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, Cabinet Secretary Wycliffe Oparanya, Wetang'ula and trade unionist Francis Atwoli, was united behind Ruto's development agenda.

“IEBC will conduct the elections according to the law. Opposition leaders should leave IEBC alone and allow it to do its work,” he said.

Wetang'ula maintained that IEBC was independent of both the government and the opposition and should be allowed to conduct its work without interference.

“IEBC is independent of the government and independent of the Opposition. You stand there to do your work fairly, truthfully and equally,” he said.

He added: “Just as Arsenal supporters cannot dictate what uniform the referee should wear, the referee's responsibility is to ensure the game is played fairly and the winner emerges through a legitimate process.”

The exchanges underline the growing political contest over the management of the 2027 elections, with the government side accusing the opposition of undermining the electoral agency before campaigns gather momentum.

Beyond the political exchanges, Ruto used his Western Kenya tour to highlight development projects, saying his administration was committed to correcting years of neglect and unequal distribution of national resources.

He also announced plans for a second phase of the Nyota programme targeting an additional 200,000 young people, each expected to receive Sh50,000 to establish or expand businesses.

The government is also targeting 100,000 college graduates for internships from January, with each expected to receive a monthly stipend of Sh20,000.

Ruto's tour comes amid growing competition for Western Kenya's support ahead of the 2027 General Election, with emerging opposition alliances seeking to challenge his influence.

World.title: Ruto sustains attacks on Gachagua, dares Opposition to name 2027 flagbearer
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto launches Matisi-Bokoli-Milani-Teremi road in Webuye West on November 19, 2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

President William Ruto has challenged Opposition leaders to name their presidential candidate and unveil a clear political agenda, accusing them of wasting time hopping from one hotel to another and holding meetings in private residences in search of a flagbearer and campaign manifesto.

The President said the Opposition was yet to settle on a flagbearer or agree on a common agenda despite the clock ticking towards the 2027 General Election.

He dismissed the rival camps' political engagements as endless consultations and manoeuvres, arguing that their leaders were more preoccupied with political meetings than developing policies to convince Kenyans.

Speaking in Bungoma during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto challenged his opponents to stop what he termed political confusion and present an alternative development agenda, insisting he was ready to face them in the 2027 contest.

"These people do not have a candidate. They are struggling, moving from one hotel to another and from one person's house to another, trying to find an agenda and a manifesto before they can start campaigning. Time is running out, yet they are still struggling to agree on an agenda," he said.

Ruto also launched a fresh attack on former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua, accusing him of promoting tribalism and hatred while questioning his remarks about relocating to Texas, United States.

The President mockingly referred to Gachagua as "Mr Chuki wa Texas", questioning why he would allegedly acquire a house in the US while engaging in politics that could divide Kenyans and fuel hostility.

"Mr Chuki wa Texas has gone to buy a house in Texas. He wants to know whether he will flee our country after spreading tribalism and hatred, dividing people and turning them against each other, before boarding a plane to Texas and leaving others to deal with the consequences," Ruto said.

He accused the former Deputy President of attempting to turn communities against one another for political gain, warning that he would not allow anyone to undermine national unity through ethnic mobilisation.

Ruto said he was ready to confront his political opponents directly but insisted that political competition should not become an avenue for spreading hatred and inciting Kenyans against one another.

The President also questioned Gachagua's allies over their reported visit to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) offices in Kizirani, accusing the Opposition of picking unnecessary fights with the electoral agency ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He suggested that politicians who begin questioning the electoral commission before elections could be preparing grounds to reject the results should they lose.

"Whenever you see someone picking a fight with IEBC, that person is already looking for an excuse to fail. Now they are coming up with all sorts of excuses, asking whether it is IEBC that votes. Is IEBC responsible for the votes?" He posed.

Ruto urged politicians to stop harassing the electoral agency, maintaining that the power to elect leaders rests with Kenyans and not the commission.

"I want to tell Kenyans to stop harassing IEBC. IEBC does not have votes. The votes belong to the people of Kenya," he said.

The President maintained that his administration was focused on delivering development, challenging the Opposition to explain its alternative plans on electricity connectivity, education, healthcare and infrastructure.

He questioned what the Opposition considered its development agenda, dismissing what he described as recycled political slogans and simplistic promises.

The President particularly took issue with promises centred on providing porridge to Kenyans, questioning whether such pledges could constitute a credible national development agenda.

He urged voters to interrogate the policies and development track records of politicians seeking their support instead of being swayed by political rhetoric and personal attacks.

The latest attack marks an escalation in political exchanges between Ruto and his rivals as competing camps intensify mobilisation ahead of the 2027 General Election.

It also comes amid efforts by Gachagua and other Opposition figures to consolidate their political formations and build a formidable challenge to Ruto's re-election bid, with Western Kenya emerging as a key battleground.

World.title: Ruto lists measures to lower cost of living, put more money in Kenyans' pockets
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his State Of The Nation Address at Parliament, Nairobi. November 18th, 2026. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

President William Ruto has outlined a raft of government interventions aimed at reducing the cost of living, increasing household incomes and creating more employment opportunities for Kenyans.

Addressing Parliament during the 2026 State of the Nation Address on Wednesday, Ruto said his administration had prioritised lowering the cost of essential goods and services while increasing earnings across key sectors of the economy.

“Our economic proposition was simple: Reduce the cost for families and increase the income from what they do,” he said.

On food prices, the President cited the government’s fertiliser subsidy programme, which has reduced the price of a 50-kilogramme bag of fertiliser from Sh7,500 in 2022 to Sh2,000 this year.

He said the government had distributed 38.5 million bags of subsidised fertiliser to farmers, contributing to an increase in maize production from 44.3 million bags in 2022 to 71 million bags last year.

Consequently, maize imports declined from 9.9 million bags to 3.3 million bags, while the average price of a two-kilogramme packet of sifted maize flour dropped from a high of Sh230 in September 2022 to Sh152 in September this year.

Ruto also highlighted gains in the tea, coffee, dairy and sugar industries, saying government interventions had helped improve production and increase farmers' earnings.

He said the Cherry Advance Revolving Fund had disbursed Sh15.07 billion to 684,000 coffee farmers, while tea export earnings increased from Sh163 billion in 2022 to Sh187 billion in 2025.

In the dairy sector, milk production rose from 4.5 billion litres to 5.52 billion litres, while average earnings for farmers increased from Sh32 to Sh60 per litre last month.

Sugar production, he added, increased by 60 per cent between January and October, with cane crushing rising by 57 per cent. The industry is projected to produce more than 900,000 tonnes by the end of the year, with Sh1.2 billion in bonuses expected to be paid to sugarcane farmers.

On healthcare, Ruto said the Social Health Authority (SHA) was designed to ease the financial burden of medical expenses on households through a shared health financing system.

In education, he said the government had employed 100,000 teachers and was preparing to recruit an additional 20,000 to address staffing shortages and reduce the burden on parents who pay teachers hired through Boards of Management.

He added that 23,000 classrooms had been constructed, while 1,600 laboratories were being built and equipped.

The President said the annual education allocation had increased from Sh521 billion in the 2022/23 financial year to Sh784 billion in the current financial year.

"These investments improve the quality of education while progressively reducing the need for Kenyans to finance education," he said.

On affordable housing, Ruto said more than 313,000 homes were at different stages of construction across the 47 counties, with over 1.37 million Kenyans registered on the Boma Yangu platform and more than 18,000 homes already allocated.

He said households could work towards homeownership through monthly payments starting at Sh4,000, which he argued would help ease the burden of rent.

The housing programme, according to the President, had also generated more than 1.1 million employment opportunities and reserved orders worth over Sh61 billion for Jua Kali artisans.

On employment, Ruto said 350,000 Kenyans had secured jobs through the digital economy programme, while another 707,000 had obtained employment abroad through international labour mobility initiatives.

He also cited the Hustler Fund, saying more than seven million Kenyans had established credit records through the programme, with cumulative borrowing reaching Sh94 billion.

Under the NYOTA programme, more than 133,000 young entrepreneurs had received training, mentorship and Sh50,000 each in start-up capital, he said.

The President further announced proposed tax measures aimed at increasing disposable incomes, including exempting workers earning Sh32,333 or less per month from Pay As You Earn (PAYE).

Other proposals include scrapping stamp duty on land transactions valued at Sh1 million or less and removing the 25 per cent import duty on mobile phones.

On pending bills, Ruto said the government had approved the settlement of 28,726 verified claims amounting to Sh27.8 billion, covering debts of Sh50 million and below dating back to 2005.

He added that Sh18 billion owed to public universities and another Sh16 billion owed to public and private hospitals under the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) had been approved for payment and were undergoing Treasury processing.

“These are not isolated interventions, but parts of one comprehensive undertaking,” Ruto said.

He maintained that the government's economic strategy was anchored on reducing household expenditure, increasing incomes and expanding opportunities for Kenyans.

World.title: After 22 years of waiting, woman welcomes quadruplet boys
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Samuel Langat speaks to journalists outside St Clare's Kaplong Mission hospital in Sotik Subcounty, Bomet county after his wife Lily Langat gave to quadruplets at the hospital. [Kiprono Kurgat, Standard]

After 22 years of waiting to become a mother, a woman has welcomed quadruplet boys in a rare and joyful birth that has brought immense happiness to her family.

Lily Langat delivered the quadruplets through a Caesarean section at St Clare’s Kaplong Mission Hospital in Sotik Sub-County on November 14, 2026.

The four boys arrived after more than two decades of waiting for a child in what the family described as a double blessing.

The 43-year-old mother could not hide her joy, saying the arrival of the four babies was an answer to years of prayer.

“I am very grateful to God for giving me four babies at once. This is a great blessing to my family. I thank the hospital staff for ensuring I got to see these bundles of joy,” she said.

“I have been praying and waiting upon God to give me double for the trouble. I have been childless for a long time, and God could not have given me a better gift than this,” she added.

She said she had been looking forward to the moment after doctors informed her early in the pregnancy that she could be carrying quadruplets.

Hospital staff celebrated the successful delivery, describing it as a rare occurrence at the facility.

A nurse who spoke with The Standard said the mother and her four newborns were in stable condition.

“We were delighted to deliver the babies. The mother faced some difficulties because of the combined weight of the four babies, but both she and the newborns are now stable,” she said.

The nurse said the babies had been placed in the nursery for observation and were doing well.

“This is a rare case in this hospital. We have had twins before, but this is different. None of the babies has developed complications so far, and we expect them to be discharged once they are fully stable,” she said.

She added that the mother was also recovering well and was expected to be discharged once doctors were satisfied with the condition of the newborns.

Lily's husband, Samuel Langat, appealed to well-wishers to support the family as they prepare to raise the four children.

“Raising four babies at once is no easy task. I am calling on well-wishers to lend a helping hand as we begin this extraordinary journey,” he said.

“Our four precious miracles have arrived safely, and while our hearts are overflowing with gratitude, the reality of caring for four newborns at once has brought challenges,” he added.

Naturally conceived quadruplets are extremely rare, although the likelihood varies depending on several factors, including maternal age and fertility treatment.

The birth marks a remarkable new beginning for the Langat family after 22 years of waiting for a child.

World.title: TSC picks Cheptumo Ayabei as new Chief Executive Officer
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Teachers Service Commission headquarters in Nairobi. [File, Standard]

The Teachers Service Commission (TSC) has picked Cheptumo Ayabei as its new Secretary and Chief Executive Officer, making him the first person with a disability to head the commission.

Ayabei emerged top in interviews conducted on Monday, beating four other candidates, including the commission’s acting chief executive, Dr Evaleen Jesang Mitei, to become the country’s top teachers’ employer.

His selection ends a prolonged search for a substantive head of the commission, which has operated under acting leadership since the departure of former CEO Nancy Macharia in June 2025.

Ayabei, who hails from Baringo County, is currently TSC’s Director of Finance, having served at the commission for more than two decades. He joined the institution in 1999 as a Finance Officer before rising through the ranks to become Director of Finance in 2009.

His elevation marks a significant milestone for the representation of persons with disabilities in the country’s public institutions.

Ayabei was the first candidate to face the selection panel at 9am at the commission’s headquarters in Upper Hill, Nairobi. He was followed by Mitei at 10am, Robert Odette at 11am, Lawrence Ngai Kaburu at noon and Farah Abdi Saman at 1pm.

The five candidates were shortlisted from 124 applicants who responded to a fresh  issued on September 29. Applications closed on October 30.

Ayabei holds a Bachelor of Education degree in Mathematics and Economics from Kenyatta University and a Master’s degree in Finance and Banking from the University of Stirling in the United Kingdom. He is also a Certified Public Accountant.

Before joining TSC, he worked at the Ministry of Education between 1990 and 1999.

He takes over at a critical time for the commission, which oversees the employment, deployment, promotion and discipline of teachers across the country. He will inherit mounting pressure over teacher shortages, recruitment, promotions, transfers and the management of the teaching workforce.

The recruitment process had faced legal challenges, with a petition filed at the Employment and Labour Relations Court in Kisii seeking to halt the exercise.

The case, filed by Evans Morara Nyangongo under Cause E038 of 2026, challenged the fresh recruitment and raised questions about Mitei’s participation in the process while serving as acting CEO and seeking the substantive position.

Nyangongo sought to stop the commission from proceeding with the appointment until the issues raised in the petition were determined.

However, the court dismissed both the application and the suit, with no orders as to costs, clearing the way for the interviews.

In its defence, TSC maintained that the decision to advertise the position had been made collectively by the commission’s board and not by the acting CEO.

In a replying affidavit, TSC chairman Jamleck Muturi John maintained that Mitei had neither participated in the board’s deliberations on the recruitment nor influenced the process.

The fresh recruitment followed an earlier court decision that nullified the previous exercise over procedural irregularities, forcing the commission to restart the search for a substantive chief executive.

World.title: Thwake Dam project reaches 94pc completion
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Thwake Multipurpose Dam, which is 94.2 per cent complete, with the government targeting April 2027 for water impoundment.[File,Standard]

Thwake Dam is 94.2 per cent complete, with the government targeting April 2027 for water impoundment as residents seek a review of alleged construction-related damage claims.

Principal Secretary for Water and Sanitation Julius Korir told the National Assembly Departmental Committee on Blue Economy, Water and Irrigation that construction had reached 94.2 per cent.

The dam is being built at the confluence of the Athi and Thwake rivers along the Makueni-Kitui border. It is designed to provide water for domestic use, irrigation and electricity generation.

Martin Kimeu, a resident of Wote, said the project would improve access to water for farming in the region.

“Ukambani is fertile. Water has been the biggest impediment to the realization of our agricultural potential. Thwake Dam water is the clear solution to this,” he said.

Kimeu also defended the compensation process, saying he had followed the project since its inception and believed the exercise had been conducted properly.

Jacob Mwanzia, a resident of Madangi Village, said households in his area had been assessed and compensated. He argued that outstanding complaints should be addressed without delaying the project.

Mariam Mwikali, another resident, said assessments had been conducted on affected properties and residents given an opportunity to raise concerns.

However, some households have complained that construction-related blasting damaged their homes. Residents have reported cracks in walls, windows and foundations as well as dust, noise and ground vibrations.

In August 2026, residents from villages in Mavindini Ward, organised under the Thwake Dam Blasting-Affected Community Committee, sought an independent review by the African Development Bank (AfDB).

The residents alleged that some properties had been left out of assessments and compensation. They also sought access to assessment reports, photographs, measurements, valuation records and estimates for repairs or reconstruction.

A project official said the dam's safety department invited competitive bids for an independent assessment of properties potentially affected by blasting. Agile Consulting was selected to conduct the exercise.

The official said the consultant assessed 330 households within a two-kilometre radius of the construction site and submitted its report to the project implementation team. A large proportion of those assessed were satisfied with the exercise, the official added, without giving a breakdown.

Ben Mwongela, a director at Agile Consulting, said the assessment reviewed blasting records, vibration data and compliance with regulatory standards.

The exercise also involved documenting households, classifying structural defects and preparing bills of quantities and cost estimates for repairs or reconstruction, he said.

The AfDB conducted a field mission to the project between September 21 and 25, with its report published on October 21, 2026.

The bank's team, led by project task manager Nancy Ogal, met residents whose homes had been affected by blasting and identified outstanding health, safety, environmental and social issues, including homeowner grievances.

The bank called for timely compensation and continued monitoring of the project's environmental and social performance.

During a stakeholder engagement visit to Mavindini in October, Korir said the government had secured additional funding after the project experienced cash-flow constraints.

“When we ran short of cash, we engaged with our development partners, and they allocated additional funding, and this money will now go towards total completion of the project,” he said.

In June 2026, the AfDB approved additional financing of €68.39 million to support completion of the first phase, alongside funding from the Kenyan government.

The bank said the financing would support engineering refinements and safety works, including strengthening foundations, raising the dam and constructing two additional saddle dams.

The project has four phases. The first involves construction of the dam, while the subsequent phases cover hydropower generation, water supply and sanitation infrastructure, and irrigation.

The dam is approximately 80.5 metres high and has a planned storage capacity of 688 million cubic metres.

Once the water supply component is operational, the project is expected to provide 150,000 cubic metres of treated water daily to an estimated 1.3 million people in Makueni and Kitui counties and Konza Technopolis in Machakos County.

The irrigation scheme is designed to cover 40,000 hectares, equivalent to about 100,000 acres of agricultural land.

The project is also designed to generate 20 megawatts of hydropower.

The water supply, irrigation and hydropower components require infrastructure beyond the dam structure, including treatment and distribution networks and power generation facilities.

World.title: Love under watch: How technology is fuelling intimate partner abuse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Your enemy is closer than you think. For many Kenyan women, the person who demands a phone password, reads private messages and tracks their movements through a screen is not a faceless troll. He is the man they live with, or the one they used to.

That is the uncomfortable picture painted by the recently released 2025–2626 Kenya Mini Demographic and Health Survey (KMDHS), which measured technology-facilitated gender-based violence, abuse committed, assisted, aggravated or amplified through digital tools.

The most common form of abuse is online control, reported by 19 per cent of women, followed by hacking at 5 per cent and online sexual harassment or cyber sexual abuse at 3 per cent. Most of it happens on platforms women use every day.

“Sixty-seven per cent of women who experienced digital gender violence say it happened on social media, with Facebook cited by 59 per cent. Messaging apps follow at 47 per cent, with WhatsApp at 26 per cent. Among girls aged 15–19, 77 per cent reported abuse on social media.”

The report shows how widespread the abuse is. “Twenty-six percent of women age 15–49 have ever experienced technology-facilitated violence from any perpetrator,” the report says, and 21 per cent experienced it often or sometimes in the 12 months before the survey. Among women who have ever had a husband or intimate partner, 27 per cent have experienced it at the hands of a current, most recent or previous partner.

The burden is not spread evenly, the report states that Nairobi City records the highest lifetime experience from any perpetrator at 33 per cent, followed by Murang’a and Baringo at 32 per cent each.

“For abuse by an intimate partner, Homa Bay 36 per cent and Baringo 35 per cent lead, while in the 12 months before the survey Trans Nzoia topped the list at 31 per cent. At the other end, Mandera and Wajir report just 3 per cent, a figure that may say as much about silence as about safety,” the report says

The picture is similar among young people. A 2024 rapid study by the Collaborative Centre for Gender and Development, working with the UNFPA and Women Economic Empowerment, found that nearly 90 per cent of young adults enrolled in three Nairobi tertiary institutions had witnessed TFGBV, and 39 per cent had experienced it personally.

Among women who have ever had a husband or intimate partner, 27 per cent have experienced gender violence committed by a current, most recent or previous partner, and 22 per cent did so in the past year. When women were asked who was responsible, the answer was blunt. Current husbands or intimate partners accounted for 61 per cent of perpetrators, former partners for 22 per cent and strangers for just 13 per cent.

Women who have never been married or had a partner face a different threat. For them, the most common perpetrators are strangers at 45 per cent, online attackers at 23 per cent and friends or acquaintances at 20 per cent.

Warning signs

Control is the common thread. The report describes such behaviours by a male partner as “important early warning signs that may escalate into violence within a relationship.”

Sixty-one per cent of ever-partnered women say their current or most recent partner has shown at least one controlling behaviour, and 27 per cent report three or more. Half say he has been jealous or angry when they spoke to other men, and 36 per cent say he insists on knowing where they are at all times. Others describe partners who demand passwords or read messages without consent.

Age and marital status matter. Technology-based gender violence is lowest among girls aged 15–19 at 10 per cent and highest among women aged 20–24 at 37 per cent. Forty-one per cent of divorced, separated or widowed women have experienced it, compared with 27 per cent of married women and 19 per cent of the never married.

Yet the digital rights advocate Cherie Oyier, a programmes officer at the Kenya ICT Action Network (KICTANet), says the low figures in some places should not be read as safety. Much of the abuse happens where nobody can see it.

“Closed applications, meaning like WhatsApp, those are the ones that most people, intimate partners will usually use,” she says. “Even as you are scrolling the internet to look for these instances, we may not be able to catch it. But it does not mean that it is not happening or that it is at a lower level.”

Culture also silences women. “Most women are told just endure, this is what marriage is about,” Oyier says. “Sometimes they don’t know, it’s so overt, like it doesn’t come out clearly that this is abuse. So most of the times, it is not reported.”

Online, abuse has been turned into entertainment. “It has become banter,” she says. “Even the people who are experiencing it have trivialised it. It’s now ingrained to you, like this is something that happens, you should expect it actually. If you post a picture, one of the things that you are thinking about is what kind of comments am I going to get.”

A 2023 report by KICTANet found that more than 30 per cent of Kenyans have experienced some form of TFGBV, while 90 per cent have witnessed it. In 2025, KICTANet and Equality Now released survivor testimonies showing how deceptive online job offers, grooming and image-based abuse leave women exposed, and how many had never received counselling despite years of trauma.

The stakes are not only digital. The 2025 Report of the Technical Working Group on GBV Including Femicide, cited in the KMDHS, indicated that many cases of homicide of women and girls, and of sexual and physical harm directed towards them, “are preceded by online and offline harassment using digital tools.”

For survivors, the law offers little comfort. “The technology is moving at a very fast pace compared to the laws,” Oyier says. In an attempt to bolster the gaps, Kenya has many fragmented laws. “You’ll have the Data Protection Act, the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, the Children’s Act, that to some extent touch on online issues, but they don’t really cohesively cover the different instances of TFGBV.”

The police, she says, often do not know either. “Just imagine you’re a woman who is in a village, for example, a village in Siaya, and you encounter violence. For you to even understand which law apply is very stressful.”

“You’re going through psychological stress and depression, and you’re also supposed to figure out which law applies in your situation. It causes even more problems for victims and survivors.”

Flagging abusive language

Artificial intelligence is adding a new layer. Even so, Oyier cautions against writing it off. “We should not vilify AI completely,” she says. KICTANet has built a lexicon to help flag abusive language and runs a tracker for online gender-based violence. “One person cannot sit down and look at everything on social media. When AI is able to pull every post that has this word, a human content moderator is able to look through it with local context and see is this TFGBV or not.”

The KMDHS findings further show that exposure to TFGBV varies across age groups and digital platforms.

“Younger women are particularly exposed on social media, with 77 per cent of women aged 15–19 and 72 per cent of those aged 20–24 who experienced TFGBV reporting abuse on social media platforms, compared with 50 per cent of women aged 40–49.”

However, messaging applications tell a different story. Women aged 40–49 reported the highest exposure through these platforms at 54 per cent, compared with 30 per cent among teenagers aged 15–19.

Wealth also influences where women encounter online abuse. Exposure on social media increases from 45 per cent among women in the lowest wealth quintile to 74 per cent among those in the highest. Conversely, women in the lowest wealth quintile report greater exposure through messaging applications, at 62 per cent, compared with 39 per cent among those in the highest wealth quintile.

These differences suggest that TFGBV cuts across age and economic backgrounds, although the platforms through which women experience it vary.

World.title: Not so fast: Court slams brake on ARA over wealth forfeiture
World.content:
Felix Mecha Nyakundi could not provide a plausible explanation for how he amassed his wealth.

The Court of Appeal has ruled that the government cannot go after a person’s wealth without prior investigations to establish reasonable grounds for suspecting that the property constitutes proceeds of crime.

In a landmark judgment, Justices Patrick Kiage, Jamila Mohammed and Nduma Nderi said that although it does not require a person to be charged for a crime for the Asset Recovery Agency (ARA) to come knocking, it bears the responsibility to link the wealth or cash to a crime.

World.title: Almost all of Anthropic’s employees are now millionaires
World.content:
New York —

Anthropic’s stock market debut turned the vast majority of the young startup’s staff into overnight millionaires — some many times over.

The company’s headcount stood at 5,300 as of September this year, according to regulatory filings. After Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, about 600 employees entered the rarefied “centi-millionaire” club, with equity holdings valued north of $100 million, according to data from Hill.com, which tracks private-company shares.

As many as 2,800 staffers, known internally as “Ants,” have holdings valued above $10 million. And about 5,100 — 96% of the staff — are sitting on equity north of $1 million.

“What’s most surprising here is how quickly this this happened,” Andrew Benson, Hill’s founder and CEO, told CNN on Thursday, noting Anthropic has seen very little attrition. “It’s been pretty clear for some time that Anthropic is a rocket ship, and so it definitely discouraged people from leaving because they knew what the opportunity cost of that would be.”

It’s not unusual for Silicon Valley startups, which are typically light on cash, to pay their staff with a combination of salary and stock. The promise of a future acquisition or initial public offering tends to keep workers motivated to work hard and stick it out until payday.

But few startups have grown as big or as quickly as Anthropic. The company, founded in 2021, had fewer than 1,000 employees at the end of 2024.

As with most tech startups, Benson noted, “being early is more important, in terms of a financial outcome, than being senior … You could be very low on the totem pole, and if you joined in 2023 or 2024, you’re likely to have a significantly better outcome than a senior person who joined earlier this year.”

SpaceX, by contrast, spent more than two decades as a private company before its blockbuster IPO in June. That debut minted around 4,400 millionaires, out of a staff of 22,000.

Anthropic’s IPO is also unique for allowing non-founder insiders to cash out on Day One of trading. In most IPOs, staff are subject to a “lockup” period — typically three to six months — during which they can’t sell their shares. But Anthropic’s listing included a complex, staggered lockup schedule that allowed non-founder insiders to cash out up to 10% of their shares as soon as the stock began trading. (It’s not known how many insiders may have taken advantage of the opportunity Thursday.)

And unlike SpaceX, which has employees spread across Texas, California and Florida, Anthropic is uniquely concentrated in San Francisco, a city whose entire economy has been reshaped by sudden surges of tech wealth.

A rash of newly minted millionaires could soon amplify pressure on San Francisco’s housing market, where home prices are already rising at their fastest pace in years.

The typical home there sold for $1.7 million in October, up nearly 19% from a year earlier, according to Redfin. By contrast, the national median home price was roughly flat over the same period, at $416,700, according to the National Association of Realtors.

World.title: Nayib Bukele promised Haiti a ‘triumph.’ Are his forces delivering?
World.content:
Gun-toting robots trotting down a dark alley. The blaze of a helicopter-launched rocket. A gang boss’s mansion crumbling in the sunshine.

Thousands of Salvadoran troops landed in Haiti last month to combat gangs overrunning the Caribbean nation. While it’s too early to tell if they’re succeeding, the personal involvement of popular Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele has stirred rare hope on the island – and avid interest across Latin America.

What’s the difference between the newly arrived Salvadorans and all the other fighting forces in Haiti’s crowded security landscape? “They’re really good at making videos,” one local security source said.

Most of what we know about the Salvadoran force has come in glimpses from Bukele’s social media accounts. The deal governing their presence has not been made public, but the 45-year-old president is effectively drumming up support with promises in Creole to root out the gangs as he has done in El Salvador, combined with explosive footage and online banter.

“For the first time, I felt like someone had listened to me,” said Sophia Fecu, describing the moment she saw a video posted by Bukele that showed helicopters attacking gang leader Lanmo Sanjou’s house on the outskirts of the capital Port-au-Prince. “I felt like my voice had finally been heard.”

Days earlier, Fecu, a Haitian entrepreneur and writer, had posted a picture of the notorious gang clubhouse on X and tagged Bukele. “I just felt that it wasn’t right for these criminals to be living so comfortably while the rest of the population was forced to flee their homes and communities,” she said from the US, where she now lives. “I honestly didn’t expect him to respond.”

But he did. Bukele answered on X asking for the location of the house, sparking a flurry of responses. Three days later, he posted an update: Video of helicopters blasting apart the building’s blue-tiled facade, shadowy figures of suspected gang members fleeing the compound on foot.

It’s hard to imagine other forces in Haiti crowdsourcing coordinates for a well-known gang headquarters. But Haitian police, a secretive task force involving a private military contractor led by Erik Prince, and the multinational Gang Suppression Force have been busy, too: Police announced on Thursday that they had killed 34 gang members in a major operation in the Port-au-Prince neighborhood of Martissant. The GSF, still building its force, said its operations are entering a “new phase” of pressure and is also posting more videos of soldiers at work. But no one boasts the same reach as Bukele.

Some friction was inevitable. Security sources in Haiti complain about a lack of cooperation and credit-sharing with the Salvadorans and point out that fighting videos don’t show the difficult reality of working in Haiti, like finding parts to repair helicopters damaged by gang fire.

Last week, Salvadoran troops reportedly fired perilously close to GSF troops. On another occasion, they sparked tensions after trying to enter a GSF outpost without notice, sources said. On Friday, two soldiers died and two others were wounded in an incident handling explosive material, according to the Salvadoran army.

Still, there is hope for a deeper eventual collaboration once the new force finds its footing. And Bukele will need it. He has raised expectations in an exhausted nation, and now he must deliver. His troops are far from home and facing a gang alliance that knows the terrain better, can replace fallen soldiers with forced conscripts, and shares information and resources across Port-au-Prince.

“Imagine if the police, task force, GSF and Salvadorans were all working together, with their combined ground and air forces — that would be amazing,” a security source said wistfully.

World.title: Venezuela a ‘compliant security partner,’ Hegseth says as he announces military deal with Caracas
World.content:
The United States has signed a new agreement to reestablish military ties with Venezuela more than 10 months after toppling its leader in a military raid, US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth announced during his first trip to the South American nation on Wednesday.

“Venezuela has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner,” Hegseth said outside the US Embassy in Caracas.

The Pentagon chief described the deal as “historic,” saying it would allow American and Venezuelan forces to train together and share intelligence, defense equipment and other capabilities.

He insisted that the partnership would not be “cosmetic” and would require defense and security reforms in Venezuela to modernize its military and eliminate “persistent threats” to both nations.

Venezuela interim President Delcy Rodriguez and US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth meet at Miraflores Palace in Caracas, Venezuela, on November 18. Miraflores Palace/Handout/Reuters

The timeline and scope of the deal remain unclear.

The Defense Department has not responded to questions about the agreement or Hegseth’s trip, nor did it provide a daily schedule for the secretary on the day of his visit.

Hegseth appeared to have signed the agreement earlier at the Venezuelan presidential palace with Defense Minister Gustavo Gonzalez Lopez, according to footage broadcast on state TV.

In a televised meeting with Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodriguez, Hegseth said the US looks forward to deepening their defense cooperation “to ensure the Venezuelan people are not threatened by foreign actors or narco-terrorists or criminals and that they are safe and secure inside sovereign borders.”

Rodriguez said their renewed “technical-military cooperation” is meant to confront common threats and make the region safer.

Both Hegseth and Rodriguez underscored their countries’ remarkable turn in relations since the US captured Venezuela’s authoritarian leader Nicolas Maduro on January 3.

“The weight of this moment does not escape me,” Hegseth said outside the embassy. “Just one year ago, my presence here, our presence here would have been deemed impossible.”

Rodriguez said, “We have turned very difficult and very harsh moments for our people … into an extraordinary space for cooperation and the mutual benefit of our countries.”

Since Maduro’s capture, the US has been working with the acting Venezuelan government on the country’s democratic transition and political reconciliation.

Rodriguez has met just about every demand from Washington, including releasing hundreds of political prisoners and making it easier for US companies to invest in the country.

Wednesday’s military deal is the latest effort by the Trump administration to bolster security cooperation with Latin American countries with the aim of combating what it calls “designated terrorist organizations” in the region.

Hegseth traveled to Colombia later on Wednesday and was expected to discuss security ties and deliver military equipment, according to the Colombian defense minister.

That visit comes amid a New York Times report that said Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella this week rejected a US plan for joint anti-crime operations on Colombian soil. The president later denied that claim.

A source from Colombia’s Ministry of Defense told CNN that while the government supports increased military cooperation and the intelligence sharing to combat drug cartels and terrorist organizations, it cannot greenlight operations involving foreign forces on the ground, as this requires legislative authorization.

Hegseth is also expected to travel to Ecuador and Honduras as part of a tour of Latin America.

World.title: The FBI was hacked again, this time the breach targeted its crime database
World.content:
The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its nationwide criminal information database that serves as a lifeline between federal, state and local law enforcement, two people briefed on the investigation said.

The intrusion of the National Crime Information Center by apparent hackers is the second such breach in recent months.

The NCIC database is used by law enforcement nationwide to share information on warrants and background checks.

The discovery of the latest intrusion in recent days comes as the Trump administration has sought to assuage public concern about the nation’s cybersecurity amid a series of high profile outages affecting banks, the National Security Agency and the FAA’s air traffic control system.

The FBI didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

On Thursday, after bureau officials learned of the latest cybersecurity incident, FBI Director Kash Patel appeared on Fox News to tout the FBI’s cybersecurity work.

Patel used the appearance to discuss an operation completed months ago aimed at urging companies to update their systems and prevent hackers from getting to their sensitive data.

Patel referred to Operation Winter Shield as if it was still in the works, and touted the current administration for making updates to key systems to protect the nation’s critical infrastructure.

“Other administrations could have made these updates, but they didn’t,” he said. “We are staying ahead of the curve and making up for lost time.”

The NCIC database is one of the most critical information-sharing systems in law enforcement, a former FBI official who led investigations into cybercriminal groups told CNN. “Every day, officers across the country rely on NCIC to identify wanted fugitives, check for outstanding warrants, and access information that can directly impact officer and public safety. My concern isn’t simply whether hackers gained access to sensitive information, although that is an issue, but whether they could compromise the accuracy of the information that officers rely on.”

Prior hacks

A September attack by a group called ShinyHunters targeted sensitive employee personal data from an FBI jobs website.

A Canadian cybersecurity researcher and author has been arrested and faces charges related to the ShinyHunters breach.

After the ShinyHunters breach, some FBI employees felt left in the dark about whether they were affected by the data theft and underwhelmed by the security resources being offered to victims, CNN previously reported.

In an earlier breach in 2023, hackers breached a computer system the FBI’s New York field office used in child sexual exploitation investigations, including a system used to store images related to the Jeffrey Epstein probe, CNN previously reported.

CNN’s Sean Lyngaas contributed to this report.

World.title: Visa facilitations underway for various nationalities in Egypt: Official
World.content:
A tourism expert and member of the General Assembly of the Chamber of Tourism Companies, Mohamed Abdel-Dayem, said that there are currently unprecedented facilities available to any foreigner wishing to visit Egypt—particularly those arriving for medical treatment or tourism.

Abdel-Dayem explained that the package of measures approved by the Egyptian state to simplify entry for visitors of various nationalities includes streamlined visa acquisition, as well as easier processes for bookings, accommodation, and transportation.

These will cover the entire journey from the visitor’s home country until their departure from Egyptian territory.

He added that these facilities also encompass assistance with obtaining visas for patients and their companions, arranging travel and accommodation, airport reception, and providing transportation, as well as ongoing support and accompaniment throughout the visit.

This spares visitors from administrative complexities, allowing them to focus entirely on the primary purpose of their trip—whether it be medical treatment, tourism, or study.

The expert emphasized that this initiative reflects the state’s commitment to opening its doors to the world and ensuring a more seamless and comfortable experience for visitors.

Medical tourism is a ‘key pillar’

Abdel-Dayem emphasized that medical tourism has become a key pillar within this initiative—a development bolstered by the establishment of the National Council for Health Tourism and the launch of a national medical tourism platform.

These initiatives help connect medical and tourism institutions with relevant authorities, while facilitating access for international patients to services at government, university, and private hospitals, as well as specialized medical centers.

Abdel-Dayem noted that the available support services encompass everything from selecting the appropriate hospital and scheduling appointments with top physicians and specialists, to coordinating medical care, follow-ups, hotel accommodations, and transportation.

He also highlighted a special focus on visitors from Africa, reflecting the deep-rooted ties between Egypt and the African continent.

Language is no obstacle

Abdel-Dayem assured that language barriers will not pose an obstacle for any visitor; plans are being considered to enlist African students currently enrolled in Egyptian universities—who speak the languages of their home countries—to serve as companions and guides.

This approach would simultaneously create job opportunities for the students and provide a valuable, humanitarian service to patients and the elderly.
