Welcome to Screencaps, "America's Best Daily Column," as named by the readers. Screencaps, which publishes seven days a week, is a mix of sports, pop culture, and emails from sane readers from around the world. This column isn't for the coastal elites. Odds & ends on this Saturday morning before Thanksgiving

Charley Hull continues to be one of us. A couple of years after she gave up cigs as part of a bet, the world's No. 8 female golfer announced this week that she's planning to give up smart phones for a month - at least - over the holidays as part of a detox. "I'm going to go home, buy myself a Nokia phone and for the whole month just change my SIM over and just completely switch off from the world," Hull, 30, said. "Just an old-school phone so I can't look at anything, don't have to worry about anything. If anyone wants to call, just call me on that phone. I'm done with texting. I'm done with social media. I just want to have a whole month detox."

GOLFER AND DEFENDER OF SYDNEY SWEENEY, CHARLEY HULL, TURNED HEADS ON THE ROLEX LPGA AWARDS GREEN CARPET

I got a text from my mom on Friday asking if I knew they were shooting a Hooters movie in Clearwater. I knew there was a movie in the works, and an hour before she texted me, I saw that Carmen Electra hinted at a starring role in the movie, but I didn't know they're shooting it in Clearwater. This is either going to be an incredible movie that pop culture desperately needs or it's going to be a total mess. There cannot be an in-between.

HOOTERS RESTAURANTS KEEP DISAPPEARING AS ICONIC CHAIN LOSES LONGTIME LOCATIONS IN FOUNDING STATE

I'm going to be a company man for a second and say today's Big Noon Kickoff is a must-see. Fox pulled the trigger that ESPN wouldn't and decided to go promote DII Ferris State. Let's face it, Big Rapids isn't Fargo, ND where GameDay had a crazy environment in 2014. Big Rapids' population is around 8,600. But, Ferris State has a student population around 10,000. It's time to see if they're ready for the big time.

I took Screencaps Jr. to the BG-Toledo game last night and he actually asked me to buy him a Toledo hoodie. Those of you with 14 year olds these days understand how big of a compliment that is. He actually requested gear from the school I went to and it wasn't a moment of charity out of him.Another big moment was when I showed him the library. He made some sort of mention about "Why is the building so big?" I then had to remind him that there was a time in history when students had to actually go to the library to do research instead of hopping on the computer. That walk with him across the campus last night brought back some vivid memories in my life. It was a nice father-son moment capped off by Eddie George trotting out an absolutely pitiful offense that resulted in a 19-0 Toledo win.

The MAC has to keep the Toledo-BG game on the Friday night a week before the Ohio State-Michigan game. The atmosphere last night was incredible. The weather was incredible. The tailgating was legit tailgating. ESPN and the other networks need to realize that these schools cannot survive unless you throw them a bone. Keep these games on days when people will actually show up.

"Would you let me play this game?" Mrs. Screencaps asked me this morning. I think she just wants to take nut shots with that 2-liter bottle. She then launched into a giggling fit. I'm onto her games.

Quick emails before I go do yard work

• Ricky A. says: I know it’s contrary to the sentiment around these parts (and for obvious reason, no denying), but would like to raise a hand in support of a dying Wendy’s brand. Been on the train for years that there is no greater deal in the culinary industry than the double stack biggie bag for years. 100% an inflation buster & on board with my (albeit maybe once a month) purchase.

Thankfully one of our local spots hasn’t been fully infested with ex-cons & meth heads. Give me that solid double & spicy nugs, my half/half tea (can’t handle the full sweet like I was in my prime) with some fresh cut fries & it’s pure white trash bliss. Love it. (Full disclosure, got smart last year & married a lady with a culinary degree so don’t get many sneak-away lunches anymore. Fair tradeoff). She had a craving some for nuggets the other night & was all about the seasonal beanies. Got her wish & landed the Frosty edition & can’t complain about my vintage Biggie. Got a long road ahead to live up to Dave’s dreams. Beanies are no solarium, but baby steps.

As for some gift ideas, if you haven’t jumped on the rechargeable handwarmer game I can’t stress it enough. Fall/Winter golf, sitting in cold stadiums, long walks with the pup, an absolute must for these occasions. I’ve got the Actionheat (not-sponsored) as my go-to. Love the long battery life. Side note, they’ve got an NFL deal to get team editions if you’re looking for that too. The Thaw is the newest addition & think I could boil a pot of water on it on low. Sucker is legit & great for those cooler windy days ($40-50). If you love card games Play Nine ($20) is a must. Don’t have to be a golf purist to pick up the game & extremely easy to pick up. Gets very cutthroat if you’re as competitive with everything as we are in our household.

Keep up the great work. Thanks for providing us this outlet & community outreach.

• Jack V. on roadside springs to fill up your water bottles on road trips: There are roadside springs on both sides of US 26 between portland and seaside oregon. I have never driven by without a car or two stopped at them filling 5 gallon jugs. We have good drinking water here in the pacific northwest so that stuff must be elixir of the gods.

Congrats to SC Jr on a great finish to his CC season, as well as one helluva time in the half marathon. Well done!

Plan to watch the Madden movie this weekend. Vividly remember the Raiders back in those days, and all the hijinks Al Davis pulled. Heard quite a few bad things about it, but was good to see a positive note today from someone with a similar background.

World.title: History buff links prominent colonial New Yorker to notorious pirate heist
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

An amateur historian believes he's found clues suggesting a link between a notorious 17th-century pirate and the namesake of New York's famous Jones Beach — and says he has the documents to back it up.

James Bailey, who found ancient coins linked to pirate Capt. Henry Every — known as the "King of the Pirates" — in 2014, recently said colonial-era records suggest Every and his crew got an assist from Thomas Jones, the namesake of the Long Island state park, The Associated Press (AP) reported.

Bailey was metal detecting at Sweet Berry Farm, a fruit orchard in Middletown, Rhode Island, when he unearthed an Every-linked 17th-century Arabian coin over a decade ago.

TREASURE HUNTERS FIND BIGGEST VIKING COIN HOARD IN COUNTRY'S HISTORY: 'WITHOUT PARALLEL'

It wasn't until 2021 that Bailey publicized his discovery to the AP and dug deeper into colonial records — which led him to do further research on Every and Jones.

Every is best known for leading the 1695 raid on the royal Indian treasure ship Ganj-i-Sawai in the Red Sea — making off with tens of millions of dollars in gold and silver before vanishing in what some consider the first worldwide manhunt.

Bailey — whose claims are not yet independently verified — said documents suggest Jones was recruited to serve as a "wheelman" for Every and help the crew steer clear of authorities.

"You have millions of visitors and generations of New Yorkers going to this beach," Bailey told the AP.

TREASURE HUNTERS RECOVER RARE SILVER BAR FROM LEGENDARY SHIPWRECK OFF FLORIDA KEYS

"Nobody knew he was actually a major player in arguably the biggest heist in the history of piracy."

Even during his lifetime, a document showed that New York's governor investigated Jones after he had already become the proprietor of a whaling operation, AP reported.

Jones was born in Ireland and moved to Rhode Island and New York before acquiring acres of land that now comprise Jones Beach.

How exactly he made his fortune was considered a mystery both now and after his death.

REVOLUTIONARY WAR ARTIFACTS UNEARTHED AT SITE OF INFAMOUS COLONIAL AMERICAN HEIST: 'VERY SURPRISED'

In 1906, one of his descendants addressed the rumors that Jones was a pirate, calling them "slander" and "improbable fictions."

"People were disposed to cast slurs upon his memory, either for mischievousness, or a spirit of malice," the writer, Thomas Floyd-Jones, said at the time.

"The reality was that privateers were pirates, just sponsored by a certain government or patron."

He added, "These myths were cherished for over a century after his death, which ignorance and superstition did not fail to magnify."

Meagan Schulman, a Fordham University doctoral candidate who specializes in 17th-century piracy and was not involved in the research, told the AP that, since Jones was already a privateer authorized to raid commercial ships of rivals, he could already be considered a pirate.

CLICK HERE TO 

It was only when war ended that those who continued to do so were called pirates.

"The reality was that privateers were pirates, just sponsored by a certain government or patron," said Schulman, as the AP reported.

"So maybe the short answer is, yes. Jones can be called a pirate, by some people, but he probably did not ever see himself as one."

Part of Jones' wealth came when his father-in-law gifted him a lot of land — something Bailey suggests gave him a fresh start.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Richard Blakemore, a maritime history professor at the University of Reading in the United Kingdom, told the AP that Bailey's research is persuasive but not yet definitive.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

He added that the records point to how deeply early British colonies were intertwined with piracy.

"Popular images of pirates show them as outcasts, but many historians have argued the opposite, based on evidence like this," Blakemore said.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"It may surprise readers to find just how much [the] early British colonies were both socially and economically connected to piracy."

World.title: 'Economic populist' Texas Gov-elect Gina Hinojosa eyes talks with Elon Musk

Texas' Democratic governor-elect, Gina Hinojosa, shared details about her political philosophy as she prepares to lead the Lone Star State.

"I'd call myself an economic populist," she told "Special Report" anchor Bret Baier on Thursday. "What I heard across the state is that people want a government that is going to roll up its sleeves and deliver."

Hinojosa's self-description could be significant for Elon Musk, whose companies SpaceX and Tesla are both headquartered in Texas. Musk, who reportedly spent around $500 million on Republican candidates and causes in the midterm elections, predicted at this week's New York Times DealBook Summit that "the new governor is going to be quite moderate."

Hinojosa told Baier that she looks forward to working with Musk.

"This is a government that people pay for," she said. "It should be working for them."

NEW TEXAS GOVERNOR-ELECT STRIKES CONCILIATORY TONE TOWARD MUSK AFTER CAMPAIGNING AGAINST SPACEX DEAL

Hinojosa is the first Democrat elected governor of Texas since Ann Richards won in 1990, a victory Hinojosa described as a "mandate for change."

The governor-elect said oneo f her first priorities is to impose a moratorium on new data center permits until new safeguards are put in place, though she doesn't expect data center companies to leave the state.

"I don't hate data centers," she told Baier. "I just hate the way they're taking advantage of Texans right now."

Hailing from the border city of Brownsville, Hinojosa said she understands Americans who want a secure border. Her agenda, however, includes reducing cooperation between Texas law enforcement and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

HOUSTON MAYOR BOLTS EARLY FROM ICE COOPERATION AFTER BLUE WAVE CRASHES IN TEXAS

"We've had people killed, Americans killed, people mowed down in the streets," she said. "That needs to end. I will not facilitate that."

DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin denounced Texas officials who plan to end local law enforcement's cooperation with ICE, warning that doing so would be "of the worst derelictions of duty we've seen in a very long time."

Hinojosa said she makes a distinction between ICE and Border Patrol, saying she wants to strengthen border security through cooperation with the Trump administration, local law enforcement and Mexican counterparts.

One Democrat says he favors Hinojosa's approach and her willingness to work with the Trump administration.

"I think if the [Democratic Party] takes a hard left, this will be a short-lived majority. And I feel the same for the great state of Texas," said Rep. Vicente Gonzalez, D-Texas. "I think now that we have the power, we need to use it thoughtfully and carefully."

World.title: Built from Scratch: How three grandsons turned $500 and a garage into a hearing aid company
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

When Ishan Patel, Dylan Garber and Zack Hubbard started Audien Hearing in 2019, they didn't have investors, a big team or millions of dollars in funding.

They had $500, a garage in Arizona and an idea that would eventually revolutionize the hearing aid industry.

The three young entrepreneurs already shared something in common: Each had a grandparent struggling with hearing loss.

They had seen firsthand how something as simple as following a conversation could become difficult. They had seen how the high cost of hearing aids could prevent people from getting the help they needed.

CEO SUNDAY: BLACKBERRY BOSS ON THE COMPANY'S EVOLUTION FROM SMARTPHONE GIANT TO SOFTWARE POWERHOUSE

So they decided to do something about it. Their mission was simple: Make hearing aids affordable and accessible to everyone.

Seven years later, Audien has grown from a handful of people working out of a residential garage into a nationwide hearing care brand with a global team of more than 100 employees. Today, Audien products are sold through major American retailers, and the company has served more than 2 million customers.

Three grandsons and a garage

In the beginning, Audien looked nothing like the company it is today.

The founders (who are not related) did everything themselves, from building the website and answering customer calls to packing orders and coordinating shipments. Boxes of hearing aids filled the garage, which became the warehouse, fulfillment center and makeshift office for the brand. Every new order was a small victory.

There was no established playbook. They learned by doing, making mistakes and figuring out how to solve each new problem they faced.

Building a business against the odds

As Audien grew, so did the challenges.

The company faced fulfillment problems during the start of the COVID pandemic.

BUILT FROM SCRATCH: HOW A METEOROLOGIST BUILT A BETTER UMBRELLA

Periods of rapid growth strained operations, causing the founders to rethink how they did business.

More than once, the future of the company was uncertain.

"There were plenty of times when we were on the brink of failure. But we never seriously considered giving up."

"There were plenty of times when we were on the brink of failure. But we never seriously considered giving up," the founders said.

What kept them going was the mission that inspired them in the first place: They wanted to help people reconnect with the world around them.

From Arizona garage to Walmart shelves

One of Audien's biggest breakthroughs came in 2023, when the company launched its Atom One hearing aids at Walmart stores nationwide for under $100.

For the founders, seeing their products on shelves across America was a remarkable milestone.

A company that had started by shipping orders from a garage was now bringing affordable hearing technology directly to customers through one of the nation's largest retailers.

More milestones followed, including national television appearances, a major QVC Today's Special Value event, expansion into additional retailers and a partnership with legendary actor William Shatner.

2 million customers later

"As an audiologist, I often had to turn patients away because they couldn't afford prescription products. That’s why I joined Audien Hearing as their head of audiology —because their products can help more people hear at a fraction of the price," said Dr. Rachel Trinker.

It's the people they've been able to help.

The next chapter

Even after reaching millions of customers, Audien's founders believe the company's biggest opportunities are still ahead.

The company plans to continue expanding its hearing technology, reaching new markets and exploring products and services that support healthy aging.

The ambition is to build on what Audien has already accomplished and help people stay connected, independent and engaged with life as they get older.

World.title: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to kill Ukrainian American rapper on its soil
World.content:
COPENHAGEN, Denmark — Authorities thwarted the attempted killing of a Ukrainian American citizen on Danish soil in a plot allegedly orchestrated by Russian intelligence services, the Danish prime minister’s office said Friday.

The Russian defense attaché has been expelled from Denmark in response, Danish Minister for Foreign Affairs Lars Løkke Rasmussen told a news conference. Two alleged members of the outlawed Danish gang “Loyal to Familia” have been arrested in connection with the attempted killing, police said.

Danish broadcaster DR, citing a court hearing, reported the men are suspected of having been recruited to assassinate ​a Ukrainian rapper ahead of a planned performance.

Police thwarted the alleged plot when they arrested ​the two men shortly before the rapper ​Kyivstoner’s September 25 concert, which was later ⁠cancelled.

It was unclear how police identified the two men, who ​were stopped in ​a vehicle ⁠carrying several weapons, or how the investigation expanded to include two other men ​who are not accused of participating ​in ⁠the alleged assassination plot targeting Kyivstoner.

However, all four men have been held in custody since September, according to ⁠the ​broadcaster.

It was also unclear how ​the Russian intelligence services allegedly recruited the two Danish suspects.

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said: “It is a clear illustration of the grave security situation Denmark and Europe find ourselves in. We are facing a Russia under pressure which is acting more aggressively and is more willing to take risks.”

The Danes’ announcement came as tensions between Europe and Russia heightened again Friday. Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland in what its prime minister said was likely a provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in his country for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine.

European Commission ​President Ursula von der Leyen said on Saturday the E.U. ⁠stands in full solidarity with Denmark.

“This was an ​attack ⁠on E.U. ‌soil. And it is unacceptable. We stand in full ‌solidarity with Denmark. ‌And with all Member States targeted by Russian ⁠hybrid attacks,” she said in an X post.

European Council President António Costa said: “We will not be intimidated. Russia’s tactics and threats will not weaken the European Union’s resolve to continue supporting Ukraine.”

The Russian embassy in Copenhagen said on Friday the accusations were not backed ‌with proof.

World.title: FBI investigating potential breach of its crime database
World.content:
The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its National Crime Information Center, two people briefed on the matter told NBC News Friday.

The FBI’s National Crime Information Center is used to connect federal, state and local authorities so that important law enforcement information is available nationwide.

The FBI had no comment as of Friday night.

CNN reported the matter earlier in the evening.

While the FBI has not addressed who may have breached the system in this case, the agency did announce an investigation in September of a notorious hacking group that claimed it had stolen data on agents through the agency’s job portal.

The breach this week follows an apparent cyberattack at the U.S. Department of Agriculture, as employees were informed Thursday that one of its systems had been targeted.

USDA officials with knowledge of the matter said that a system the agency uses to pay farmers was hit by the breach, though as of Friday, no other systems were targeted. Officials raised alarms that the hackers could find a way to access more sensitive information due to the breach.

Alongside the reported breaches, outages affecting both private and public sectors over the last several days have raised concerns about the nation’s cybersecurity.

An internal classified computer network used by the National Security Agency endured a multi-day outage after it first went down Tuesday due to a technical problem, according to two people with knowledge of the matter. As of Friday, the outage has been resolved, sources said.

Sources told NBC News that the network went down while maintenance was being performed. They said that there was no sign that the outage was caused by a cyberattack.

Addressing the widespread tech outages, Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., the top Democrat on the Senate Intelligence Committee, said Wednesday that evidence showed that the tech outages were not caused by cyberattacks, though he warned that AI could have played a role in the systems’ vulnerabilities.

Amid rising concerns about the outages, a White House official confirmed to NBC News Thursday that White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was leaving his role.

Cairncross was directly involved with the White House’s deliberations on AI policy, including its move to direct Anthropic to take down its two most powerful AI systems over the summer due to national security concerns.

World.title: Trump formally ends minting of the penny after nearly 250 years of production
World.content:
Washington is officially done with spending a pretty penny on penny production.

President Donald Trump on Friday signed the bipartisan Common Cents Act, which formally directs the federal government to stop minting the penny.

Both the House and the Senate passed the measure by voice vote, meaning no notable opposition.

“It costs nearly FOUR cents to make just one penny,” the bill’s author, Rep. Lisa McClain, R-Mich., said Sept. 29 on X a day after Senate passage. “This legislation will save $85 million per year by permanently ending penny production — it’s common sense!”

The government stopped making pennies in November 2025, nine months after Trump called for the Treasury Department to stop production, writing at the time that the process was “so wasteful!” Stephen Hilger / Bloomberg via Getty Images

The U.S. Mint last year put the immediate annual savings of discontinuing penny production at $56 million.

The government stopped making pennies in November 2025, nine months after Trump called for the Treasury Department to stop production, writing at the time that the process was “so wasteful!” However, the U.S. Mint said it would still produce collector versions to be produced in “limited quantities.”

The penny can still be used as legal tender “for all debts, public charges, taxes, and dues,” according to the new law. The Treasury Department said last year that the Federal Reserve will continue to recirculate the approximately 114 billion pennies that are in existence “for as long as possible.”

The new measure also provides a procedure for stores and businesses that accept cash payments to round their prices to the nearest amount divisible by 5 cents.

And, as the nickel replaces the penny at the bottom of the U.S. Mint’s currency list, that coin can now be manufactured with an inner layer of zinc and an outer layer of nickel. It is currently produced with nickel and copper, which costs more than zinc.

Congress passed the Coinage Act in 1792, and the U.S. Mint began producing the penny, known officially as the cent, the following year.

It wasn’t until 1909 that it was given its modern-day face, featuring President Abraham Lincoln. Stephen Hilger / Bloomberg via Getty Images file

In its nearly 250 years in production, the penny has had multiple facades. It wasn’t until 1909 that it was given its modern-day face, featuring President Abraham Lincoln.

The first penny, produced in 1787, had a sundial design created by Benjamin Franklin. After the U.S. Mint took over, the penny was slightly bigger and included the image of a woman representing Liberty on one side and 15 chain links on the other.

The next penny debuted in 1857, taking on a smaller shape and displaying a flying eagle design on one side and a wreath on the other. It also changed from being 100% copper to 88% copper and 12% nickel. Two years later, an “Indian Head” design was added to one side.

The most recent design from the U.S. Mint was issued in 2010, featuring its “Union Shield” theme. It shows a shield on the tails side of the coin to represent “Lincoln’s preservation of the United States as a single country,” the U.S. Mint wrote.

World.title: Get the 47+ best Advent calendars of the year before they sell out
World.content:
Traditionally, Advent calendars count down the days until Christmas. Some classic options have chocolate, caramels or other sweet treats hidden behind little doors, while others require you to turn on a light or check off a box leading up to the holiday. In recent years, however, Advent calendars have taken on a new life. Now, there’s an option for any holiday you celebrate, and they’re filled with coffee, wine, Legos, beauty products, pet treats and more.

If you plan on counting down to the holidays this year with an Advent calendar, you don’t have much time left to buy one: You need a 24-day option by Dec. 1 or a 12-day option by Dec. 13 to stay on track. Popular calendars are already selling out, so don’t dilly-dally. This is officially your last chance to get one for yourself or a loved one.

Below, I rounded up the best Advent calendars of 2026. I’ll frequently update this article throughout the next few weeks to share ones that are still available.

Want more from NBC Selected? 

Best Advent calendars overall

I’m loyal to Bonne Maman jam, and every year, I look forward to its Advent calendar, which is filled with new limited-edition spreads. There’s a mini glass jar hidden inside each of the 24 boxes, and the festively decorated calendar opens like a book, which lets me stand it up on a shelf, doubling as holiday decor. This year, you’ll get to try spreads like caramel with salted butter, strawberry with Madagascar vanilla and raspberry with dark chocolate. Don’t worry if you can’t finish every jar before the end of the season — the spreads will last through June 2027, according to Bonne Maman.

You can’t go wrong with a chocolate Advent calendar whether you’re buying it for yourself or gifting it to a loved one. It’s a classic for a reason, and getting to unwrap a new piece of chocolate every day is a small joy that anyone can appreciate. Lindt’s Advent calendar comes with 24 pieces of chocolate, including those shaped like mini bears, chocolate balls and chocolate neapolitans. For the first time this year, Lindt is adding an interactive element to its Advent calendar: From December 1 to 24, you can scan the QR code on the box to unlock the augmented reality experience, with new video drops daily.

“The hot Advent calendar with the five-year-olds who can’t get the Needoh calendar is the Squishmallow calendar, so that’s what I’m buying for my daughter this year,” says NBC Selected commerce editor Bethany Heitman. “As a mom, I appreciate that the smaller-sized stuffies will be easy to contain and don’t add a ton more clutter to our playroom, and my daughter will love seeing which cute character she gets each day.”

This Advent calendar comes with 24 itty bitty Squishmallows stuffies that are 2.5 inches tall. Your recipient gets to collect characters like Junie the Banana, James the Fox, Cam the Cat and Benny the Bigfoot decked out in their holiday apparel.

BETA We can help you find

Papier’s Advent calendar is as beautiful as it is useful. There’s 24 days worth of desk accessories inside, all of which are items you likely use every day at the office, home or school, like pens, journals, sticky tabs, highlighters, to-do notepads and stationary sets. Each item is individually wrapped in a paper box, which really makes it feel like you’re opening a gift every day. The Advent calendar, which folds open on the top and has three drawers, is designed to be a reusable organizer. Papier is also selling a 12-Day Advent Calendar for the first time this year.

There are 12 Voluspa mini coconut wax candles inside this Advent calendar, each of which comes in a decorative glass votive. You’ll collect candles in a few of the brand’s bestselling scents, like white cypress, forbidden fig and santal vanille, as well as some holiday-specific fragrances like Gingerbread Chalet. The Advent calendar comes with a gold-plated wick trimmer, too.

Anyone who thinks gifting candles is overdone clearly doesn’t know about Baobab Collection. These candles are not just things to make your space smell good: They also offer one-of-a-kind decor that will always be a conversation piece when you host. This 24-day Advent calendar is the ultimate gift — and it’s priced that way.

“You could keep half of the items for yourself and gift the other half to twelve people you love, and everyone would be so happy,” says NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans. “I don’t even celebrate Christmas and I want this because I am absolutely in love with this brand’s offerings. Everything it makes looks exquisite and luxe, and yes, the candles smell divine.” You get candles — some that are calendar exclusives — along with hand creams, shower gels and home sprays.

There’s a handful of candle Advent calendars out there, but Yankee Candle fans will only have eyes for this one. It comes with 12 1.3-ounce candles made from a soy wax blend, and the fragrances are all bestsellers like Pink Sands, Vanilla Cupcake, Sparkling Cinnamon, Spiced Pumpkin and Christmas Cookie.

Best chocolate and candy Advent calendars

Even Swedish candy makers are getting in on the Advent calendar game. Socketbit’s has drawers packed with tasty gummies, letting you sample some of the brand’s most beloved options, all of which NBC Selected commerce editor Mili Godio says are addicting. “I had a Swedish candy phase a few years ago and never looked back — at this point, I’ve tried several dozens of sweet and sour candies from countless brands,” she says. “Sockerbit quickly became one of my favorites. Its mixed candy is perfectly curated, and I specifically love the sour candies because they’re actually sour, unlike some brands that don’t even scrape the sour surface.”

Compartés’ Nutcracker and Winter Forest Advent calendars are back this year, plus the brand added a brand new one: the Enchanted Castle Advent calendar. There’s 24 chocolates inside, and each one has a different filling, like buttered croissant, espresso toffee, pistachio marzipan, cinnamon sugar donut and salted honeycomb. The calendar starts shipping on November 2.

There’s plenty of candy-filled Advent calendars to choose from if you or your loved one don’t eat chocolate. Sugarfina’s is packed with the brand’s gummies, like sugared cranberries, sour rainbow bears, heavenly sours and magic mangos, plus there’s caramel and cereal balls. You get four pieces of candy per drawer for 24 days. Sugarfina is also selling a 12-day Advent calendar this year, as well as a Peanuts themed one.

There are also seasonal candies inside, including green apple marshmallow Christmas trees, milk chocolate Santa’s helpers, gingerbread man lollipops and fruity gummy snowflakes.

Opening the See’s Candy Advent calendar is the best way to try a variety of the brand’s chocolates and confections. There’s about a pound of sweets hidden inside the box’s drawers, including dark chocolate peppermint patties, chocolate lollypops, dark chocolate marshmallow trees and milk chocolate almond caramels. The box is also decorated with a storybook scene that has 3D illustrations and foil accents, so it’s worth displaying at home.

Swedish candy company BonBon’s Advent calendar is filled with 24 individually-wrapped, numbered mini bags of candy — you eat them in order leading up to the holiday. Some of customers’ favorite sweets are included, in addition to 13 never-before-released candies.

Snack on a Ferrero confection each day leading up to the holidays with this calendar — you can save them for dessert, but I believe that chocolate compliments any meal (or activity). There are three types of treats inside: a hazelnut milk chocolate Ferrero Rocher, a creamy coconut Raddaello and a rich dark chocolate Rondnoir.

Best beauty Advent calendars

L’Occitane’s Advent calendar is filled with 24 of the brand’s bestselling skin, body, hand and hair care products, many of which come highly recommended by NBC Selected commerce editor Cory Fernandez. “I love just about everything from L’Occitane, and it’s not only because everything smells amazing,” he says. “The products are also effective — they don’t have a greasy residue and don’t dry my skin or hair. Also, the Advent calendar is great because everything is the perfect sample size.”

This holiday season, you’ll get to unbox L’Occitane’s hand creams, shower oil, exfoliating shower gel, fragrance and more, some of which are scented with the brand’s signature almond fragrance.

This is the ideal Advent calendar for the person who never leaves home without lip balm and has one in every bag they own. There’s 12 Burt’s Bees lip balms inside in flavors like sugar cookie, cinnamon apple crisp, vanilla bean and peppermint bark, the latter of which is exclusive to Amazon. The lip balms are all made with beeswax and vitamin E to soften and hydrate skin for up to 24 hours, according to the brand.

The Glow Recipe Advent calendar is filled with 12 skin care finds, including the brand’s watermelon glow products, like the niacinamide drops, BHA toner and moisturizers. It also comes with multiple toner pads, a cleanser, a lip treatment and other products to help brighten and hydrate the skin, which is key heading into the winter months.

Some of Charlotte Tilbury’s most beloved makeup and skin care products are hidden inside this treasure chest-shaped Advent calendar’s drawers. You get 15 items in total, four of which are full-size, including the Matte Revolution Lipstick and Hollywood Beauty Light Wand Highlighter in Pillow Talk, the Unreal Blush Healthy Glow Stick and a Lip Cheat Contour Duo. For the first time this year, the brand added two accessories to the calendar: a gua sha tool and a velvet makeup bag.

Expand your lineup of Laneige skin care beyond the Lip Sleeping Mask with the K-beauty brand’s Advent calendar, which is filled with 12 products in full and mini sizes. You get the lip mask, of course, as well as face masks to put on before bed, moisturizer, cleanser, serums and lip balms. Laneige says the products are formulated with ingredients like peptides, hyaluronic acid and ceramides to help hydrate, plump and nourish skin.

Ulta only put the absolute best of its offerings inside this 25 Days of Beauty Advent calendar, which comes with 31 products total. You’ll get nine full-size products, including a set of Glamnetic Press-On Nails, The Ordinary’s Multi-Active Delivery Essence and NYX Professional Makeup Butter Gloss. The rest of the skin care, hair care, nail care, makeup and fragrances are mini- and travel-size from brands like Amika, Morphe, Tarte, Osea and Peach & Lily.

You may pay $250 for Dermstore’s Advent calendar, but there’s $1,147 worth of skin care, hair care and makeup inside. You’ll get to try mini versions of products from brands like Korres, PCA Skin, Oribe and Dr. Dennis Gross, as well as numerous full-size items from Morccanoil, Paula’s Choice, Tarte and Elemis.

I’ve used Kiehl’s Ultra Facial Cream for years, but I haven’t ventured out and tested many of the brand’s other products — its Advent calendar is the perfect opportunity to do so. There’s 24 customer favorites inside, including three full-size items, three travel-size items and 18 minis. By the end of the month, you’ll open a full Kiehl’s skin care routine complete with cleansers, serums, treatments, moisturizers, eye creams, hair care and body care.

Best hair care Advent calendars

Kitsch’s 12-day Advent calendar helps you refresh your collection of hair care and styling products. You get full-size items, most notably the brand’s beloved silk pillowcase — I own about six of them and sleep on one every night to protect my curls. The Advent calendar also includes clips, scrunches, a bonnet, hair perfume and shampoo and conditioner bars. There’s also two dermaplaning products for your face: dermaplaners and oil.

The glitzy, glamorous hair accessories in Conair’s Advent calendar are exactly what you need to dress up any look, especially during the holiday season. It comes with 24 products, including bobby and hair pins, ponytail holders, claw clips and a scrunchie with a bow on it. You also get salon clips to help with skin care and makeup application, and a 2-in-1 mini boar slick back brush and taming wand.

Best nail Advent calendars

You get $316 worth of nail salon-quality products for $139 with this Advent calendar from Manucurist. It comes with 24 full-size products, like eight quick-drying polishes that have a gel-like finish and three polishes that can go on bare nails without needing a base or top coat. Nail and hand care essentials are also included, like a file, cuticle oil and cream, plus a jar of gold glitter.

Olive & June’s Advent calendar will upgrade your at-home manicures with 11 exclusive and previously sold out full-size nail polishes in a rainbow of shades. It also comes with two types of top coats: Sparkle Fairy Top Coat, which has an iridescent effect to it, and Long-Lasting Top Coat, which has a glossy finish.

If you prefer a gel mani but want to do it yourself without the UV or LED light, Dazzle Dry’s Advent calendar is calling your name. It comes with everything you need to prep, paint, finish and touch up your nails, and directions that tell you which order to use all the products in. You get two exclusive full-size nail polish shades, as well as two sparkly minis. The polish is quick-drying and lasts for up to two weeks, according to the brand.

Best wine and spirits Advent calendars

Each of VineBox’s Advent calendars comes with 3.4-ounce sampler bottles of wine from across the world, and you get an insert with tasting notes and food pairing recommendations, a limited-edition art print and access to sommelier-led virtual tasting videos. So you could essentially host your own wine tastings at home.

Vinebox sells three Advent calendars: the 12 Nights Velvet Collection, which comes with eight reds and four whites; the 12 Nights Vine Collection, which comes with six reds, one rosé and five distinctive wines; and the 24 Nights of Wine, which comes with all the wines in the Velvet and Vine collections.

The 12 canned wines in this Advent calendar come from small-batch female- and minority-led wineries, and they have zero grams of sugar, according to the brand. The cans are each equivalent to about one-third of a bottle, giving you about two glasses to share with someone or enjoy yourself. You get a mix of red, white, rosé and sparkling wines, plus a guide that provides links with in-depth information about each type. The calendar ships November 6.

In Good Taste releases numerous wine Advent calendars every year, and it just debuted a Wine Cocktail Advent Calendar for the first time. There are 24 ready-to-drink wine-based cocktails inside, including an espresso martini, piňa colada, mimosa, mojito and cosmopolitan. You get a 6-ounce serving of each one, as well as daily videos that pair with drinks so you can learn about tasting notes, food pairing suggestions and tips for garnishing.

Straightaway’s Advent calendar comes with 12 pre-made canned cocktails, so you don’t need to be a mixologist to enjoy a margarita, whisky sour, Manhattan or gimlet at home this holiday season. Just crack open an 3.4-ounce can, sip directly out of it or pour it into a glass and add ice. This is the third year the brand is selling an Advent calendar, and it added three brand-new beverages for 2026 customers.

Best coffee and tea Advent calendars

Instead of drinking the same type of coffee every morning, mix it up around the holidays with this Advent calendar. It comes with 24 K-Cups from brands like Caribou Coffee, Green Mountain Coffee Roasters, The Original Donut Shop and Peets, which you can pop into any compatible single-serve machine. In addition to standard, flavored and seasonal coffee pods, you also get hot cocoa and latte pods.

No coffee maker? No problem. Cometeer’s coffee concentrate pods come frozen, and to turn one into a cup of joe, you just melt it with hot water. You can also melt the coffee in its capsule by leaving it in the refrigerator or at room temperature, and pour it over iced water to make iced coffee, or over hot or cold milk to make a latte. Cometeer’s Advent calendar comes with 24 pods from a handful of roasters the brand works with, like Birch, Joe Coffee and Red Bay Coffee. There are rare blends, single-origin roasts and festive holiday varieties. You have to store the calendar in the freezer to keep the pods frozen throughout the month.

There’s 24 2-ounce packets of single-origin beans behind the doors of this Advent calendar, each of which makes about 24 ounces of pour-over coffee. You’ll get to try a new type of coffee every day from December 1 to Christmas Eve, so each one tastes a little different and you can learn about your preferences. In addition to the beans, you’ll get a custom 500-piece puzzle, access to Onyx’s web game and daily brew guides that share information about the coffee you’re drinking, recipes and stories from the Onyx team.

Tea Forte is known for its pyramid-shaped tea sachets, which lets the tea leaves unfurl and steep properly, making your beverage more flavorful and aromatic, according to the brand. There’s 24 sachets in this Advent calendar, including varieties like harvest apple spice, English breakfast, pumpkin spice and Belgian mint. Tea Forte also sells other Advent calendars that come with different types of tea: Winter Chalet (12 days), Warming Joy Herbal (24 days), Volaré (12 days) and Demoiselle (12 days).

This is the only Advent calendar on my list that’s filled with loose leaf tea rather than tea bags, giving you more control over how you make and enjoy it. The teas are packed in 10-gram tins, enough for a single cup, and come in flavors like blooming rose, turmeric chamomile, mint melody and original chai.

Restock your supply of Twinings tea with the brand’s Advent calendar, which covers the 24 days leading up to the holidays but is packed with double the amount of sachets — there are two behind every door, so you can sip one in the morning and keep one for your evening wind down. You get black green and herbal teas, including flavors like gingerbread joy, lemon and ginger, winter spice and lady grey.

Best food Advent calendars

There are 24 all-butter shortbread cookies inside Walker’s Advent calendar, which takes care of dessert (at least somewhat) prior to the holidays. They come in six different shapes and flavors, like shortbread fingers, rounds, hearts and stars, as well as chocolate chip and salted caramel square cookies.

As far as I’m concerned, Fishwife is responsible for making tinned fish a cool ingredient to snack on and add to meals, not something you ignore at the grocery store. The brand launched its first Advent calendar this year, which is filled with multiple cans of tinned fish, like smoked salmon, sardines, tuna and mussels. There’s also a handful of other surprises, like fish-shaped moisturizers from a collaboration with Bag Balm and a mini jar of hot sauce.

Baking cookies around the holidays is a tradition for many, and Williams Sonoma’s Advent calendar comes with lots of the supplies you need to whip up and package a batch. There’s 24 items inside, including cookie and biscuit cutters, piping bags, stencils, decorating tips, gift bags and spatulas.

Best Advent calendars for kids

After kids open all the doors of Magna-Tiles’ Advent calendar, they’ll be able to use the pieces to build a train that runs along a built-in track and create characters ready to board. It comes with exclusive figures you can mix and match the pieces of, as well as 10 decorated square blocks and three decorated triangle blocks.

The Miffy lover in your life will look forward to finding out what stickers they’ll get from this Advent calendar leading up to the holidays. It comes with 12 sticker sheets; the recipient can use them on notebooks, toys, their clothes and coloring book pages.

Your little scientist will have 24 days of hands-on activities to do in December with this Advent calendar. It comes with 13 kits for mini experiments and 11 specimens to study, like fossils and gemstones. And on Christmas Eve, they’ll get an extra special surprise: a sparkly piece of fool’s gold.

Kids will take extra pride in decorating their Christmas tree with the ornaments inside this Advent calendar, which they can make themselves. Each day, they’ll open a pack of materials and directions that teach them how to put together the final product. The ornaments they create all move: For example, the reindeer ornament flops forward, the polar bear ornament throws a snowball and the snowglobe ornament has falling flurries. KiwiCo says the calendar is best for kids age 5 and older.

Best Advent calendars for pets

If your dog could talk they might agree that the 24 treats packed inside Wufers’ Advent calendar are as tasty as they are beautifully decorated. They come in festive shapes and when you open the calendar, it starts playing “Jingle Bells.”

Bark’s Advent calendar is packed with 24 goodies for your dog. They’ll get 16 treats and eight plush toys, including those with squeakers, crinkle-textured fabric and strong hairs to prevent shredding.

Make playtime more exciting for your cat during the holidays with Chewy’s Frisco Advent calendar, which gives them 12 new toys to swat, kick, scratch and chase. They’ll get plush toys stuffed with silvervine and catnip, springs, plastic balls with bells, crinkle balls, feather teasers and more. There’s also a version for small dogs, which includes squeaky plush toys and several balls for them to play with.

The 24 dog treats that come in this Advent calendar are likely the fanciest ones your pup will ever be offered. They’re made in small batches with natural, human-grade ingredients, and come shaped like bones, truffles and macarons. The treats are decorated with festive “frosting” and “sprinkles,” too.

How I picked the best Advent calendars of 2026

To recommend the best Advent calendars, I researched highl -rated options across major categories like chocolate and candy, coffee and tea, food, wine and beauty. Every option on my final list comes from a brand we’ve previously covered or have personally tried. Some of the calendars were also sent to us as courtesy samples from brands or ones we bought with our own money.

To evaluate each one, I assessed its contents, price and packaging. Our list includes options that countdown the 12, 24 and 25 days before a holiday.

Why trust NBC Selected?

I’m a reporter at NBC Selected, where I’ve been writing gift guides for more than six years. I’ve specifically covered Advent calendars for the past four years. For this article, I compiled a list of the best Advent calendars of 2026, including highly-rated options, NBC Selected reader favorites and ones our team tested.

World.title: Princess Kate announces she's in remission from cancer
World.content:
Catherine, the Princess of Wales, said Tuesday her cancer is in remission, about 10 months after announcing her diagnosis. Princess Kate made the announcement on social media after visiting the London hospital where she received treatment.

"It is a relief to now be in remission and I remain focused on recovery," she said in her post on Instagram after visiting the Royal Marsden Hospital in London. "As anyone who has experienced a cancer diagnosis will know, it takes time to adjust to a new normal."

The princess had announced last March that cancer was discovered following an abdominal surgery and she was undergoing preventative chemotherapy.

In September, she said she had finished chemotherapy. She spoke about receiving the cancer treatment during her visit Tuesday. "It's really tough,'' she said, according to the Associated Press. "It's such a shock."

Kate spoke with patient Katherine Field about the chemotherapy port that's used to deliver the treatment, saying, "I got so attached to it," and joking that she was almost reluctant to have it removed, according to the AP.

Catherine, Princess of Wales, talks with Katherine Field as she visits The Royal Marsden hospital on Jan. 14, 2025, in London. Chris Jackson/Pool via Reuters

On social media Tuesday, Kate said she visited the hospital to thank the staff "for looking after me so well during the past year."

"My heartfelt thanks goes to all those who have quietly walked alongside William and me as we have navigated everything," she said, referring to her husband, the Prince of Wales. "We couldn't have asked for more. The care and advice we have received throughout my time as a patient has been exceptional."

Britain's Catherine, Princess of Wales, waves following a visit to the Royal Marsden Hospital in west London on Jan. 14, 2025. Chris Jackson/Pool/AFP via Getty Images

Kensington Palace also announced that she and William have become patrons of the hospital.

"My hope is, that by supporting groundbreaking research and clinical excellence, as well as promoting patient and family wellbeing, we might save many more lives, and transform the experience of all those impacted by cancer," Kate said on social media.

Since 2007, William has held the role of the hospital's president. His mother, Princess Diana, also held that position, according to the palace. The hospital is known as a world-leading cancer center with three sites in London.

Kate spoke with other patients as well as doctors and nurses during Tuesday's visit, according to Britain's Press Association news agency.

"The body is amazing at telling us 'you need to take time out,'" she said after learning about a man's diagnosis.

Catherine, Princess of Wales, visits The Royal Marsden hospital on Jan. 14, 2025, in London. Chris Jackson/Pool via Reuters

She also talked about receiving her cancer diagnosis, according to the news agency.

"It's the uncertainty of that initial diagnosis," she said. "It's such a wealth of information. Understanding the diagnosis, it's a massive amount of information to take on as a patient. Having that continuity, in the clinical setting and outside in the home setting, is so important."

World.title: Britain's Princess Kate climbs 3 mountains in 24 hours for charity
World.content:
London - Catherine, the Princess of Wales, has completed the U.K.'s National Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest peaks in Scotland, England and Wales in 24 hours, to raise awareness and money for a cancer charity.

Kate, as the 44-year-old royal is commonly known, was diagnosed with an unspecified form of cancer in March 2024. She announced in early 2025 that she was in remission after undergoing chemotherapy.

In a social media post on Sunday, Kate and Prince William's official home, Kensington Palace, said the Princess of Wales had undertaken the climb not just for the physical challenge, but also "as a chance to explore life beyond diagnosis and to give something back."

Catherine, the Princess of Wales, hiked up the U.K.'s three tallest mountains in 24 hours to raise awareness and money for a cancer charity. @princeandprincessofwales/Instagram

The National Three Peaks Challenge involves hiking up Ben Nevis in Scotland, Scafell Pike in England, and Mount Snowdon in Wales - a total of 23 miles and 10,052 feet of ascent - in 24 hours. Hiking all three also requires 462 miles of driving to get between the peaks.

Kate undertook the challenge in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, an organization connected to the hospital where Kate received her treatment.

"Through this challenge, I want to raise awareness for the deeper impact of serious illness and the importance of holistic healthcare," Kate said. "The journey through and beyond treatment requires more than medicine alone."

According to the charity, holistic cancer care integrates physical, emotional, spiritual and social well-being alongside traditional medical treatments such as chemotherapy. "Healing, whether personal or collective, is not just about fixing what is wrong. It is about finding balance in how we live, between effort and acceptance," Kate said.

The princess carried out the challenge alone but received support along the route from Britain's Mountain Rescue charity. At the end, she was greeted by her husband Prince William, who is heir to the throne, and their children Prince George, Prince Louis and Princess Charlotte, as well as her parents and brother.

Writing about her own experience with cancer diagnosis, Kate said in the social media post that hundreds of thousands of people every year hear the words that "no one wants to hear." "What follows is a path that tests every part of who we are: physically, emotionally, psychologically and spiritually," she said, adding that it impacts everything around them, including "the quiet moments we spend alone with our thoughts."

Kate paused her public engagements after receiving her cancer diagnosis to focus on the treatment, but she has begun returning to public life since announcing that she was in remission last year.

In May 2026, she carried out her first overseas trip since the diagnosis was revealed, visiting northern Italy.

World.title: Kicker with knee cancer beats the odds to resume pro sports career
World.content:
Henry Nell's career pushed his body to the limit. He played rugby professionally in his home country of South Africa. Then he moved to the United States and began playing arena football, an indoor version of American football played on a slightly smaller field. He played for multiple teams across two leagues, always serving as the kicker.

In 2021, he began to feel some stiffness in his knee. Nell brushed it off as a strained muscle. When it didn't go away, he assumed it was a sign of aging. But in 2025, when he was playing for the Albany Firebirds, the team trainer recommended an X-ray.

The scan showed a mass behind his knee. Nell tried to convince himself that it was just a cyst or a pocket of fluid. But it was diagnosed as parosteal osteosarcoma — a rare, slow-growing type of bone cancer. The tumor had been growing for years, doctors said.

Hearing the word "cancer" wasn't the scariest part, Nell said. The terror came when he met with a local oncologist, who recommended amputation.

Henry Nell plays for the Orlando Pirates. Shivonie Ross/SD School Photography

"I felt like, nothing could get better, like everything's caving in. My sports career is in jeopardy. My whole rest of my life is in jeopardy," Nell recalled. "If we have to amputate the leg, what's the next 60, 70 years of my life going to be? What effect does that have on my family? Is my wife going to push me in a wheelchair? All these thoughts ran through my head. It was one of the most frightening times I've ever experienced."

A second opinion and a complex plan



Nell and his wife, a physical therapist, wanted a second opinion. They traveled to New York City to meet with Dr. Nicola Fabbri, a surgical oncologist and chief of the Division of Musculoskeletal Oncology Surgery at NYU Langone Health who specializes in complex limb-preserving surgeries.

Fabbri proposed a plan that could let Nell treat the cancer and keep his leg. Parosteal osteosarcoma occurs at the surface of the bone. Fabbri would remove just enough bone to ensure the tumor was gone and couldn't grow back, then support Nell's knee with cadaver bone and metal plates.

The tumor behind Henry Nell's knee. NYU Langone

"We sat down for almost an hour, and the last 10 minutes of us being there, I was just in tears," Nell recalled. "I couldn't even talk to the man. I felt so bad, but I was just crying because there was hope."

Fabbri felt sure he could help Nell keep his leg, but wasn't sure about his athletic career. The surgical plan posed a risk to two important ligaments: the anterior cruciate ligament, or ACL, and posterior cruciate ligament, or PCL. Removing the necessary bone and tissue could damage them, Fabbri said. They might even need to be removed entirely.

The operation was scheduled for July 2025, three weeks after the end of Nell's season. As it neared, he hoped for the best.

"I was like, 'I might retain all my ligaments. He'll go, he'll scoop the cancer. Five hours later, we'll start our recovery process,'" Nell said. "But nothing like that actually happened."

"This has never been done before"

It took Fabbri about 11 hours to complete Nell's operation. When Nell awoke, Fabbri delivered upsetting news: He had needed to remove both ligaments to excise the cancer.

When Nell heard that, his "world shattered once more." The development "made it significantly harder to see the light at the end of the tunnel," he said.

Henry Nell after surgery. Henry Nell

The rest of Fabbri's plan had been a success. Two metal plates, 12 screws and cadaver bone were successfully supporting Nell's knee. And it was better than the amputation that had first been suggested. After his spirits recovered, Nell began to ask Fabbri about next steps. But Fabbri didn't have the answers.

"I kept asking 'Do you think I'll be able to play again? Do you think I can kick again?' And his answer was, 'You go and tell me. This has never been done before,'" Nell said. "He was like, 'If you go and do it, we can tell our next patient it's possible.'"

Six weeks after the surgery, Nell was cleared to put weight on his leg. He surrounded himself with a team that could support his recovery, which included physical therapy and strength training. Fabbri oversaw the regimen to make sure Nell wasn't pushing too hard.

The professionals estimated that it would take Nell about 18 months to regain normal day-to-day function, and wouldn't guess when he could be back on the field.

Henry Nell practices walking. Henry Nell

But within three months of surgery, Nell was doing well enough to lightly jog and kick. The small steps kept him inspired. He continued to amp up his regimen, taking careful notes with Fabbri about what he was doing and when.

Less than a year after the operation, he was well enough to return to the field with the Kansas Barrels for their season opener. The team took home a win, Nell said.

"It was a big moment in my life," Nell said. "It's something I will forever cherish."

"Leaving a legacy behind"

Nell "rarely thinks about the leg" these days. He played for the Barrels, then with the Orlando Pirates. He and his wife recently went on a hiking trip in Peru. He'll participate in another season of arena football in the spring of 2027. He is also beginning to practice rugby with a local team — "1just to see if my body can still do it."

Nell remains cancer-free, Fabbri said. Because the entire osteosarcoma was removed, the odds of recurrence are low, Fabbri said, adding that the longer Nell goes without a recurrence, the better the chance that he'll never have one.

Nell said he hopes his experience will give hope to the next person who receives a seemingly devastating diagnosis.

"In the football world, everyone talks about leaving a legacy behind, and what have you done for the game, and I've thought about that for a very long time," Nell said. "For me, it's if I can just help one person or change the life of one person that's feeling hopeless right now."

World.content:
Killer robots: U.N. talks fall short of hopes for legally binding rules

toggle caption i Efrem Lukatsky/AP

GENEVA — Diplomats meeting at the United Nations in Geneva have agreed to start discussing options to regulate lethal autonomous weapons, often called "killer robots."

After a week of negotiations that dragged on until the small hours of Saturday morning, a compromise emerged: countries would have two years to suggest regulations that could be legally binding, but could also be optional.

Bleary-eyed negotiators insisted the agreement was better than nothing and showed the U.N.'s disarmament process could still function. But for many humanitarian organizations and many countries, the deal falls far short of what they had hoped for.

Sponsor Message

Before the negotiations got underway, the International Committee of the Red Cross, the guardian of the Geneva Conventions, said it was urgent for legally binding rules to be drafted within a year. That call was backed by the U.N. secretary-general and by Pope Leo.

Their concerns stem from the kind of warfare we are now seeing. In Ukraine, Sudan and Gaza, civilians are being killed by semi-autonomous drones. This year in Sudan, 80% of civilian deaths were caused by drones according to the U.N.

Humans remain, albeit very remotely, in control for now, but humanitarian organizations fear we are on the verge of seeing artificial intelligence-assisted weapons make the decision to kill entirely on their own.

Algorithms making life-and-death decisions

"There is a fundamental ethical concern with having what are essentially these life-and-death decisions determined by programming, determined by an algorithm," said ICRC legal adviser Georgia Hinds. "That's not something that you can fix with better technology. That is a moral red line that we cannot cross."

No one went into the negotiations thinking they would be easy; some of the world's most powerful countries, among them the U.S., Russia and Israel, had already indicated their reluctance to agree to binding regulations.

Sponsor Message

On day one, Russia delayed proceedings by objecting to the meeting's agenda. Then the United States proposed a five-year window to discuss nonbinding, optional guidelines for autonomous weapons.

"They're just kicking the can down the road," said one frustrated delegate. As the clock ticked on and the weekend approached, diplomats scrambled to get some kind of result from negotiations that had been billed as a last chance to regulate weapons whose technology and decision-making capabilities we may not even fully understand.

Finally, at 4:30 a.m. on Saturday morning, they emerged from the negotiating room to announce their compromise: no to a deal within a year, maybe to legally binding rules, or maybe not.

A "nothing burger"

The ICRC immediately said it regretted the move and renewed its appeal for a binding treaty. Other campaigners were less polite, calling the deal "a real disappointment" and a "nothing burger." "I am concerned people will die because of this," added another.

A key worry is that, with two years to talk about possible rules that might only be optional, the technology will race ahead, uncontrolled.

"We're likely to see the systems proliferate," said Anna Hehir, an expert in military AI governance at the Future of Life Institute. "They're not like nuclear weapons in that they're inaccessible. There are autonomous weapons that are easy to purchase or even to create for all kinds of actors: individuals, nonstate actors, criminal groups."

There are also big questions about how our existing rules of war – the Geneva Conventions – can be upheld if those doing the killing are not humans, but machines.

"These rules are the bare minimum that militaries and states have developed and agreed to adhere to," said the ICRC's Hinds. "The commander remains responsible for making sure that the use of force is lawful. The commander remains accountable. You cannot hold a machine accountable for a violation of the law."

Sponsor Message

But in the race to develop new weapons, no country wants to come second. Although most U.N. member states do agree there should be some controls over autonomous weapons, the compromise in Geneva means that, for the next two years at least, weapons that can use artificial intelligence to make life-and-death decisions will remain unregulated.

Meanwhile, weapons technology is developing at pace, while diplomacy is struggling to keep up.

World.title: Federal jury convicts man of starting the deadly 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles
World.content:
Federal jury convicts man of starting the deadly 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles

toggle caption i Etienne Laurent/AP

LOS ANGELES — The man accused of sparking last year's deadly Palisades Fire was found guilty of arson charges Friday after his first federal case earlier this year ended in a mistrial.

Jurors convicted Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, of lighting a fire on Jan. 1, 2025, that burned undetected deep in root systems before flaring back up Jan. 7, becoming one of the most destructive wildfires in California history. The Palisades Fire killed 12 people as it incinerated entire neighborhoods in Los Angeles and Malibu.

Rinderknecht pleaded not guilty to federal charges of destruction of property by means of fire and arson. The scope of the first charge was narrowed to only include the Jan. 1 blaze, known as the Lachman Fire, and the second addresses the Palisades Fire. He was convicted on both charges.

Sponsor Message

With little apparent reaction, Rinderknecht gave his attorneys hugs before leaving the courtroom. The verdict was delivered on the third day of deliberation.

Bill Essayli, the top federal prosecutor in LA, said the verdict was a "testament of the hard work" his team put into the case. He said he was "intimately familiar" with the strength of the evidence and was happy with the jury that convicted Rinderknecht.

Rinderknecht's attorney Steve Haney said in a statement they were disappointed in the verdict but respected the jury process.

"After a lengthy deliberation, they clearly gave this case a great deal of consideration," Haney said. Regarding an appeal, he said they would review all the options at the right time.

Rinderknecht is set to be sentenced March 17, 2027. Each count carries a mandatory minimum of five years and a maximum of 20 years in federal prison.

Prosecutors continued to pursue the case after Rinderknecht's first jury deadlocked 10 to 2 in favor of acquittal after a two-week trial in June. They dropped a third charge of timber set afire when they filed a new indictment for the retrial. Essayli said he believed the first jury acted improperly and appeared to consider things in their decision that weren't presented as evidence during the trial.

Sponsor Message

Juror says Rinderknecht's own testimony pointed to a guilty verdict

toggle caption i U.S. Attorney's Office/AP

Juror No. 3, who only wanted to be identified by his first name Cameron, said he was the only person who felt Rinderknecht was not guilty at the start of deliberations. Another person was undecided, and the rest of the 10 jurors believed Rinderknecht was guilty.

"It took a lot for me to be convinced otherwise," he said. "After listening to every single point, I do now agree that he's guilty."

Cameron said he initially had concerns about a technical review conducted by a defense expert witness, who argued the government had gotten the origin area of the fire wrong. He said there was a "lack of information" presented to the jury about the technical review.

In the end, it was Rinderknecht's own testimony that was the strongest piece of evidence pointing to a guilty verdict, he said.

"Stating that he was up on the hill, didn't smell a fire, didn't see fireworks … no one else was on the hill that night," Cameron said.

Prosecutors say Rinderknecht had been 'mad at everything'

During the second trial, prosecutors presented a more tightly organized case that presented digital forensic data, expert testimony and Rinderknecht's state of mind in the hours leading up to the fire. They did not focus as much on his resentment toward the rich and powerful to present the crime as arson motivated by "societal revenge" like they previously did.

Prosecutors zeroed in on evidence placing him at the fire's origin area, such as photographs that showed his car parked at the base of a trail leading up to where the fire started and cellphone tower data pointing to his movement on the hill. Fire detection camera images showed the time window the blaze ignited, and experts eliminated any other source of ignition that night, including fireworks.

Sponsor Message

They established that Rinderknecht was acting erratic and angry in the hours leading up to the fire through the testimony of Uber passengers and texts sent to his girlfriend at the time.

"He was mad at everything, and frustrated," said Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark Williams.

After the fire began, Rinderknecht called 911 more than a dozen times as he walked down the hill. Prosecutors presented the video he screen-recorded on his phone while calling. As he was calling, he asked ChatGPT: "Are you at fault if a fire is lit because of your cigarettes?"

These were part of an alibi Rinderknecht was trying to create for himself, prosecutors said.

They also presented extensive testimony on how fire investigators determined the Palisades Fire was a holdover fire from the initial blaze Rinderknecht sparked.

Defense argues fire's origin is unproven

Haney cast doubt on the government's case, saying the fire scene could have been compromised because the area was publicly accessible until the Palisades Fire started Jan. 7.

The defense called their own expert witnesses, including a retired fire investigator for the U.S. Forest Service who argued the fire origin area was different from what the government concluded.

Prosecutors attacked the fire investigator during cross examination and at one point accused him of perjury, alleging he did not disclose all records related to the case. The judge ultimately rejected prosecutors' request to strike his testimony.

Haney argued the government could not conclusively say there was no one else by the fire ignition point that night because of missing cell data records, and pointed to a neighbor's testimony that he saw a group of teenagers running away from the direction of the trailhead.

He told jurors to disregard any evidence related to Rinderknecht's character, such as his angry text messages, because they were "evidence of the man, not evidence of the act."

Sponsor Message

Finally, Haney presented an alternate explanation for what ignited the fire — fireworks. Multiple witnesses, including two neighbors and a local firefighter, all said they heard a loud bang or explosion from the direction of the hill the fire purportedly started on.

In the thousands of images of the evening collected from cameras in the area, none showed fireworks in the sky above the hill where the fire started, prosecutors said.

World.title: Perspective: Defining 'human'
World.content:
Perspective: Defining 'human'

toggle caption i Andreea Alexandru/AP

The Cambridge Dictionary has revealed its Word of the Year for 2026. It won't need much explanation. Unlike "parasocial," their 2025 word, which refers to an unreciprocated emotional connection, perhaps with a chatbot, or 2018's word, "nomophobia," which is an irrational fear of having no mobile phone service–although, given all the recent cyber-struggles, why would that be irrational?

The Cambridge 2026 World of the Year is … human. As in us. And perhaps humanity could stand some recognition in times when people see Artificial Intelligence seep into our lives the way ancient dinosaurs may have watched the asteroid plunge through the atmosphere, and think, "They're coming for us!" though I suspect a few T-Rexes might have said, "Hey, don't worry! We're too big to fail!"

Sponsor Message

Cambridge defines "human" as: "(h)aving the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines," but they don't specify much about what those qualities, faults and feelings are.

I'd say that humans have a sense of responsibility. We can say, "I'm sorry, that's my fault," when we screw up or fall short, as opposed to screens that just flash, SYSTEM OVERLOAD or UPDATE IN PROGRESS, 12% COMPLETE.

Humans seek joy, not just continued existence. Laughter, tears, love, spice, poetry, and all that jazz, not just code or text. Humans like jokes and prayers. We're driven by feelings, not just steered by algorithms. Love, fear, anger, desire, joy, and courage, excited by events, nerves and hormones – combine to make us unpredictable, irreverent and unreliable. But our experiences can also instill judgement; an appreciation for what's important; what endures; and what makes the lives we have worth living and savoring.

Making human the 2026 Word of the Year may remind us that we human beings, unlike any robots we have yet devised, have a sense of our own fragility. We know we don't last forever. And so it is important to strive, laugh, and love while we have the chance. The Cambridge dictionary leaves what human truly means to us.
