World.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
World.content:
A deal covering 730 million people promises lower tariffs and new investment opportunities as the European Union seeks to diversify trade ties amid growing global economic tensions.

The European Union and Indonesia signed a free trade deal on Saturday, describing it as a new chapter in economic relations between the two sides.

"This is one of the most ambitious deals the European Union has concluded in Asia," Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission, said at the signing ceremony on Saturday.

"Together, we represent a market of 730 million people," she added.

The Indonesia-European Union Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) and the additional Investment Protection Agreement (IPA) are designed to reduce trade barriers and attract investment in strategic sectors such as electric vehicles, electronics, and pharmaceuticals.

The agreement comes after almost 10 years of negotiations and is part of a wider series of trade deals by the EU.

'Keeping the doors open when others are closing theirs'

The bloc hopes to reduce its reliance on individual economic partners as trade with both China and the US has become more difficult in recent years.

Von der Leyen also stressed the importance of international cooperation, saying that "in a time when others are closing their doors, we keep ours open."

In 2025, von der Leyen met with Indonesian President Pabowo Subianto to work on the agreement Image: Laily Rachev - Biro Pers Sekretariat Presiden

The deal sees tariffs on about 98% of EU exports to Indonesia to be done away with. The EU estimates that European companies could save more than €600 million (around €658 million) per year.

"The benefits for our exporters are concrete and measurable," Indonesian Minister of Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto said, hailing a "new chapter" in economic relations with the EU. He said the deal would benefit his country’s main exports to Europe, including palm oil, footwear and textiles.

Palm oil and deforestation had been major stumbling blocks during the negotiations, and the agreement includes mechanisms for cooperation on regulatory and sustainability issues as well as a dedicated protocol on palm oil to address environmental concerns.

The EU parliament is now expected to greenlight the deal while Indonesian authorities will also complete the ratification process so it can enter into force in 2027.

World.title: New EU budget proposal aims at tax gobal tech giants
World.content:
European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected the plan as inadequate.

European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a new draft for the next EU budget .

Among other things, he is suggesting a tax on big tech firms to ease the contributions of member states, some of which strongly criticised earlier proposals.

The EU budget is theEuropean Union’s shared budget and it is used for things ranging from agricultural subsidies, infrastructure projects to border control and defence.

A first draft for the 2028 to 2034 budget was proposed by the EU Commission in 2025 but was criticised, especially by a group of northern European members including Germany who wanted the budget to be much smaller.

Following that criticism, the European Council President has now suggested a new draft, which is smaller by €204 billion.

But divisions among member states appear to remain, with France immediately coming out against Costa’s new draft, saying it was "deeply disappointing."

The EU budget also covers financial aid for Ukraine Image: Hans Lucas/AFP/Getty Images

What’s the plan for the tech tax?

The proposal includes a string of new "revenue channels," explicitly intended to "to keep national contributions at a reasonable level," so that member state will have to contribute less than otherwise would be the case.

The biggest splash would likely come from a tax on companies with an annual turnover from digital activities of at least 50 million euros in the EU and 750 million euros worldwide.

Those firms would be subject to "an annual contribution corresponding to 3% of the annual net turnover from online advertising, digital intermediation services and user-generated data," according to Costa.

Aside from the tech tax, the "balanced basket of new own resources" also includes taxes on tobacco products and electronic waste.

What happens next?

Neither the EU Commission nor European Council President Costa will have the final word on the budget. Costa's plan will now be at the centre of hours of talks when EU leaders meet in Brussels next week.

"This is a realistic budget that addresses our new priorities while preserving our established policies," Costa wrote about his proposal. "I am confident that this proposal is a good basis for moving towards a final agreement."

But an initial reaction from France suggests that any final agreement might still be some way off.

The French presidency said the budget "falls well short ​of ‌what is needed, particularly on ‌the Common Agricultural Policy, ‌notably ​to guarantee income support for farmers."

"As it ⁠stands, ​this proposal ​from the President ​of the European ‌Council does not ​provide ⁠a basis for an ⁠agreement."

The EU was hoping to reach a general agreement on the budget by the end of 2026 with its formal adoption planned for 2027.

World.title: Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2
World.content:
The attacks follow Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks this week on the Kerch Bridge, linking Russian-occupied Crimea.

Russian ballistic missile strikes on Ukraine's southern city of Kryvyi Rih — President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown — killed two people and wounded dozens of others, local officials said Saturday.

The attacks come amid little progress in talks to end the nearly five-year-old war and after Ukraine, on three occasions this week, struck the Kerch bridge linking Russian-occupied Crimea with Russia.

Russian President Vladimir Putin had vowed a "painful" response to the Kerch attack, as the bridge is vital for war supplies for Russian forces in the south.

Russia intensifies aerial attacks on Ukraine To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

What do we know?

Among the dead in Friday evening's double-tap strikes on Kryvyi Rih were a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman, while several children were among the 60 wounded, the Ukrainian officials said.

Several fires broke out and damage was caused to about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and an industrial facility, Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of the city administration, wrote on Telegram.

Moscow, meanwhile, confirmed a further strike on Friday night in Kryvyi Rih.

Russia's Defense Ministry said a thermal power plant in the city was hit, along with a power substation in the region of Rivne, on the opposite side of the country.

Both facilities supply electricity to the industry supporting Ukraine's military, the ministry added.

Kryvyi Rih has been hit several times by Russia during the war Image: Press service of the National Police of Ukraine/Handout/REUTERS

What are the other latest developments?

Elsewhere in the nearly five-year-long war, Russia ​also struck a ​cargo vessel ‌near Odesa, which Moscow said was carrying dual-use goods ​for ⁠the Ukrainian military.

Eleven people, including two children, were wounded when a Russian drone attacked a five-story apartment building in the northeastern Kharkiv region, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said Saturday.

One person was wounded in a Russian attack on the capital, Kyiv, according to the service.

In Russia, local officials said Saturday that Ukrainian drone attacks wounded three people in the Bryansk and Belgorod border regions.

Finland, meanwhile, said it detected a drone attack on Saturday morning on a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea, prompting Prime Minister Petteri Orpo to warn that the war is "spilling over into our immediate vicinity."

After damage to Russia's Kerch bridge to Crimea, Zelenskyy warned in an interview with US broadcaster NBC that the structure "will not remain standing anyway."

World.title: Germany's religious freedom report: Authoritarian regimes, holy wars, and spies abroad
World.content:
Harassment, persecution, surveillance: Across much of the world, people of faith are facing growing pressure. A new German government report is unusually direct in criticizing China in particular.

The report spans more than 150 pages, but its conclusion can be summed up in a single sentence: "The global situation regarding freedom of religion and belief deteriorated during the reporting period," said Thomas Rachel, the German government's commissioner for freedom of religion and belief, and a member of parliament for the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU). Recently adopted by the Cabinet, the government's fourth report on the subject covers developments from 2023 to 2025.

The government has issued a dedicated report on freedom of religion and belief around the world. According to the report, this freedom is facing "increasing pressure" globally. The focus is not primarily on the suppression of religious institutions or structures, but on the situation of individuals who hold a religious belief, or none at all.

Faith in the Digital Age To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Authoritarian regimes increase pressure on religious communities

The importance of religious freedom is reflected in the way the government commissioner describes the issue: "Religion and faith are of great importance to four out of five people around the world and are central to their identity. People wake up with God and go to sleep with God. It is part of their everyday lives." Research by the Pew Research Center suggests that about 84% of the world's population identifies with a certain religion.

At a time when authoritarian regimes are gaining ground and expanding their surveillance capabilities, the report paints a bleak picture. The growing number of violent conflicts, the rise of authoritarian rule, and the spread of populism have led to "painful restrictions on freedom of religion and belief around the world."

The German government report does not attempt to provide a statistical tally of attacks or the number of people facing persecution. Instead, it examines 30 countries as case studies where, in the federal government's view, freedom of religion and belief is being restricted. These include about six countries each from Africa, Asia, and the Arab world. In Europe, the report focuses on Belarus, Russia, Ukraine, and Turkey, while in Latin America it highlights Mexico, Nicaragua, and Cuba. It also identifies shortcomings in five of the world's six most populous countries: China, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, and Nigeria.

India: Hindu nationalists force religious conversions To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Regarding India, the report refers to "Hindu nationalist efforts" that threaten the equal treatment of all officially recognized religions. It states that the generally peaceful coexistence of different faiths is "repeatedly overshadowed by tensions and, at times, violence." Both Muslim and Christian communities report growing intolerance and hate speech. According to the report, violent Hindu extremist groups have carried out a "large number of physical attacks" against Muslims, while the police and government authorities often respond inadequately.

In China, the German government identifies a "significant tightening of the legal framework of state control at the expense of freedom of religion and belief." According to the report, this particularly affects Uyghurs, Tibetans, and churches that lack official state approval and are subject to harsh measures by the authorities. The law on the "Promotion of Ethnic Unity and Progress," which came into force on July 1, 2026, subordinates religion to "the formation of national identity" and patriotic education.

One of the countries where the situation has deteriorated most dramatically is Nicaragua, which has severely restricted freedom of religion and belief since 2018. The repression has primarily targeted the Catholic Church. According to the report, "intimidation, persecution, imprisonment, and expulsion" have forced around 130 priests and nuns to leave the country.

Exploring Africa's indigenous religions To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The reports reserves some of its sharpest criticism for Kirill, the patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church. Under his leadership, the church has strongly supported Russia's war against Ukraine and portrayed it as a "holy war." According to the report, "weapons are blessed, Russian soldiers are absolved of their sins, and donations are collected for the war." It is perhaps the clearest example in the report of how religion can be used to justify oppression and violence.

Intimidation reaches beyond borders

The report explicitly addresses the threat posed by "transnational repression" (TNR), which it describes as a "growing global problem" that also affects Germany. The term refers to the persecution or intimidation of individuals by their country of origin beyond its own borders.

Ultimately, it argues, this amounts to a "continuation of domestic repression." Such "cross-border repression" has become considerably easier through the growing availability of digital means of repression, including smear campaigns on social media and spyware.

These forms of pressure range from physical attacks on individuals to digital assaults such as online intimidation and defamation. In some cases, repression is also carried out by threatening family members who remain in the country of origin. Russia and Iran, for example, are identified as the "main perpetrators of transnational repression" in Germany.

China is a particularly prominent example of religious and ideological tensions. Repression by Beijing in Germany primarily targets members of groups that the country's Communist Party classifies as "hostile to the system." These include Uyghurs, Tibetans, and members of the Falun Gong movement. According to the report, they are "also subject to surveillance and repressive measures in Germany," while relatives living in China are pressured.

Thomas Rachel hopes the newly published report will be "discussed in as many Bundestag committees as possible" and that members of parliament will "engage with the issue accordingly." Previous government reports on the subject have been debated in the Bundestag plenary at least once and, in some cases, twice.

Sweden: Hybrid warfare in a Russian Orthodox church To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Religion: A matter of German foreign policy

The issue's place within the German government has also changed during the current legislative term. Commissioner Thomas Rachel is now based at the Foreign Ministry, while both of his predecessors since 2018 were attached to the Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development. Today, Rachel says, the importance of religion is being "taken into account" in German foreign policy. He also points to his involvement in the Foreign Ministry's diplomatic training programs.

In doing so, the government led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) reversed a structural decision made by the previous center-left coalition, which was led from 2021 to 2025 by Chancellor Olaf Scholz of the Social Democratic Party (SPD). The Scholz government had reduced the issue's prominence by assigning it to the "Religion and Foreign Policy" division. Religion and foreign policy have now regained a more prominent place within government.

One example is the current foreign minister, Johann Wadephul, who has already visited the Vatican more often than his two predecessors combined. In addition, alongside Rachel, the ministry has for some time maintained a dedicated unit headed by an ambassador that deals with, among other things, "fundamental issues relating to religion and foreign policy."

World.title: COP31: UN Climate summit runs into overtime as deal remains elusive
World.content:
Skip next section Peru blames 'geopolitical divisions' for lack of COP31 progress

The head of Peru's delegation at COP31, Andres Martin Garrido Sanchez, warned that the UN climate summit was unlikely to end with a concrete deal on climate financing or cutting fossil fuel use.

Garrido Sanchez lamented that the outcome "would be very limited."

He reiterated how "geopolitical divisions" were stopping any final deal from mentioning reducing reliance on oil, gas and coal.

The Peruvian delegate singled out major oil producers, such as Gulf Arab states and Russia, as showing significant opposition.

He noted that while Latin American neighbor Panama had also signaled objection to including the term fossil fuels in the final text, Peru was "not so radical" and is keen to attract investment to "ensure our energy security" through renewables.

World.title: Anthropic researcher uses AI to solve math's greatest riddle
World.content:
The proposed breakthrough could reshape mathematical research, but still needs independent verification. It's the latest in a string of cases where AI has outpaced humans in solving famous maths problems.

A mathematician working for AI giant Anthropic says he used the company's Claude AI tool to solve one of mathematics most famous problems.

The Riemann hypothesis dates back to 1859 and centers on the distribution of prime numbers underpinning a much wider scope of mathematical work.

Levent Alpoge, a member of Anthropic's technical staff, made the announcement on his website. "I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis," Levent Alpoge wrote in a note released Friday .

The proof still has to be verified and confirmed by other mathematicians. If it withstands independent examination, it would be a major milestone both in mathematics and the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI) in scientific research.

The Riemann hypothesis is the latest and most important in a string of famous mathematical problems that were tackled with the help of AI.

What did Alpoge say about the breakthrough?

Alpoge said that the collaboration with AI had generated more than 250,000 pages of mathematical material, adding that he had not yet mastered all the mathematics involved.

"Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line," he wrote. "No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line."

AI is increasingly outpacing humans when it comes to mathematical research Image: Design Pics/IMAGO

The Riemann Hypothesis is one of seven major mathematical problems, the so-called Millennium Prize Problems , selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which offers $1 million for a solution to each of those.

"This is an announcement of historic significance," Martin Bridson, president of the institute, said in a statement quoted by news agency AP.

He added it "holds the promise of a dramatic transformation in the perception of what is possible in the struggle to extend the human understanding of mathematics."

"But the journey from today’s announcement to a place of real understanding will be long and difficult."

What is the Riemann hypothesis?

Formulated by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in the 19th century, the hypothesis is about the distribution of prime numbers, which are numbers that can only be divided by themselves and the number 1.

The hypothesis describes a fundamental pattern of how these numbers are distributed as they become ever larger. Confirming that hypothesis is thought to have crucial implications for a wide range of further mathematical research.

The potential breakthrough by Alpoge and Claude AI comes amid a growing number of examples where artificial intelligence systems are making significant contributions to advanced mathematical research.

In September, rival AI company OpenAI said its technology had helped solve a problem involving the Navier-Stokes equations.

The equations, which describe the movement of fluids such as water and air, are another of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, but the claim that they've been solved also still needs independent verification.

World.title: Germany news: Support for Ukraine military aid waning, survey shows
World.content:
Kane was named the world's best male soccer player last month Image: Karl-Josef Hildenbrand/AFP

Harry Kane, Bayern Munich's star striker, has pledged to return to the field for the important matches at the end of the current campaign after undergoing surgery for a torn ankle ligament.

"I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season," he wrote on social media above a photo of himself on his hospital bed, also thanking fans for their messages of support.

Kane, 33, was injured around 20 minutes into Bayern's 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday.

Bayern issued a statement on Saturday saying that Kane had "successfully undergone surgery" on his left ankle but was expected to be out for three to four months.

England captain Kane, who finished the 2025–26 season with over 70 goals for club and country, was awarded the Ballon d'Or for his efforts.

World.title: 'Killer robots' talks at UN end with no legally binding ban
World.content:
Countries have agreed to extend discussions over controls on lethal autonomous weapons systems for two years.

United Nations talks on regulating lethal autonomous weapons systems ended on Saturday without an agreement on a legally binding ban.

The negotiations did, however, yield an agreement for further discussions to develop new rules by 2028.

Delegates from 128 states that are parties to the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) had been meeting in Geneva since Monday amid rising concerns over the use of the so-called killer robots in global conflicts.

The conference ended early on Saturday in what campaigners deemed a "weakened" outcome, following several hours of overnight parleying.

What happened at the CCW conference?

Nearly 100 nations had called for negotiations on a legally binding agreement on the systems capable of killing without a human making the final decision to fire.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres, Pope Leo XIV and the Red Cross had also supported a ban on killer robots.

However, countries that have the technology, including arms-producing giants like the ​US, Russia ‌and Israel, were among those opposing the mandate.

Ultimately, the 128 countries "agreed to launch the elaboration of an international instrument on lethal autonomous weapons systems, which should be conducted over the next two years", the conference's Swiss chair, Julien Thoni, told the media on Saturday.

Rights groups expressed disappointment at the watered down deal Image: Fabrice Coffrini/AFP

Groups decry a softened mandate on 'killer robots'

But while Thoni hailed a multilateral diplomacy delivering "concrete results" even in "today's deeply divided world," rights groups expressed disappointment at the minimal agreement.

"States adopted a watered-down mandate that fails to chart a clear path towards a legally binding instrument," news agency AFP quoted Stop Killer Robots, a global coalition of over 300 organizations, as saying.

"Over 95 states expressed their support for a treaty. In the final hours, a small number of states weakened the mandate introducing uncertainty about the legal status of the final document," it added.

The group had earlier said that autonomous weapons systems were already reaching the battlefield and such systems had been tested or deployed, including in the Ukraine war.

World.title: La distancia entre el PP y el PSOE se estrecha al mínimo pese a la victoria de Feijóo en el debate
World.content:
Alberto Núñez Feijóo ganó con claridad, en opinión de los ciudadanos, su cara a cara con Pedro Sánchez. La encuesta de urgencia realizada por 40dB. para EL PAÍS y la SER no deja lugar a dudas: el 43% de los entrevistados señala como triunfador al líder del PP, diez puntos más de los que apuntan al socialista. Pero no todo son malas noticias para el PSOE, porque el acumulado del tracking diario de los últimos cuatro días estrecha al máximo la diferencia entre los dos grandes partidos, apenas siete décimas, equivalente a un empate técnico.

El aparente contrasentido se explica por las diferencias entre las muestras. Y por un detalle relevante: el debate, con una media de 10 millones de espectadores de audiencia, fue mucho más seguido por los votantes del PP. Un 61,5% del total de simpatizantes del primer partido de la oposición asegura que siguió el cara a cara hasta el final, mientras que entre los del PSOE baja hasta el 49%. La encuesta de urgencia fue elaborada con una muestra de 500 entrevistas en línea, recogidas entre las 23.43 horas del jueves, recién concluido el programa, hasta las 8.27 de este viernes 20. Esos datos se han incorporado hasta engrosar otro contigente mayor de 2.000 entrevistas que reflejan las intenciones de voto manifestadas en los últimos cuatro días.

En el debate, Feijóo se mostró mucho más convincente que Sánchez (47,9% frente a 38,8%) y algo más competente (43,5% frente a 40,9%). Pese a aparecer como derrotado, el actual presidente aún fue visto como más carismático que su contrincante: 46,8% frente a 39%. El duelo dialéctico fue seguido por casi tres de cada cuatro de los entrevistados, aunque no llegan a la mitad los que afirman haber asistido íntegramente

En las opiniones sobre el cara a cara pesa de modo determinante la simpatía política de los entrevistados. Entre los votantes del PP y Vox, Feijóo es visto abrumadoramente como triunfador. Sin embargo, tres de cada cuatro simpatizantes socialistas eligen a Sánchez, así como uno de cada tres del Frente Amplio (FA), la misma porción de los que manifiestan que no ganó ninguno de los dos.

Los 500 entrevistados por 40dB. tras el debate también manifestaron su intención de voto y esos resultados se incorporaron a los recogidos en los tres días anteriores hasta conformar una muestra de 2.000. Con esa perspectiva más amplia, y a pesar del revés del cara a cara, el PSOE consigue su mejor resultado no solo desde el comienzo de la campaña, sino también de toda la legislatura, en la que el instituto demoscópico ha realizado barómetros mensuales para EL PAÍS y la SER. De ese modo la diferencia entre los dos grandes partidos se reduce a siete décimas, la mitad de la ventaja que el PP logró sobre el PSOE en las anteriores elecciones de 2023. Lo que no impide que el conjunto del bloque de la derecha conserve su amplia distancia, con 189 escaños, 13 más que la mayoría absoluta.

Los socialistas ganan un punto en esta última entrega del tracking, sumarían un 31,2% y, aun con cinco décimas menos que en 2023, obtendrían tres escaños más que entonces, hasta 124. El PP, con el 31,9%, quedaría un poco por debajo de su cosecha en las anteriores elecciones y se anotaría 131 diputados, seis menos que en el Congreso saliente. Pero la tendencia general de los populares desde el inicio de la campaña apunta a una recuperación, cimentada sobre todo en el freno a las fugas hacia Vox. La encuesta incluso advierte un pequeño flujo en sentido contrario, de antiguos votantes de la extrema derecha que ahora se decantan por Feijóo.

Aun así, Vox sería la formación que más crece comparado con los anteriores comicios, casi cinco puntos, hasta situarse en el 17,1%. El Frente Amplio y las confluencias territoriales en las que participa siguen sin sumar mucho más allá del 5%, mientras que Podemos quedaría fuera del Congreso.

Descargables

World.title: ¿Cómo se mueven las encuestas? Lo que dice nuestro promedio
World.content:
El promedio de EL PAÍS se actualiza día a día, dando más peso a las mejores encuestadoras. Además, construye tu propio promedio

Se publican decenas de encuestas en una campaña. Son el mejor instrumento para predecir unas elecciones, sobre todo cuando las miramos juntas: eso hace nuestro promedio. Combina todos los estudios dando más peso a las encuestadoras que más aciertan. Ahora mismo, ese promedio sitúa al PP con el 31,2% de los votos, algo más de tres puntos por delante del PSOE (28,1%), y con Vox alrededor del 19%.

En el gráfico puedes elegir entre tres promedios. El “medio” es el que usamos habitualmente; los otros dos sirven para comparar: “agresivo” (que reacciona antes a los cambios pero tiene más ruido), y otro “cauto” (que se mueve menos).

Los sondeos se han movido desde la convocatoria del 6 de octubre. El cambio más claro es un bajón del PP que estrecha su ventaja sobre el PSOE: era de 6 puntos y ahora es de algo más de 3. Nuestros cálculos dicen que el PSOE tiene ya un 20%-25% de probabilidad de ser primero.

Algo que también ha cambiado es la izquierda del PSOE. Hoy las encuestas estiman un 6,7% de voto para lo que hemos llamado Frentes (Frente Amplio y las coaliciones con Podemos, Compromís, Ara Més o Unidad del Pueblo Canario) y un 1,3% para Podemos, que solo cuenta donde concurre en solitario. Juntos rondan el 8% de voto, lejos del 12,3% que logró Sumar en 2023.

La suma de izquierdas y derechas

El número clave de las elecciones es el resultado por bloques. Ahora mismo la derecha suma casi el 52% de los votos (PP, Vox y SALF) y la izquierda, el 37,8% (PSOE, Frentes, Podemos y Adelante Andalucía). Son casi 14 puntos de distancia, cuando en las generales de 2023 casi empataron, con 45,4% y 44% respectivamente.

La ventaja de la derecha creció entre 2024 y el verano de 2025, cuando sus votos pasaron del 48% al 52%. En campaña se ha reducido ligeramente, aunque todavía ronda los 14 puntos. Nuestra hipótesis inicial era que la izquierda, que partía desmovilizada, recuperaría terreno con la convocatoria electoral. Todavía pensamos que es la tendencia para las semanas que quedan.

El promedio también constata que las encuestadoras discrepan. Casi todas ponen al PP primero, pero con ventajas distintas: desde menos de un punto de 40dB hasta más de seis de NC Report. Solo SW Demoscopia sitúa al PSOE por delante, además del CIS. Pero el dato de este último es poco informativo porque el centro sobrestima a la izquierda desde 2018.

¿Y si corregimos los llamados sesgos? Algunas encuestadoras se desvían hacia la derecha o hacia la izquierda. Nuestro promedio no lo corrige por un motivo: esas desviaciones cambian de una elección a otra y casi nunca son sistemáticas. Pero podemos ver qué pasaría si lo hiciéramos: el siguiente gráfico permite corregir cada encuesta con el sesgo histórico de su casa.

El resultado depende de qué elecciones miramos. Con los errores de todas las elecciones desde 2018, generales y autonómicas, la ventaja del PP sobre el PSOE sube de 3,1 a 4,2 puntos: en conjunto las encuestas se han quedado cortas con la derecha. Pero en las generales ha pasado lo contrario: subestimaron a la izquierda. El caso más recordado es 2023: las últimas encuestas daban a la derecha 5,5 puntos de ventaja, y en las urnas sacó solo 1,4. Si ajustamos las encuestas con sus sesgos solo en las tres generales desde 2018, la ventaja del PP baja a 1,6 puntos, pero la suma de derechas sigue claramente por delante.

Todos estos números son tentativos. Primero, porque las encuestas son una aproximación. Y segundo, porque todavía queda una semana hasta el 29-N.

¿Cómo funciona el promedio?

Un promedio de encuestas suele ser más preciso que cualquier encuesta aislada: suma la muestra de todas y compensa en parte sus errores, porque mezcla la “cocina” de cada encuestadora. El nuestro funciona así:

1) Todas las encuestas. Usamos las de voto al Congreso publicadas desde las generales de 2023, salvo las encargadas por partidos y las que no tienen trabajo de campo propio. La mayoría las tomamos de Wikipedia.

2) Con distinto peso. Cada encuesta importa según su encuestadora, su muestra y su antigüedad. La nota de cada casa sale de nuestro comparador, que valora su error, su sesgo y si publica sus microdatos (las mejores pesan el doble que una casa normal). El peso de una encuesta se reduce a la mitad cada diez días y desaparece a los 30.

3) Cada casa cuenta una vez. De cada encuestadora pesa su último sondeo, para que no mande quien publica más.

4) Mira hacia atrás. El promedio de cada día solo usa las encuestas publicadas hasta entonces: la línea no se reescribe cuando llegan sondeos nuevos.

5) Tres ritmos. El promedio central y dos para comparar: el agresivo reduce el peso a la mitad cada 8 días y corta a los 14; el cauto, cada 30 y a los 60.

6) Las listas del 29N. Desde el 14 de octubre medimos las candidaturas nuevas, y las encuestas anteriores se traducen a ellas. SALF y Adelante Andalucía entran en el promedio poco a poco, a medida que las publican las encuestadoras.

7) El sesgo, aparte. La corrección del interactivo usa el error de cada casa en la ventaja entre bloques desde 2018, entero: enseña qué pasaría si las casas volvieran a fallar como de media.

8) El promedio es sólido, pero no infalible. Lo hemos probado con 41 elecciones desde 2018: cinco días antes de votar, falla 1,5 puntos por partido de media. Cambiar la ventana o los pesos lo mejora una décima como mucho. Cuando falla es porque fallan todas las encuestas a la vez, algo que ningún promedio puede corregir: por eso nuestro modelo añade esa incertidumbre.

Todas las encuestas

World.title: Llamadas para comprar una bici, mangos o un tratamiento para la vagina: qué pasa si la IA distribuye tu número de teléfono
World.content:
Un hombre cuenta cómo recibe llamadas con quejas y dudas de clientes de clínicas estéticas, tiendas de persianas o farmacias online después de que Gemini y ChatGPT ofrecieran su móvil por error

Una chica enfadada escribió en agosto por WhatsApp a Fernando, un ingeniero español de 39 años. Adjuntaba capturas de una farmacia online: “Han pasado ocho días desde que hice mi pedido, quiero que se me devuelva el dinero y poner una hoja de reclamaciones”. Fernando se lo tomó bien: “Entiendo que has intentado ponerte en contacto con una empresa de mensajería; yo soy un particular cualquiera”.

La chica se disculpó y le mandó una captura de una conversación con Gemini Flash, un modelo de IA de Google, donde salía el teléfono de Fernando como número de WhatsApp de la farmacia. “Coño, ese es mi número”, respondió Fernando, que prefiere no dar su apellido para que no se mezcle este problema con su trabajo ni le genere otros. “A ver qué hago ahora”, añadió.

Antes de poder pensar mucho, le escribió otra mujer un largo párrafo también en WhatsApp: “Me pongo en contacto con ustedes porque estoy interesada en recibir información y precios sobre el tratamiento de láser CO2 fraccionado vaginal para tratar la atrofia y la laxitud debido a la menopausia”. El mensaje iba acompañado del nombre y la foto de perfil de la mujer, a quien Fernando bloqueó enseguida. Luego, otro tipo le escribió buscando una “mountain bike rígida usada”, y adjuntaba su presupuesto y altura. Era un mensaje para una tienda de bicis.

Luego empezaron a llamarle por teléfono: alguien le hablaba de un pedido de mangos en Toledo, otra persona le preguntaba dónde debían llevar su coche para limpiarlo. Fernando ha recibido al menos ocho mensajes o llamadas entre agosto y octubre. Las consultas a la IA que habían dado su número eran, sobre todo, siempre que pudo confirmarlo, al modelo Gemini Flash. En un caso fue a ChatGPT: un hombre ruso que buscaba trabajo de cocinero y escribía a un restaurante. La IA en este caso dio el número de Fernando junto a un texto en cirílico.

“Lo que me empezó a mosquear fue que cada vez fuera más recurrente y frecuente”, explica Fernando a este periódico. “De ahí pasé a pensar que era muy raro que alucinara siempre el mismo número y que se les había colado en los datos de entreno”, añade.

Que un modelo de lenguaje alucine, es decir, que genere información falsa, no es nada nuevo. Lo que es más raro es la insistencia de la IA en dar el mismo número. Pero no es único. “Ha habido casos en que el asistente de WhatsApp de Meta ha dado el número de un particular en lugar del teléfono de una empresa, y otros en los que los resúmenes de IA de Google han mostrado números falsos de atención al cliente colocados en internet por estafadores”, dice Linda Petrini, investigadora en seguridad de IA. “El patrón es real y es de esperar que más gente corriente acabe atrapada a medida que más personas busquen empresas a través de chatbots”.

Fernando no conoce a nadie más a quien le haya pasado. Tiene este número solo desde 2021 y sospecha que podría haber sido antes de algún negocio. De ahí, intuye, que pudiera estar en los datos que entrenaron a la IA. Es la misma sospecha que tiene Petrini: “Mi mejor hipótesis es que el número aparece en webs reales de negocios, y que los chatbots lo sacan de internet cuando responden, en lugar de inventárselo de la nada”.

Pero no es la única opción que hay. José Hernández-Orallo, director de investigación del Centro Leverhulme de la Universidad de Cambridge y catedrático de la Universidad Politécnica de Valencia, cree que puede tratarse de una alucinación completa, puesto que el número de teléfono se asocia a varias tiendas. “No parece un número que estuviera asociado a nada específico en el entrenamiento”, asegura. “Así que tiene pinta de ser una alucinación. Por alguna razón, su número es más probable que otros y le pasa más a él que a otras personas”.

Las fechas también coinciden para Gemini. Entre finales de julio y principios de agosto, Google sacó sus modelos Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite y 3.7 Flash. “Los modelos gratuitos de Gemini son bastante flojos comparados con otros de pago, así que puede ser que sigan siendo flojos en alucinación, como se ve en distintas clasificaciones”, explica Hernández-Orallo.

En Google creen lo mismo, que es una alucinación, según explica una portavoz de la compañía a este periódico: “Los grandes modelos de lenguaje a veces pueden generar respuestas que, aunque parezcan plausibles, en realidad son incorrectas desde el punto de vista factual. Se conocen como alucinaciones”. Una búsqueda normal del número de Fernando en Google no da resultados.

No es algo menor

Puede parecer un problema fácil de solucionar o poco importante, pero tiene más peligro del que parece: “Me inquieta que se pueda dar mi número”, explica Fernando. “Estos casos no hacen daño, pero como la gente le pregunta todo tipo de cosas a la IA, me preocupa en qué manos podía acabar mi número de teléfono, si con algo de drogas, delincuencia, suicidio, gurús”, considera el afectado. También es un reto para la privacidad: “Lo que me daba más miedo es que yo doy mi Instagram o cualquier cosa antes que mi número de teléfono, que es sagrado. A través del número, está mi foto de perfil y con un número se pueden hacer mil cosas”.

Si se hicieran 10.000 preguntas sobre un servicio y saliera el mismo teléfono con cierta frecuencia, entonces se podría demostrar al menos que Fernando ha tenido mala suerte, dice Hernández-Orallo: “Las distribuciones de las alucinaciones no son uniformes, igual que los humanos generamos números aleatorios mucho más frecuentes que otros”, añade Hernández-Orallo, que cree que los humanos tendríamos aquí el mismo problema que Gemini Flash: “Su número podría incluso no haber existido como teléfono. Es como si te preguntan el número de tu primera novia, no te acuerdas y no vale decir que no lo sabes. Si te lo pregunto mil veces, habrá algún número que aparecerá una docena de veces”.

Un peligro añadido sería si este tipo de problema persiste y se alarga en el tiempo. ¿Cómo solucionarlo? Más allá de contactar con los negocios implicados para advertirles “puede presentar solicitudes de retirada a Google y a OpenAI”, explica Petrini. “Según el Reglamento General de Protección de Datos [la normativa europea que regula la privacidad y la protección de los datos personales de las personas físicas dentro de la Unión Europea], el teléfono es un dato personal, lo que da a la solicitud un peso real”.

World.title: Vamos a setas: seis rutas micológicas para el otoño, haya o no hongos
World.content:
El cambio climático ha retrasado un mes la temporada en España y los expertos no descartan que se alargue. En estos montes podremos saciar nuestro apetito de paisajes

Antes empezaba a tronar y a jarrear a finales de agosto y justo a los 21 días aparecían las setas en el monte. Así ocurría, por lo menos, en la sierra de Guadarrama, a caballo entre Madrid, Segovia y Ávila, donde el que esto escribe vive desde 1995. También antes el veranillo de San Miguel –29 de septiembre– y el de San Martín –11 de noviembre– eran unos pocos días de otoño en los que repuntaba el calor y se podía salir en manga corta a buscar setas, porque las había a patadas. Con el cambio climático, sin embargo, dejó de llover y de refrescar a finales de agosto y llegó el veroño, que comenzó siendo cosa de una o dos semanas y amenaza ya con suplantar al verdadero otoño, para desesperación de los seteros, a los que cada vez nos cuesta más entender y encontrar algo en este mundo al revés.

Pero veamos la botella –y la cesta– medio llena. Quizá todo esté ocurriendo a deshora y solo haya que aguardar. Las lluvias que no cayeron este año en agosto lo han hecho en octubre y algunas setas han salido. Si llueve más en noviembre y las temperaturas se mantienen altas, ¿por qué no podría haber un brote tardío? En ese caso, los siguientes montes serán buenos para salir a buscarlas, pues la experiencia nos dice que en ellos no suelen faltar. Y si no las encontramos, allá penas: disfrutaremos de seis de las excursiones más agradables que pueden hacerse en noviembre en España, con la cesta vacía y en manga corta.

Más información Cómo evitar una intoxicación por setas y por qué no hay que fiarse de las aplicaciones del móvil

1. Las Burbonas del Gorbeia (Álava)

La hayas que pueblan las laderas de las Burbonas alavesas son magníficas, hasta el punto de que en otoño el caminante no puede dejar de mirarlas y fotografiarlas, aun sabiendo que en el suelo se esconden setas deliciosas.

José David Fernández, director del parque micológico de Gorbeialdea –que abarca la cuarta parte del parque natural del Gorbeia, el mayor y más setero del País Vasco–, cree que las setas van con un mes de retraso y que este año se dejarán ver hasta finales de noviembre “con permiso de las heladas”. Recomienda, como es lógico, sacar el preceptivo permiso –10 euros por persona y día– y participar en alguna de las rutas que él mismo guía todos los fines de semana y en las que se recolectan alrededor de 25 especies distintas.

Una buscadora de setas junto a una haya monumental en las Burbonas del Gorbeia. Andrés Campos

Los boletus aereus y los edulis son dos de los hongos más abundantes y apreciados. Y la ruta favorita de José David y de cualquiera de los seteros que frecuentamos el “corazón verde de Euskadi” es la que asciende desde la casa del parque de Sarria hasta la triple cima de las Burbonas y luego regresa al punto de partida siguiendo de cerca al saltarín río Baias. Subiendo y bajando de las Burbonas, además de setas, se ven hayas majestuosas de melena dorada, cobriza y roja que, por sí solas, justificarían recorrer este itinerario circular de 16 kilómetros y cinco horas de duración, seis si nos paramos a ver qué hay debajo de la hojarasca. Para no perderse, hay que seguir las indicaciones y el track de Wikiloc. Para reponer fuerzas después de la excursión, nada como el cocido de alubias y las habitaciones del Hotel Doña Lola, que ocupa un caserío de piedra del siglo XVI en Izarra.

Al día siguiente podemos ver la cascada de Gouiri –una de las más altas de España, de 105 metros– y comprar el queso de Idiazábal que los hermanos hermanos Basterra elaboran con la leche de un montón de ovejas latxas que pastan arrastrando sus largas guedejas al lado mismo del salto.

Si andamos un lunes por la zona y deseamos profundizar en su riqueza micológica, podemos acercarnos a la Sociedad Micológica Gorbeiako Bazterra, en Murgia, donde ese día hay un servicio gratuito de identificación. Su vicepresidente, Vicente Blasco, es categórico respecto al anómalo comportamiento de las setas este año, que han brotado muy tarde sin que apenas haya llovido en cinco meses: “Han salido por aburrimiento”.

Queseria de los Hermanos Basterra, en Goiuri. Andrés Campos

2. Castañar de los Ojestos (Cáceres)

El Castañar de los Ojestos, en la sierra cacereña de Gata, también es espectacular en esta época, cuando las hojas se vuelven amarillas y caedizas, pero lo de no fijarse en el suelo aquí es más complicado. Además de setas hay castañas, y eso ya es demasiada golosina para no prestar atención. En San Martín de Trevejo, uno de los pueblos más bonitos de España, arranca el sendero PR-CC 184, que atraviesa de abajo arriba este castañar, el más extenso de Extremadura.

A 2,5 kilómetros del inicio, como a una hora de paseo sosegado, se llega a la altura de los Abuelos, dos castaños enormes a los que se les calcula una edad de 600 años. Media hora después se cruza el río de la Vega, que con las lluvias otoñales forma unas buenas chorreras. Y en media más se alcanza el puerto de Santa Clara, donde acaba Cáceres y empieza Salamanca.

La bajada, que es por el mismo camino, toca hacerla –ahora sí– fijándose en el suelo, donde en noviembre suele haber níscalos, lenguas de vaca, parasoles, algún que otro boletus y las últimas castañas llovidas del cielo amarillo. En el restaurante Saboris de Sempris, en San Martín de Trevejo, los boletus edulis se sirven acompañados con unas tostas de torta del Casar. Otros dos comedores serranos donde no faltan en temporada los edulis son el gastrobar Los Portales, en Gata, y la taberna El Buen Avío de Trevejo.

Puesta de sol en el hotel Habitat Cigüeña Negra, en la sierra de Gata. Andrés Campos

El año que viene, porque ya es tarde para encontrarlas, vendremos a buscar la codiciada Amanita caesarea o huevo de rey. Para ello, lo más fácil y gratificante es alojarse a principios de otoño en el hotel Habitat Cigüeña Negra y salir a pasear con la cesta por la dehesa de encinas que lo rodea. Curiosamente, la especialidad del restaurante, que tiene una estrella verde Michelin por su cocina sostenible, no son las setas, sino la carne de Retwagyu, un cruce de vaca retinta extremeña y buey wagyu japonés que pace alrededor del hotel sin mostrar ningún interés por este bocado de césares. Aquí cada cual –los seteros, los clientes del asador y las vacas– van a lo suyo.

3. Sierra de Cebollera (La Rioja)

En la ermita de Lomos de Orios, en Villoslada de Cameros, un lagarto tallado en cuerno de vaca recuerda la historia que cuenta que en 1824, la Virgen salvó a un pastor de ser comido por uno gigantesco. Lino Martínez, que así se llamaba el pastor, lo había criado, hasta que éste que alcanzó un metro y medio de longitud. Un día, la criatura se abalanzó sobre su cuidador, el cual se libró in extremis de ser devorado al entrar corriendo en la ermita y cerrarse milagrosamente la puerta detrás de él, partiendo en dos al lagarto. Grandes como aquel animal y su ingratitud son los boletus edulis que se cogen hasta que empiezan a blanquear las cimas de la sierra riojana de Cebollera. Unos piensan que se llama así por la forma redondeada de sus montes y otros opinan que es por la abundancia que hay en ella de gamones blancos (Asphodelus albus), también llamados cebollanas, cebollinos, cebolletas de monte, cebollas de culebra, cebollas gamonitas, cebolleras moriscas o ceborrinchas.

Además de hermosos boletus, aquí las cestas se llenan de níscalos, parasoles, pardillas, negrillas, trompetas de la muerte y, entrado ya el invierno, pies azules. Algunas zonas de recolección pillan tan lejos que hay que acercarse en coche por pistas forestales de acceso restringido, pagando otro permiso además del que uno ya saca para ver si coge algo: seis euros en total. Para quien no quiere complicarse pidiendo ese otro permiso y metiéndose con el coche por vaya usted a saber qué caminos, existe un cómodo un cómodo sendero circular circular de algo menos de siete kilómetros –un par de horas a paso tranquilo– que lleva desde la misma ermita hasta las cascadas de Puente Ra, atravesando un hayedo precioso. No tiene pérdida: está marcado con trazos de pintura naranja y verde.

Su mayor aliciente, aparte de hallar setas, es ver los saltos de hasta diez metros que pega el arroyo de Puente Ra, afluente del río Iregua, el principal del valle. El premio de consolación para los que acaban con la cesta vacía es comerse unas pochas con boletus o un guiso de jabalí con hongos confitados y salsa de arándanos en el restaurante Corona, en Villoslada de Cameros. Al lado hay un alojamiento rural que se llama como lo que se acaba de admirar paseando valle arriba: Cascadas de Puente Ra.

Cascadas de Puente Ra, en sierra de Cebollera. Andrés Campos

4. Barranco de la Barbulla y Muela de Cortes (Valencia)

Donde ha llovido bastante en lo que va de otoño es en las montañas del interior de Valencia, que ahora están a tope de rebollones –como allí llaman a los níscalos–, de lenguas de vaca y de seteros con la navaja afilada y el brillo del ansia viva en la mirada. El Rincón de Ademuz y la comarca de los Serranos o del Alto Turia –cuya capital, Chelva, exploramos a fondo recientemente– son dos lugares famosos por su riqueza micológica.

Quien busque otras zonas menos trilladas y otras atracciones, aparte de esa, hará bien en acercarse a Cortes de Pallás. A la entrada de este recóndito pueblo, plantado en un barranco lateral del encañonado río Júcar y al pie de la alta y acantilada Muela de Cortes, un cartel de la oficina de turismo anuncia: “Un mundo aparte”. Y es verdad: más apartado no puede estar. Aquí el coche sirve ya para poco: toca echarse a caminar monte arriba, explorando los manantiales, los saltos de agua, los canales de riego y las balsas que convirtieron el barranco de la Barbulla en uno de los mayores paraísos hortícolas de los moriscos.

Recorriendo la llamada ruta de las Cascadas, veremos en un par de horas media docena de ellas. La mayor de todas, la de El Corbinet, resbala por una cornisa rocosa de ocho metros de altura y cae en una charca amplia, verde y sombría, idónea para comer –hay mesas alrededor– las tortas de sal o de embutido que se compraron en Ca’ la Conchin, frente a la oficina de turismo.

Vista desde el castillo Chirel, al que se llega por un sencillo sendero de tres kilómetros (ida y vuelta). Andrés Campos

Un camino más largo y esforzado, de siete kilómetros y casi cinco horas con paradas contemplativas, es la senda Cavanilles, que sube zigzagueando como una serpiente de escalera a la Muela de Cortes, donde 4.000 de los muchos moriscos que vivían en la comarca se refugiaron en el otoño de 1609 porque no querían ser expulsados de España ni abjurar de su fe.

Otro más sencillo, de solo tres kilómetros –ida y vuelta–, es el que lleva al castillo de Chirel, que fue el cuartel general de las tropas gubernamentales cuando los moriscos se rebelaron e hicieron fuertes en la Muela de Cortes. Desde la ruinosa fortaleza, a 300 metros sobre el Júcar, se ven como desde un helicóptero las aguas color turquesa del río y los barcos que navegan por ellas llenos de pensionistas del balneario de Cofrentes.

Si haciendo estas rutas no encontramos algún rebollón o alguna llanega negra –la seta mocosa típica de estos bosques de pino carrasco sobre rocas calizas, que suele alargar la temporada hasta enero–, solo nos queda subir en coche a la Muela de Cortes y parar por el camino en algún pinar prometedor. Donde haya vehículos en el arcén, habrá setas.

05 Sierra de Aracena (Huelva)

Esta sierra del norte de Huelva, fronteriza con Portugal, Badajoz y Sevilla, es Eldorado andaluz de las setas, donde cualquiera que haya estado en otoño habrá visto por doquier camiones frigoríficos cargando toneladas de ellas para llevarlas al extranjero. Aun así, el tiempo está tan loco, tan trastocado, que “este octubre no se ha cogido ni una”. Jorge Jaímez, gerente y guía de Lynxaia, confía en las lluvias de noviembre: “A finales de mes, casi dos más tarde de lo habitual, esperamos estar haciendo rutas micológicas”. Como otras 26 empresas de la sierra, Lynxaia participa en Soy Ecoturista, una iniciativa de la Asociación de Ecoturismo en España para proponer experiencias que contribuyan a la conservación de los espacios naturales y al desarrollo local.

Senderista en Alajar, municipio de la sierra de Aracena. Andrés Campos

Las rutas son sumamente respetuosas con el entorno y con los vecinos, a los cuales se pide permiso para hacerlas, no solo por cortesía, sino porque casi todo el monte en la sierra de Aracena es privado. Aunque tarde, este año volverán a salir las tanas (Amanita caesarea) y los hongos negros (Boletus aereus) entre los castaños de Fuenteheridos, Galaroza, Alájar o Castaño del Robledo y en las dehesas que los rodean, y los boletus edulis a alturas superiores a 600 metros.

Más adelante aún lo harán los níscalos en los pinares y los rebozuelos en los castañares y alcornocales más húmedos. El que no volverá a abrir sus puertas –no con Luismi López y Adela Ortiz al frente, por lo menos– es el restaurante Los Arrieros, en Linares de la Sierra, que era un templo de la cocina del terruño y de las setas en particular. Pero en la sierra sigue habiendo dos establecimientos donde las preparan con cariño en otoño: Peña de Arias Montano, en Alájar, y Montecruz, en Aracena. Un comercio de referencia para comprarlas frescas es Sirlache, en la calle Constitución, 1. Y un hotel idóneo para quienes estamos enganchados a ellas es Finca La Fronda. No hace falta ni salir de él para buscarlas: solo pasear por el jardín.

Cogiendo setas en el Pinar de Valsaín. Andrés Campos

6. Pinar de Valsaín (Segovia)

En la sierra de Guadarrama, este octubre ha sido flojo micológicamente, con temperaturas altísimas y la humedad justa para que los seteros locales cogiéramos seis o siete boletus edulis y un puñado de níscalos cada uno. Parasoles (Macrolepiota procera) hay muchos, pero pocos los recolectamos, aun sabiendo que, cortados sus sombreros en cuartos, empanados junto a una loncha de jamón serrano y fritos en aceite de oliva, están muy ricos.

Un lugar donde cabe esperar que con algo más de lluvia se anime la cosa a mediados o finales de noviembre es el pinar de Valsaín, en la vertiente segoviana del puerto de Navacerrada. Podemos dejar el coche en el aparcamiento de más de 30 plazas que hay junto a la fuente de la Canaleja y el puente de la Cantina, al pie de las Siete Revueltas –kilómetro 17 de la carretera CL-601.

La bicicleta es una excelente manera de explorar el pinar de Valsaín. Andrés Campos

Allí mismo veremos un portillo con un cartel que dice “acotado de setas” –habremos pedido permiso antes, claro– y un sendero que se adentra en este magnífico bosque de pino silvestre, ligado a la corona desde tiempos de Carlos III. Subiendo siempre a corta distancia del arroyo del Puerto del Paular, que baja del puerto de Cotos, o de su afluente de las Pintadas, siempre encontraremos veneros y tollas donde, por seco y mustio que esté el resto del pinar, crecen los níscalos. Noviembre es su mejor mes y también el de las capuchinas.

Otra excelente manera de explorar este pinar es en bici, siguiendo la pista forestal asfaltada que lo rodea por completo. Es una vuelta de 35 kilómetros, con salida y llegada en la Granja de San Ildefonso, que se puede hacer en unas tres o cuatro horas, depende del tiempo que se invierta en examinar las muchas zonas húmedas que se atraviesan. Tampoco es mala idea dejar de registrar el bosque a mediodía y bajar al real sitio a probar los famosos buñuelos de setas con foie del restaurante La Fundición.

World.title: IDFA 2026 winners: Chinese family portrait takes top prize
World.content:
The Year of the Ghost, a Dutch-Chinese documentary about a filmmaker’s mother and sister after his father’s death, has won the top prize at the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA).

Louis Hothothot’s film won three awards at Thursday’s ceremony at the Eye Filmmuseum. It took best film in the International Competition, which carries a €15,000 prize, as well as best editing and the €5,000 award for best Dutch film.

The festival’s 39th edition runs until Sunday, with 253 films from 80 countries. One of the five documentaries in our preview, You Can See Everything, came second in the audience vote.

These are the films that took the main prizes:



The Year of the Ghost

Hothothot was born in China in 1986 as a second child under the one-child policy and moved to Amsterdam in his twenties. His first film, Four Journeys, opened at IDFA in 2021. In this second film, Covid restrictions stop him from getting back to China in time to say goodbye to his father. He then follows his mother, who wants to stay in her husband’s home town to care for his spirit, and his sister, who is trying to get by as a single woman in a big city. The jury praised the film’s “bold honesty, a rare attention to detail, cinematic curiosity and love”.

Memories of Lightning

Riccardo Giacconi’s French-Italian film won best film in the Envision Competition for experimental work, also worth €15,000. Radio journalist Sibilla Scinti Roger (30) travels to an almost deserted village in Le Marche, central Italy, to make an audio documentary about a murder there in 1982 – and finds out the 14-year-old victim was her aunt. Scinti Roger also won the award for outstanding artistic contribution.

Hazara Town

Afghan-born director Khadim Dai won the award for best first feature and the international critics’ prize (Fipresci), as well as a special mention in the International Competition. The film follows his Hazara family, who fled Afghanistan 20 years ago and now face growing persecution in Pakistan. They have to decide whether to stay together or leave one by one, knowing they may never see each other again.

The Clearing

Dutch director Sabine Groenewegen won the award for best use of archive footage, sponsored by the media archive Beeld & Geluid. Her film is a feminist history of Dutch colonial rubber plantations in the Dutch East Indies, where local women were subjected to violence and sexual enslavement. On the festival’s opening night, Groenewegen also received the €50,000 Cultuurfonds documentary grant, which an anonymous donor gives every year to a Dutch documentary maker.

Women and War

The €5,000 audience award, announced on Friday, went to Elwira Niewiera’s German-Polish-Ukrainian documentary. Four women attend therapy sessions in a chalet in the Ukrainian mountains, each trying to recover from very different traumatic experiences of the war. Festivalgoers gave it an average score of 4.856 out of 5, just ahead of You Can See Everything on 4.842.

Other winners included Joël Akafou’s Lonan Tché for best directing and Tala Hadid’s Bardi, set among horse riders in central Morocco, for best cinematography. Raluca Lupaşcu’s A Modern Roma Fairytale got a special mention for best Dutch film, and Ant Hampton’s Dutch-Belgian All the Downtime won the DocLab award for digital storytelling.

The full list of winners is on the IDFA website.

World.title: Inburgering with DN: understanding education system acronyms
World.content:
International parents in the Netherlands often find the Dutch school system baffling: HBO, SBO, DUO, WO… the jargon is endless. So to help you pass this particular parenting test, our Inburgering course this month looks at educational acronyms and the like.

Lesson 65: educational jargon

Primary school in the Netherlands is relatively straightforward – although parents often face a bewildering number of school philosophies when deciding which school to entrust their offspring to. It is in groep 8, the final year of primary school, that the trouble really starts.

Doorstroomtoets

Previously known as the Citotoets and the Eindtoets Basisonderwijs, the doorstroomtoets is taken by children in their final year at primary school. The tests focus on language and arithmetic, and the results are used to help determine which type of secondary education children should go on to. In principle, the teacher’s recommendation takes precedence.

The Dutch love of tests and early streaming has been widely criticised, and more secondary schools now offer mixed-ability classes in the first and second years.

Secondary education itself is divided into three main streams. Schools may offer just one – typically in cities – or a combination.

VWO

VWO (voorbereidend wetenschappelijk onderwijs, or preparatory academic education) is the highest level of Dutch secondary education and is followed by some 20% of pupils. A VWO education takes six years, with pupils choosing a specialism (profiel) in the sciences or humanities after three. There are two variants: atheneum and gymnasium. Gymnasium pupils take Latin and Greek in addition to the dozen or so other VWO subjects.

HAVO

HAVO (hoger algemeen voortgezet onderwijs) literally means ‘higher general continued education’. It takes five years to get a HAVO diploma, which prepares school leavers for a hogeschool (see HBO below) rather than a university. Around 30% of pupils are in a HAVO stream. After three years, HAVO pupils also choose a specialism in the sciences or humanities.

VMBO

VMBO stands for voorbereidend middelbaar beroepsonderwijs (preparatory intermediate vocational education). Some 50% of pupils attend this type of secondary education, which is subdivided into four streams. It takes four years to complete a VMBO course.

The most academic VMBO stream is still widely known as MAVO (middelbaar algemeen voortgezet onderwijs, or intermediate general continued education), after the type of school it replaced in 1999.

Middle-class parents push hard to avoid a VMBO recommendation, hence the popularity of tutors and crammers – and exam stress – for 12-year-olds.

SBO, SO and VSO

Special needs pupils have their own category of jargon, depending on their age, the nature of their disability and how much care they need. The main types are speciaal basisonderwijs (SBO, special primary education), speciaal onderwijs (SO, special education) and voortgezet speciaal onderwijs (VSO, special secondary education).

Lighthouse Special Education in The Hague is the only international school for special needs pupils.

After secondary school, most young people move on to further education. Education is compulsory until 16, and until 18 for anyone who does not yet have at least a HAVO, VWO or MBO level 2 diploma.

MBO

MBO, or middelbaar beroepsonderwijs (vocational education and training), is the highest level of education reached by around 40% of the working population. There are four levels of MBO diploma, and students can either attend college full time or combine work and study.

HBO

There are two types of degree course in the Netherlands: the academic courses offered by universities and the more vocational courses (HBO, or hoger beroepsonderwijs) offered by hogescholen. Their umbrella body, the Vereniging Hogescholen, calls them ‘universities of applied sciences’ in English. The Netherlands has 36 hogescholen ranging from art academies to hotel schools and technical colleges.

WO

The Netherlands has 14 official universities offering wetenschappelijk onderwijs (research-oriented education), including the Open University. Delft, Eindhoven and Twente are universities of technology, while Wageningen focuses on agriculture and food. A bachelor’s degree takes three years, a master’s one or two.

DUO

If you have any connection to post-school education, you cannot avoid dealing with the education ministry’s Dienst Uitvoering Onderwijs (DUO), which runs student finance and related services. DUO holds the diploma records that colleges and universities use to check whether you can enrol, organises the lotteries for popular courses and works out how much student finance you are entitled to.

After you graduate, DUO will follow you for years to make sure you pay back your student loan. DUO should not be confused with DUWO, which specialises in student housing.

World.title: Prosecutors hacked and wiretapped Tata Steel, court hears
World.content:
The public prosecution service (OM) hacked into Tata Steel’s internal communication network, wiretapped phones, and made video recordings as part of its investigation into alleged criminal pollution, it was revealed on Friday in Amsterdam’s district court.

During the first hearing of the case, the OM revealed it had conducted a “covert intrusion into Tata Steel’s corporate network”, broadcaster NOS reported. Documents were also taken, witnesses questioned and deposition measurements examined.

The case, which has been years in the making, accuses the steelmaker of intentionally ignoring harmful pollution stemming from its coke and gas plants in IJmuiden.

Police and prosecutors are allowed to use hacking techniques in criminal cases under highly specific circumstances. This has been allowed since 2019, NOS reported, and only in a handful of cases, including child pornography and criminal communication investigations.

A defence lawyer for Tata Steel said that there was “unfounded distrust” against the company, that its employees go to work to do the right thing, and that “wire tapping and hacking” had been used as part of an “unbalanced” criminal file.

The investigation is ongoing and could lead to the prosecution of individual executives of the company. The process is not expected to be completed until the first quarter of next year, the OM said, at which point it will also become clear if the current CEO Hans van den Berg could be charged.

The public health institute RIVM records an above-average rate of lung cancer for residents living around the plant, and soot regularly collects in the surrounding neighbourhoods, including school playgrounds.

Many people have suffered serious health problems, which they attribute to the plant.

In 2021, lawyer Bénédicte Ficq filed a complaint on behalf of 1,200 residents and the following year prosecutors began investigating. In July, the OM summoned Tata Steel to court on criminal charges.

Shortly thereafter, the government said it could pull out of a planned €2 billion subsidy package for the company if the criminal case raises “serious concerns” for the Dutch state.

World.title: Bruna and Readshop avoid bankruptcy, for now
World.content:
Audax, the parent company of the popular Bruna and Readshop shops, was granted two months of protection against creditors by a Breda court Thursday.

The move follows a provisional cooling-off period granted to the company earlier this month and a hearing earlier this week attended by more than 10 creditors and auditors, many of whom signaled they were willing to grant Audax more time to get its financial affairs in order.

Audax, which was acquired by Lector Capital in January 2026, has been experiencing financial difficulties for years. It says at the time of the acquisition, Lector agreed to invest €8.6 million in Audax, money they say never came through.

Audax is said to owe its suppliers more than €9 million. Some have demanded payment before delivering new products, which could impact the upcoming Christmas shopping season.

World.title: Exiled Colombian climate activist wins children’s peace prize
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

A 17-year-old Colombian climate activist, Francisco Javier Vera Manzanares, has won the 2026 International Children’s Peace Prize given out by the Amsterdam-based KidsRights Foundation for “putting children’s rights at the heart of climate justice”.

The young activist is currently living in exile in Spain after receiving death threats over his activism in Colombia.

“Although our 17-year-old winner Francisco is an example of peaceful activism for climate rights defenders around the world, he has been forced to flee due to violent death threats against him,” KidsRights chairman Marc Dullaert told broadcaster NOS.

“It is shocking that peaceful child activists are threatened and that governments are unable to protect these children and their right to be heard.”

But in the imposing Peace Palace in The Hague Thursday afternoon, it was all celebration as Francisco received the prize from 72-year-old Kailash Satyarthi, an Indian child rights activist and 2014 Nobel Peace Prize winner.

“All children around the world have the right to live on a healthy, clean, dignified, and peaceful planet,” Francisco said.

Child activist

Francisco got involved in climate action in 2019 after seeing devastating wildfires engulf the Amazon rainforest. At just nine-years-old, he and six friends founded Guardians for Life, which today has more than 1,400 young members from across Colombia and Latin America.

He became the first child ever in Colombia to speak before Congress that same year.

According to KidsRights, Francisco “believes children are citizens of today, not just tomorrow, and should have a meaningful voice in the decisions that shape their lives and futures.”

He’s served as a Child Advisor to the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child, helping to craft implementation guidelines on children’s rights and climate change.

Francisco’s work has led to the planting of more than 5,000 trees across Latin America and Europe and the training of some 10,000 young people in climate leadership, human rights and citizen participation.

More young winners

Francisco was chosen from 280 nominations across 57 countries. Former winners include Swedish activist Greta Thunberg, who won the prestigious award in 2019.

Two finalists were also recognised at Thursday’s ceremony, Chilean justice activist Issaiah Guzman Arancibia (15) and 17-year-old Sufaira, a Rohingya refugee from Myanmar currently living in Bangladesh who works to prevent child marriages.

Some 700,000 Rohingya fled to Bangladesh refugee camps after a 2017 government crackdown that judges in the same Peace Palace ruled hours before the award ceremony was a genocide committed by Myanmar against its Rohingya population – the first time a country has been held responsible for committing genocide.

World.title: Students walk out against conscription and defence spending
World.content:
High school and university students nationwide will walk out of their classrooms at 1pm on Friday in a National Peace Protest against conscription and increasing defence spending, part of an international action day also taking place in 24 other countries including Germany, England and France.

“In our opinion, money is being taken away from care, education and housing to go to defence,” National Student Union (LSVb) chairwoman Evy Kras told RTL news. “At the same time, they want us to enlist. Young people feel betrayed and say: so far and no further. We want to be invested in us.”

She says these political spending choices are at the expense of young people, and that campaigns by the defence ministry paint an unrealistic picture of war. “They pretend it’s all very adventurous and flashy, but fighting in a war is not flashy.”

The LSVb, together with research and activist group Stop Wapenhandel, published a report earlier this week saying that defence spends €260 million annually on recruitment campaigns at schools and online. Meanwhile, they say, students have trouble making ends meet.

In at least 16 Dutch cities and dozens of schools, students will leave their classrooms at 1pm, fighting for an “affordable future”. In Amsterdam, students will gather at the Stopera, while in Utrecht, they’ll head to the Domplein and in Groningen to the Broerplein.

The Dutch group Stop the War Fever, which is organising the walkout, says on its website that the government refuses to work towards peace yet “pumps billions into weapons and war.”

Conscription

The group is asking to do away with conscription, move defence out of education and invest in the future of young people instead of weapons of war.

Currently, both men and women in the Netherlands aged between 17 and 45 must register for conscription, but since 1997, there has been no obligation to serve.

But the government is preparing legislation for a selective military conscription system that could be employed if it’s deemed necessary for security reasons.

Junior minister Derk Boswijk said in March that he couldn’t rule out the deployment of young people in the coming years.

“Many young people see it coming, now that the war is near at hand on the European continent,” student Camiel Breet told RTL News. “We want to fight against the cabinet’s plans.”

“This is the first post-Cold War generation that is both the generation of misfortune and grows up with the threat of war,” Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam professor of social change and conflict Jacquelien van Stekelenburg told RTL News. “A basic sense of peace is no longer self-evident for them.”

World.title: Tata Steel goes on trial accused of deliberate air pollution
World.content:
The criminal case against Tata Steel over alleged deliberate air pollution around its IJmuiden plant began at Amsterdam district court on Friday.

The public prosecution service (OM) accuses Tata Steel IJmuiden of intentionally and unlawfully releasing harmful substances into the air. The complainants say they suffer serious health problems and worry about local children, with soot accumulating in local playgrounds, broadcaster NOS reported. The public health institute RIVM has recorded above-average lung cancer rates in the area.

The case began in 2021, when lawyer Bénédicte Ficq filed a complaint on behalf of people living near the plant. Prosecutors opened an investigation the following year and announced in July that they would take the company to court. They are still considering whether individual managers can be held personally liable.

The case focuses on the plant’s coke-making ovens, where coal is heated at very high temperatures without oxygen to produce coke, a material used to make steel. If the coal is not heated for long enough, it remains partly unfinished (called raw coke) and can release harmful gases into the air and spread soot into the environment.

Tata says it is technically unavoidable that a batch is sometimes not heated for long enough. Prosecutors suspect the company accepts these incidents and deliberately does not report them. In July, Tata called the allegations “essentially unjust”.

Ficq told NOS it was “a tremendously important day” and said the emissions incidents were “foreseeable and avoidable”. She wants executives, including chairman Hans van den Berg, to be prosecuted as well.

€2bn subsidy at steak

The criminal case also affects a €2 billion state support package for Tata’s switch to greener steel. The cabinet said in July that it could pull out of the deal if the investigation raised “serious concerns”. According to NOS, talks have now been extended to March, and the trial is unlikely to be over by then.

World.title: FedEx-led consortium completes €7.8bn takeover of Polish delivery giant InPost
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A consortium led by FedEx has completed its €7.8 billion (34.5 billion zloty) takeover of Polish delivery giant InPost. The deal will see InPost remain headquartered in Poland, with founder and CEO Rafał Brzoska staying at the helm. Friday’s announcement brings to a close a process that was first announced in February and received European Commission approval in August. InPost’s shares have now been delisted from the stock exchange. The takeover follows years of rapid growth for InPost, which pioneered the use of parcel delivery lockers in Poland before spreading rapidly in major western European markets, including France, Spain and the UK. A consortium of Advent, FedEx, A&R Investments and PPF has completed its takeover of Poland's InPost, which is now private. InPost has delisted from Euronext Amsterdam. Founder Rafał Brzoska stays on as CEO, and the company remains headquartered in Poland. pic.twitter.com/HWigKVPC3w — IPO Newsroom (@IPONewsroom_) November 20, 2026 Under the deal, FedEx and Advent, an American private equity firm, each hold 37% of InPost. A&R Investments, Brzoska’s own investment vehicle, has 16% and PPF, a Czech investment fund founded by the late billionaire Petr Kellner, 10%. PPF, A&R and Advent were previously already stakeholders. The consortium acquired InPost at a price of €15.60 per share, valuing the company at approximately €7.8 billion. In a statement published on Friday, Advent confirmed that InPost would retain its name, branding, Polish headquarters and operational independence following the takeover. Brzoska, who founded his business in 1999, will continue as CEO alongside the existing management team. “InPost’s home market of Poland will remain the blueprint for new innovations, which will then be scaled across InPost’s wider European network,” said Advent. They added that the new consortium would now “accelerate investment” in InPost’s operations, helping the firm “extend its reach further”. FedEx and InPost would also “explore opportunities” to cooperate with one another. “InPost has built a leading position in Europe’s out-of-home delivery segment,” said FedEx’s CEO and president, Raj Subramaniam. “Connecting our global network…with InPost’s last-mile capabilities gives both businesses a potential springboard for profitable growth.” Brzoska, who is one of Poland’s wealthiest individuals, said that the new partnership would “deliver the long-term capital, global reach and deep technology expertise we require to build on what we have already achieved together as a leading European e-commerce enabler”. President Macron has thanked Polish delivery giant InPost for its latest investment in France The firm, which already operates over 9,000 parcel lockers in France through its subsidiary Mondial Relay, will now spend a further €500m to expand its presence https://t.co/caOGNQemfm — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 2, 2026 InPost is the largest operator of parcel lockers in Europe, with around 70,000 across the continent. That includes roughly 30,000 in Poland and 16,000 in the UK, including in branches of the British Post Office, with over 23,000 more in the seven Eurozone countries where InPost operates. In the second quarter of 2026, InPost had revenue of 4.18 billion zloty (€970 million), up 18.2% year on year, while its number of parcels handled rose 16% to 380.9 million. The strongest revenue growth came in the eurozone, where sales increased 37.9%, followed by Poland, with 12.7% growth. Revenue in the UK and Ireland rose 9.8%.
