World.title: Gallery: Estonia's largest solar park opens in Risti with 340,000 panels
World.content:
Estonia's largest solar park has opened in Risti, Lääne County, with enough capacity to cover the annual electricity consumption of roughly 90,000 households.

Built by renewable energy firm Sunly at a cost of €125 million, the 244-megawatt site is set to expand into a hybrid energy hub with battery storage, wind and a data center.

Spanning 270 hectares with 340,000 panels, the facility is the second largest in the Baltic states. Sunly CEO Priit Lepasepp noted that 90,000 households equals the combined populations of Tartu, Narva and Pärnu.

A substation is already complete and battery park construction has begun with Rolls-Royce, while a wind farm and major data center are also in the pipeline. Lääne-Nigula Mayor Janno Randmaa welcomed the local community payments and future tech jobs tied to the project.

Rapid solar expansion in Estonia has pushed installed solar capacity past annual peak demand, driving summer midday power prices to zero. Lepasepp said standalone solar or wind farms are no longer viable, noting Sunly will earn revenue from frequency regulation and selling stored battery power when gas-fired electricity is expensive.

State-owned rival Enefit has paused standalone solar projects, with Baltic business development head Johann-Gustav Lend agreeing that future sites require hybrid setups paired with large on-site power consumers.

World.title: Stefan Vaaks one assist shy of triple-double in Illinois NCAA blowout
World.content:
Estonian guard Stefan Vaaks finished one assist short of a triple-double on Friday as 10th-ranked Illinois routed Eastern Illinois 114-52 in NCAA men's basketball.

Vaaks tied his season high with 20 points and grabbed an NCAA career-best 11 rebounds while the Fighting Illini tied a Big Ten Conference record with 23 three-pointers.

Building a 68-18 halftime lead, Vaaks shot 3 of 5 inside the arc, 4 of 8 from three-point range, and 2 of 2 from the free-throw line while adding a season-high nine assists alongside two turnovers and two fouls. Ethan Brown led Illinois with 26 points and Tomislav Ivišić added 22, while Jalen Calloway scored 17 for Eastern Illinois. Illinois improved to 5-1 overall and 4-0 at home ahead of Monday's home matchup against winless Winthrop.

Elsewhere for Estonians in U.S. college basketbal, Erik Makke scored 18 points with seven assists and two rebounds as Stephen F. Austin beat Indiana State 86-76. Kätlin Kangur went scoreless in 24 minutes with two rebounds and one assist as Idaho defeated Nevada 67-47 on the road.

World.title: New sand and gravel quarry blocked at Männiku quarry due to EDF training area
World.content:
A mining firm has been denied permission to extract sand at a new site in a quarry zone near Tallinn, because the Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) needs the land.

Geological surveys at the site in Männiku, just south of the capital, have wrapped up, and mining company AS Silikaat has been denied permission to go ahead with quarrying.

The Estonian Center for Defense Investments (RKIK) wants the newly surveyed sand deposits registered as passive rather than active reserves, to protect training routes and safety zones.

Located in Männiku village in Harju County's Saku Municipality, the area has seen sand extraction for more than 70 years alongside an EDF training area spanning over 1,000 hectares and which encompasses the Männiku quarry.

Silikaat received an Environmental Board permit late last year to conduct geological surveys on 13 hectares of defense land — including up to 70 boreholes — with RKIK approval to assess sand volume and quality.

However, RKIK portfolio manager for training areas Elari Kalmaru said mining and quarrying cannot go ahead there now because the surveyed blocks sit directly on the Männiku training area, including a key transit route between sections of the site and firing danger zones.

"Whenever we review such permitting procedures, our only criterion is that the training area can continue operating in the same way it has up to now, and in this case that is not possible," Kalmaru told Vikerraadio.

The RKIK has proposed registering the deposits as passive reserves — meaning the sand's presence is noted, but cannot be extracted while the EDF uses the site for training — rather than active reserves sought by Silikaat for near-term mining. Kalmaru rejected the suggestion that the survey was pointless, saying passive registration remains valid, though mining would require offsetting changes elsewhere, such as expanded training facilities to accommodate growing conscript numbers.

Silikaat Group CEO Priit Poks declined to provide comment on the matter to ERR. Aside from Männiku, the company mines sand at the Tika II quarry in Rapla County and the Pihlaka quarry in Viljandi County.

World.title: RIA: Scammers create fake online stores to steal banking data
World.content:
Scammers are creating websites that imitate well-known brands and can appear highly convincing. Their goal is to lure shoppers to fraudulent pages and gain access to their banking information, the Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) warns.

With Black Friday and the holiday shopping season approaching, many online retailers have already launched sales campaigns, creating opportunities for fraudsters to target unsuspecting consumers.

As an example, RIA highlighted a fake website that imitated the online store of retailer JYSK in a Facebook post.

"A fake site can often be identified by its web address. Users should carefully read the URL and compare it with the official online store's address. Even a single different letter may indicate a fraudulent website," the agency warned.

"Consumers should also be cautious when clicking on s on social media. Alongside promotions from legitimate online stores, there may be ads leading to fake sites created to obtain banking card details and other sensitive information," RIA said.

If a website appears suspicious, RIA asks people to report it to cert@cert.ee. Specialists will investigate the information and, if necessary, block the site to help prevent further fraud.

Tips in English language for safe online shopping are available on RIA's website.

World.title: Külli Kraner: Minimum wage should rise no faster than prices
World.content:
Employers and labor unions are currently negotiating next year's minimum wage. Their responsibility is to agree on an increase that businesses and the broader economy can sustain. In the accommodation and food service sector, that means the minimum wage should not rise faster than inflation in 2027, writes Külli Kraner.

While the minimum wage across the economy equals about 43 percent of the average wage, in accommodation and food services it already amounts to roughly three-quarters of the sector's median wage. As a result, it is no longer merely the lowest permissible wage but effectively sets the pay level for the entire sector.

The purpose of the minimum wage is to protect the lowest-paid workers. When it approaches the standard wage level, the link between pay and skills, experience and responsibility begins to disappear, leaving employers with fewer opportunities to reward competence and experience through higher pay.

"Businesses have been unable to raise prices at the same pace because customers' purchasing power has declined."

If the minimum wage were to increase by, for example, 5.7 percent next year and reach €1,000 per month, the gap between the pay of an experienced chef or waiter and that of an entry-level assistant would narrow even further. Preserving that gap requires raising the wages of experienced employees as well, pushing up the entire pay structure. In Tallinn, where wages are higher, such increases are easier to absorb, but the minimum wage is the same throughout Estonia.

Rising costs with limited room for price increases

Over the past three years, costs for hotels and restaurants have risen faster than revenues. Wages per employee have increased by nearly 18 percent in restaurants and nearly 15 percent in hotels. Food, beverages, energy and services have become more expensive, while value-added tax rates for both accommodation and food services have increased.

Businesses have been unable to raise prices at the same pace because customers' purchasing power has declined. Restaurants are selling less than they did three years ago, and hotel room rates in Tallinn have remained nearly unchanged.

Labor costs are the largest expense in the sector. A survey conducted among members of the Estonian Hotel and Restaurant Association this fall found that nearly half of businesses would consider reducing staff numbers or working hours if the minimum wage rises rapidly.

Entry-level jobs disappear first

Hotels and restaurants provide many people's first jobs. Employees often enter the sector while studying, after graduation or while seeking a new career, frequently without training or experience. Skills are learned on the job, and employers invest both time and money in that process.

The minimum wage is the entry-level wage for these workers. If it rises faster than company revenues allow, employers will prefer experienced workers who can start immediately. Beginners will have fewer opportunities, and the jobs that launch so many careers will be the first to disappear.

"A reduction in value-added tax would also help the food service sector."

Minimum wage increases also affect competition in the accommodation market. Hotels pay wages and employment taxes for receptionists, cleaners and cooks. Short-term rental providers often have no formally employed workers, even though many operate at a scale comparable to a small accommodation business, with multiple apartments, daily cleaning, linen services and key handovers.

The work is still being done. The question is whether labor taxes are being paid on it. Minimum wage increases only raise costs for businesses that formally employ workers, and with every increase the gap widens between companies that comply with the rules and those that do not.

We do not want to restrict short-term rentals. We want equal rules for providers of the same service.

Tourism organizations have proposed a solution to the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications, arguing that little has been done on the issue for years. One element would distinguish between occasional home-sharing and commercial activity. If someone rents out their home occasionally, it is part of the sharing economy. If a property is rented for more than 60 nights per year or if more than one apartment is rented out, it should be treated as a business, registered and subject to the same requirements as other accommodation providers.

Sustainable wage growth depends on what customers can afford

Workers' financial well-being matters. In terms of purchasing power, Estonia's minimum wage was the lowest in the European Union at the beginning of 2026. But purchasing power depends not only on wages, but also on taxes and prices. If the tax-free income threshold increases, workers take home more pay without increasing employers' costs.

A reduction in value-added tax would also help the food service sector. A large share of restaurant prices reflects labor costs, and because VAT is applied to the full price, labor is effectively taxed as well.

Estonia's VAT rate for food services is 24 percent, while most European countries apply lower rates. In Finland it is 13.5 percent, and Germany cut its rate to seven percent at the beginning of 2026. If Estonia reduced the rate to 13 percent, businesses could raise wages without cutting jobs, while customers would face less price pressure, helping to sustain demand.

We want our employees' wages to increase. Sustainable wage growth, however, comes from workers' skills and from what customers are willing to pay for services. A minimum wage increase raises everyone's wages equally, regardless of what a business can earn.

From the perspective of the hotel and restaurant sector, therefore, the minimum wage increase in 2027 should not exceed inflation. Flexible working-hour rates should be decoupled from the minimum wage, and policymakers should recognize that in some sectors the minimum wage is already close to the standard wage level. Measures such as increasing tax-free income and adjusting VAT spread the burden more broadly and do not threaten jobs as directly as rapid minimum wage increases.

Külli Kraner is chief executive officer of the Estonian Hotel and Restaurant Association, which is a member of the Estonian Employers' Confederation.

World.title: Data center boom in Estonia: Who is building, where and at what cost
World.content:
Developers have filed grid connection requests for 2,900 megawatts of data centers in Estonia, nearly double the country's current peak electricity demand of 1,700 megawatts.

While only one major facility operates today, billions of euros in proposed artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud campuses across western and northern Estonia could reshape both power prices and grid stability.

National grid operator Elering has received seven connection applications totaling 2,900 megawatts. By contrast, Estonia's sole existing next-generation facility — Greenergy Data Centers in Hüüru, near Tallinn — currently draws just 2 megawatts, though it plans to scale to 200 megawatts by early 2028.

Lääne County emerges as the main hotspot

Most of the proposed capacity is clustered along high-voltage transmission lines in western Estonia's Lääne-Nigula and Lääneranna municipalities, particularly around the small towns of Risti and Lihula.

In Risti, Estonian renewable energy firm Sunly and Norway's Magnora Data Center are jointly developing a campus designed to connect at 180 megawatts initially and expand up to 400 megawatts if the local substation is upgraded — a buildout estimated at €1.7 billion.

AI-generated illustration of a potential data center in Estonia. Source: ChatGPT

Domestic renewables developer Evecon is also pursuing a 41-hectare industrial park next to Risti featuring two data center buildings and up to nine industrial facilities, projected to create around 150 jobs. A third developer, Sinfra, has initiated planning for a center in nearby Jõgisoo village, while a fourth unnamed company has made early-stage inquiries.

Lääne-Nigula Mayor Janno Randmaa said Sunly's project is furthest along because the company is pairing the campus with a local solar park to cover its power demand. For the others, he said, municipalities still lack clarity on energy and cooling-water needs.

"These applications come in fairly quickly, and at times the question is whether this is a serious trend or a passing fad, and how much of it will actually become reality," Randmaa said, noting that local residents have so far focused on practical questions around water use and noise rather than outright opposition.

Thirty kilometers south in Lihula, Evecon has entered detailed planning for a 100-megawatt data center, while Norwegian group Northern Europe Energy Group has unveiled plans for a 136-hectare site targeting 100 MVA initially and up to 1,100 MVA via a nearby 330-kilovolt line. Project manager Janis Paeglitis said the venture remains at an early feasibility stage, with final scale and investment yet to be set.

Evecon CEO Karl-Joonatan Kvell said pairing data centers with generation is a logical business model: steady, long-term power buyers make new renewable and storage projects far easier to finance.

Concept rendering of Sunly and Magnora's planned Risti data center campus. Source: Sunly

Billions eyed in northern and southwestern Estonia

Plans extend beyond the west coast. In Tapa, domestic firms Sustainable Investments and Sinfra, alongside Finland's Ehrnrooth business family, are weighing an investment of up to €3.4 billion.

Evecon has also received design conditions for a project in Varja, Lüganuse Municipality, in northeastern Estonia, and applied for a 100-megawatt facility near Kilingi-Nõmme in Saarde Municipality — a proposal that sparked a local council dispute over municipal jurisdiction and triggered the collapse of the local governing coalition.

State backs local AI compute, warns against 'closed' campuses

The Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs considers domestic data centers essential for running critical public and private digital services and safeguarding sensitive state data.

"Artificial intelligence infrastructure technologies and their security are still in an early stage of development, which is why it is safer to keep servers close to home," the ministry said.

Estonia has joined the European Commission's AI gigafactory joint procurement, pledging €20 million over 2028–2032 to purchase high-performance computing capacity on condition that one branch of the facility is located in Estonia. However, the ministry warned that closed campuses built solely for a single foreign tech giant's global operations bring minimal economic benefit compared to centers serving Estonian businesses, researchers and public institutions.

Concept rendering of the Norwegian developer's planned Lihula campus. Source: Screenshot from Northern Europe Energy Group's website.

What 2,900 megawatts could mean for electricity bills

If even a fraction of the 2,900 megawatts is built without matching new power generation, Estonia will rely more heavily on electricity imports from Finland — where a parallel data center boom is already poised to push Nordic exchange prices higher, according to Baltic Energy Partners board member Marko Allikson.

Still, Allikson noted that actual data center demand in Estonia stands at just 2 megawatts today and may barely top 20 megawatts next year, remaining marginal in the short term. Over the longer run, he said, data centers could unlock subsidy-free power plants through long-term power purchase agreements — pointing to Finland, where Google's off-take deal helped utility Fortum justify extending the lifespan of its Loviisa nuclear reactors.

Energy expert Arvi Hamburg added that higher overall consumption could reduce per-kilowatt-hour grid and frequency-reserve fees for ordinary consumers — unless developers connect via direct lines that bypass the public network.

Hamburg also warned that Estonia's small grid faces technical risks from rapid load swings at large server farms, urging authorities to site facilities strictly near major backbone substations and require operators to help keep the system balanced.

In an interview given to ERR's science portal Novaator, Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech) professor Mart Landsberg explained the impact of data centers on the electricity system in more detail, here.

World.title: Artist Raivo Järvi's cheerful drawings masked a life marked by personal tragedy
World.content:
Generations of Estonians grew up admiring the comics and illustrations of artist Raivo Järvi, better known as onu Raivo (uncle Raivo). Over the course of two decades, he also became a familiar radio voice and later spent nearly a decade in politics.

A new exhibition opening Friday at the Tartu Art Museum, "Pildi ees ja pildi sees" ("In Front of the Picture and Inside the Picture"), sheds light on lesser-known aspects of Järvi's life and work, revealing a more complex and at times deeply tragic personal story.

Born in Pärnu in 1954 as the only child of a violinist father and a ballet master mother, Järvi showed an interest in art from an early age. According to family recollections, he decided to become an artist at around age five after his mother warned him that an actor's life was difficult.

While artists are often associated with bohemian lifestyles, Järvi was known for discipline and meticulousness. From earning top marks in school to refining artistic motifs throughout his career, precision was one of his defining characteristics.

Uus kogumik tõi taas lugejate ette Raivo Järvi 1980. aastate koomiksid Autor/allikas: ERR

"It is a very interesting combination for an artist: meticulousness, a love of order and cleanliness. If you look at his graphic works, you see that same precision and stylistic purity," said his son, Richard-Erik Järvi.

Järvi's television career began almost by accident in 1977 while he was studying graphic arts at the Estonian State Art Institute (ERKI). When singer Voldemar Kuslap was unexpectedly unable to appear on the children's program "Laulujütsid," Järvi volunteered to draw with the children on air.

Over the next two decades, he became a beloved fixture of Estonian children's television, appearing in programs such as "Laupäeval koos isaga" ("Saturday With Dad"), "Kõige suurem sõber" ("The Greatest Friend") and "Jutupliiats" ("Story Pencil"). Viewers were particularly captivated by the drawings he created live on air, often completing elaborate characters before their eyes.

The 1983 children's television program "Kõige suurem sõber". Source: Heidi Maasikmets

Exhibition curator Stella Mõttus said audiences frequently wondered whether the outlines of the drawings had been prepared in advance.

"But no, he simply practiced them an enormous amount beforehand," she said.

Yet behind his public success lay significant personal hardship. Biography author Piret Kooli, who interviewed nearly 40 friends and colleagues while researching Järvi's life, said he endured profound losses. His father died when he was just ten years old. Later, he lost his first great love, dancer and actress Raili, who drowned during a film shoot under circumstances that remained unclear.

Richard-Erik Järvi said his father rarely spoke about her, but it was evident that the loss affected him deeply.

"It was the hardest period of his life," he said.

Järvi's later relationships were also troubled. His relationship with a beauty pageant princess named Signe, the mother of his son Richard-Erik, was short-lived. As a child, Richard-Erik knew little about his mother and was largely raised by his father, with invaluable help from family friend Tiia-Liis Jürgenson.

Jürgenson, whose own son was born just a week before Richard-Erik, helped care for the infant and later became a central figure in his upbringing.

"What began as a few days turned into a lifetime," she said. "For our family, it became completely natural."

Richard-Erik describes her as his guardian angel and says he often refers to her as his mother figure despite maintaining respect and gratitude toward his biological mother.

Raivo Järvi in "Pildi ees ja pildi sees". Source: Toomas Tuul

Despite his fame and productivity as an illustrator, radio host and later politician, Järvi never achieved substantial financial success. One notable example is the redesigned packaging for a popular curd snack introduced in 1996, featuring a cat illustration that became one of the most widely reproduced artworks in Estonia.

"Many people assume that cat earned him money for the rest of his life. In reality, it did not," Kooli noted.

According to those close to him, financial considerations partly motivated Järvi's decision to enter politics with the Reform Party. He served two terms in the Riigikogu, seeking financial stability for himself and his son.

A small room in an outbuilding on Faehlmanni tänav in Tallinn became his refuge when life became overwhelming. By then, his third major relationship, with an Estonia Theatre ballerina named Tatjana, had also deteriorated. Kooli believes Järvi spent much of his life searching for the love he had lost with Raili.

"He was looking for love, approval and himself," she said. "In reality, he was always looking for Raili."

Friends and family say that although Järvi maintained an upbeat public image, he often struggled privately. Kooli reflected that today he might well have been diagnosed with depression.

Despite being diagnosed with cancer, Järvi chose to keep his illness largely private. He continued working in Parliament and hosting radio programs until he was physically no longer able.

"He didn't want many people to know," his son recalled. "He had always felt the hardest way to leave was to slowly fade away in front of others."

Kooli remembered that Järvi continued broadcasting despite severe pain and diminishing strength. During his final broadcasts, medication affected his speech, leading some listeners to mistakenly assume he was intoxicated.

"Those comments were especially painful," Jürgenson said.

Raivo Järvi. Source: Ülo Josing/ERR

Fourteen years after Järvi's death, the Tartu Art Museum launched a public appeal for works to include in a retrospective exhibition. Nearly 500 pieces were identified in private collections and museums, with around 60 selected for display.

Curator Stella Mõttus said the exhibition reveals aspects of Järvi that many people never saw. While known primarily for the cheerful illustrations loved by children, some of his black-and-white graphic works are dark, unsettling and even apocalyptic.

"His life wasn't exactly rosy either," she said.

Richard-Erik Järvi, however, believes the works convey not only sadness and trauma but also resilience.

"We've talked about the tragic moments," he said, "but he always tried to remain positive."

World.title: US denies Iranian account that missile damaged F-16 over Gulf
World.content:
WASHINGTON: US Central Command on Saturday denied an Iranian account that its forces had fired a missile at a US F-16 fighter jet over the Gulf, damaging the aircraft and forcing it to make an emergency landing.

Iranian state media ⁠earlier reported that ⁠the country’s air defense systems targeted the aircraft on Friday evening, causing it to abort its mission and land at a nearby airport.

“Iran did ⁠not attack a US F-16 fighter aircraft yesterday — at all,” Central Command said in a statement, adding that all US military fighter jets in the Middle East were safe and accounted for.

Iran has made similar accounts during the war of shooting down or ⁠damaging ⁠US aircraft, which the US military has denied.

The war erupted when the United States and Israel attacked Iran in February and has since spread across the Middle East, killing thousands of people, disrupting shipping and pushing up global energy prices.

World.title: Where We Are Going Today: Craving the food in your favorite K-drama? Try Sigdang
World.content:
If you are a fan of Korean dramas and often find yourself craving the food you see characters eating on screen, Sigdang offers a chance to try those dishes for yourself.

The name of the eatery is said to be derived from the Korean word sikdang, meaning “restaurant,” and can often refer to any dining establishment serving homestyle meals and banchan, or side dishes.

It first popped up in Alkhobar in early 2024, as a compact, K-drama-inspired canteen, focused on kitschy, customizable Korean-style snacks and comfort foods.

On my recent visit, I noticed the tiny details instantly; the exterior wall art, the old-school telephone on the counter, the moving digital banner at the top and the layout of the seating area felt reminiscent of my visit to South Korea. And the cute takeaway boxes.

While waiting for my order, I noticed a TV screen playing clips of food scenes from popular K-dramas. I immediately recognized the bowls of noodles from the 2009 hit “Boys Over Flowers” — many of the show’s most memorable moments revolved around everyday Korean comfort foods, and I remembered how much I had wanted to try the dishes I saw on screen when I first watched it. Now, we finally have the chance.

We tried the kimchi noodles for SR22 ($5); the portion was shockingly generous and was my absolute favorite find. This will be on my regular rotation when in Alkhobar.

We also ordered the Asian fried rice for SR24. It was good but since I’m more of a noodles girl, it ranked slightly lower on my scale.

The sweet chilli fried chicken (SR18) was delicious. Little bite-sized bits of chicken paired with the perfect side sauce was a 10/10 snack for me.

They did not have spring rolls or dumplings available on the day of my visit, which is what I need to go back for.

They also had a waraq enab noodle — which I was not brave enough to try — inspired by local favorite flavors. I would be curious as to which K-drama character would eat a plate of that though.

With three locations across the Eastern Province — the original branch in Alkhobar Al-Shamalia, which I visited, the Dhahran ADNOC branch and a Dammam branch in Taybah — there are plenty of opportunities to slurp or munch along.

And of course, if you feel like staying in, you can place an order via the numerous local delivery apps and feast on the goods while watching your K-drama episode uninterrupted.

At some point in the episode, the characters are bound to tuck into something on Sigdang’s menu — or a dish that looks much like it. Just grab your chopsticks, or whatever cutlery you prefer, and join them.

For updates, check their Instagram @hello.sigdang.

World.title: Israeli strike kills three in vehicle distributing aid in Gaza, witnesses say
World.content:
JERUSALEM: An Israeli strike killed three Palestinians in a vehicle carrying papers and food for the World Central Kitchen charity in Gaza City on Saturday, according to Gaza’s health ministry and eyewitnesses.



The Israeli military said several militant operatives were targeted in the area without providing further details. It did not immediately respond to questions on why it had hit a vehicle that appeared to be distributing aid.



World Central Kitchen did not immediately respond to a request for comment.



The vehicle appeared to be carrying packaged foodstuffs, and papers ⁠inside carried the ⁠logo of World Central Kitchen, an aid organization that distributes food in Gaza, according to a Reuters witness.



“It was just about to stop to distribute the food and drink to children when it was hit by a missile,” said Abu Zein Al-Daya, who also witnessed the strike.



Afterwards, meals of cooked rice were scattered around the vehicle, which was partially covered in the ⁠blood of the victims of the attack.

ISRAELI STRIKES CONTINUE IN GAZA



The Israeli military previously killed seven World Central Kitchen workers in a 2024 strike, including citizens of Australia, Britain and Poland.



At the time, the military said there had been “serious errors and breaches of procedure” but in 2026 it said it had found no basis upon which to open criminal investigations into the incident.



Israel briefly launched a ground operation in Gaza earlier this week and killed six in a strike on a hospital that it said was targeting a Hamas commander.



An October 2025 US-backed ceasefire halted major fighting in the shattered ⁠territory but ⁠has not stopped Israeli attacks on Gaza or secured Hamas’ disarmament.



At least 1,600 Palestinians and 5 Israeli soldiers have been killed in the time since, according to respective Palestinian and Israeli tallies.



Israeli troops now control around two-thirds of Gaza, up from more than half at the time of the ceasefire, with Hamas controlling a sliver of territory along Gaza’s coast.



Israel’s more than two-year-long assault on Gaza has killed tens of thousands, caused a hunger crisis, internally displaced Gaza’s entire population and led to assessments of genocide from scholars and a United Nations inquiry.



Israel calls its actions self-defense after Hamas-led militants killed 1,200 people and took more than 250 hostages in an October 2023 attack.

World.title: Pakistan drops former captains Masood and Rizwan from central contracts list
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Cricket Board left out former captains Shan Masood and Mohammad Rizwan from its new format-based central contracts awarded to 38 players Saturday.

Abdullah Shafique, who scored a test century against the West Indies in this World Test Championship cycle, Saim Ayub, Hasan Ali and left-arm spinner Noman Ali are some of the other notable players whose contracts were not renewed.

Pakistan test captain Babar Azam and Salman Ali Agha were named in test and ODI category while only four players — Azan Awais, Mohammad Abbas, Sajid Khan and Saud Shakeel — were given test contracts.

Opening batter Awais, fast bowler Abbas, middle-order batter Shakeel along with Babar and Agha played in Pakistan’s 1-0 victory in the test series against Sri Lanka after beating the tourists by eight wickets in the second test at Rawalpindi on Friday.

“We are going through a phase in which we are bringing in new talent,” said Aqib Javed, the PCB’s high performance director. “The idea is to award contracts to the players who have been active across formats and who the selectors and coaches foresee playing (international matches) in their respective formats.”

Pakistan are last in the WTC points table with three wins in 11 test matches. They will round off their campaign in this WTC cycle with a two-test home series against New Zealand in 2027.

Aix players were given contracts in ODIs: Shaheen Afridi, Abrar Ahmed, Arafat Minhas, Fakhar Zaman, Faheem Ashraf and Haris Rauf.

The PCB also identified seven cricketers in the T20 category of central contract that comprises Hasan Nawaz, Maaz Sadaqat, Salman Mirza, Naseem Shah, Sahibzada Farhan, Shadab Khan and Usman Tariq.

Express fast bowler Razaullah, Tayyab Arif, Mohammad Taha, pace bowler Saqib Khan and wicketkeeper-batter Ghazi Ghori, who all played in the test series against Sri Lanka, were among 19 cricketers handed contracts in development category.

Pakistan all-format coach Mike Hesson said that the majority of Pakistan test players were handed contracts in development category, “because they’ve just come on the scene and shown good signs.”

“This central contract model allows the players to remain focused on the formats they are most likely to be involved in,” he said. “It doesn’t exclude them from the other formats, and it also doesn’t exclude players who are not awarded the contracts, as they can continue to push their case for Pakistan.”

The new contracts run until June 30, 2027.

World.title: Iran says allies China, Russia oppose change in nuclear doctrine
World.content:
TEHRAN: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said China and Russia oppose a change in Tehran’s nuclear doctrine, amid domestic calls for a shift, state media reported.

In an interview published on Saturday, Araghchi told the state-run Iran Daily newspaper that the issue was “broad, serious” and had its own “supporters and opponents.”

“Russia and China are also opposed” to a change in Iran’s doctrine, he added. Both countries have strategic cooperation agreements with Iran.

“What matters is that, up to this point, our doctrine has not changed, and our official positions remain the same as before,” Araghchi said.

Debate over changing Iran’s nuclear doctrine has resurfaced in the country’s political circles, particularly among hard-liners, following wars with Israel and the United States that saw Iranian nuclear facilities come under heavy attack.

Some advocates of a shift argue that it would pave the way for Tehran to develop a nuclear weapon as a deterrent.

Iran has barred the International Atomic Energy Agency from inspecting its nuclear sites, citing security concerns and blaming the agency for failing to condemn US and Israeli attacks on its nuclear facilities.

Last week, the UN nuclear watchdog urged Iran to take “incremental steps” to allow inspectors to return to key facilities, saying such access was “critical.”

Iranian officials continue to cite a fatwa, or religious decree, issued by former supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei that prohibited the development of weapons of mass destruction, including nuclear weapons.

“There are those who believe the country’s nuclear doctrine should be maintained in its current form, and others who speak of the need to change it. Both sides have their own arguments and rationale,” Araghchi said.

Khamenei, was killed in a US-Israeli strike on his compound in central Tehran on February 28, triggering a regional war as Iran responded with missile and drone attacks across the Middle East.

His successor and son, Mojtaba Khamenei, who has remained out of public view since his appointment in March, has not issued a decree that would overturn his father’s ruling.

World.title: Endurance athlete Lewis Pugh swims in Strait of Hormuz to highlight Iran war’s impact on wildlife
World.content:
LONDON: British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh has swum in the North Pole and Antarctica to draw attention to environmental causes. But battling freezing waters and extreme conditions hasn’t prepared him for his latest challenge: swimming the Strait of Hormuz while tankers are attacked and blown up nearby.

Pugh, who is a United Nations Patron of the Oceans, spent three days this week swimming parts of the dangerous waterway to highlight how the war with Iran threatens the area’s habitat and wildlife.

Wearing only swimming trunks, goggles and a cap bearing the UN logo, the athlete started from the Musandam peninsula, on the southern tip of the strait, and ended by rounding the Cape of Hormuz, completing about 15 kilometers in total. Pugh is believed to be the first person to undertake a long-distance swim there since the war started.

British endurance swimmer and UNEP Patron of the Oceans Lewis Pugh swims in the Strait of Hormuz off the Musandam Peninsula, Oman, on Monday.

The swimmer said that minutes after he entered the water on Monday, he heard two loud explosions that rocked the sea.

“I looked up and I could see that an oil tanker about four kilometers away had been hit,” he told The Associated Press after he returned to London. “The explosion was so loud, two booms, and then fighter jets coming in. And at that moment I realized we have to get out of here right now.”

Pugh, 56, managed to finish his feat after more stops and starts, including passing another vessel that sent fireballs into the sky after it was attacked.

British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh swimming in the Strait of Hormuz, off the Musandam Peninsula, Oman, on Wednesday.

“Most people, when they think about the Strait of Hormuz, they think of a shipping lane,” he said. “But it is also one of the most beautiful places I have ever been … it’s one of the treasure troves of the natural world.”

“With all these ships being sunk, this area is under severe threat,” he added. “It’s going to take years, decades for this area to recover.”

Oil pollution from damaged tankers threatens dolphins and mangroves

Iran has in recent weeks increased attacks on vessels that it claimed traveled along unauthorized routes in the strait as it seeks to impose its control on the crucial waterway, where a fifth of all oil traded passed through before the US and Israel launched the war on Feb. 28.

Several tankers have also struck sea mines laid by Tehran, in some cases exploding and bursting into flames, among them one that was carrying over 2 million barrels of oil last month.

Smoke rises from a burning liquefied petroleum gas tanker in the Strait of Hormuz off the Musandam Peninsula, Oman, on Tuesday.

Pugh warned of how oil leaking from the dozens of tankers damaged since February could create lasting problems for the region’s animals, as well as its coastlines, coral reefs and mangrove forests.

He described seeing large numbers of dolphins following his boat as he sailed in, as well as turtles and ospreys. He also marveled at the hundreds of turtles he saw during a swim along the Omani coast before the war.

“When oil gets in there, when chemical pollution gets in there, it becomes very, very difficult to clean up that type of mess,” he said. “It lasts for generations.”

Swim challenge took place as vessels were attacked

Pugh has had plenty of experience facing extreme temperatures and predators, including great white sharks. But swimming in a conflict zone presented entirely new dangers.

To stay safe, the challenge was done in sections over three days, with a total of about six and a half hours of swimming. The athlete recalled seeing a gas carrier being struck as he returned to the harbor on the second day.

British endurance swimmer and UNEP Patron of the Oceans Lewis Pugh aimed to bring attention to the Iran war's impact on habitats and wildlife.

“I’ll never ever forget going past that gas carrier, the smell of the chemicals and then the flames, they were literally like fireballs going up into the sky. Around the ship, the water was on fire,” Pugh said.

“And to think of the impact which a casualty like this has on nature — it was very, very acute.”

Using sport to lobby for green causes

Pugh has spent much of the past 40 years swimming in places from Antarctica to the Red Sea and the English Channel to urge more action to protect marine environments from climate change, pollution and loss of biodiversity.

He was the first athlete to swim across the North Pole and complete a long-distance swim in every one of the world’s oceans. In 2023, he swam all 315 miles (507 kilometers) of the Hudson River to highlight the importance of clean rivers.

His foundation says the challenges have helped secure official agreements to protect more than 3.5 million square kilometers (about 1.35 million square miles) of vulnerable ocean.

Some have dubbed Pugh’s blend of epic swimming and political outreach as “Speedo diplomacy.”

“Sport opens doors, it creates dialogue, it enables people to start thinking about these important issues,” Pugh said.

“My message is very simple,” he added. “We’ve got to stop the war. We’ve got to open the strait, and we’ve got to clean up the pollution.”

World.title: Mexico captures drug kingpin on FBI’s most wanted list
World.content:
MEXICO CITY: Mexico’s military announced on Saturday that it had captured the leader of a drug-trafficking group who was among the 10 most-wanted fugitives sought by US law enforcement.

Fausto Isidro Meza, alias “Chapo Isidro,” and two other leaders of his drug gang were captured during a special force raid Friday night in Sinaloa state, the Mexican National Defense Secretariat announced on X.

A firefight ensued between the military and gang members in the town of Guasave, sparking panic in the surrounding area, including at a professional baseball game, local media reported.

“Chapo Isidro” is the alleged leader of the Beltran Leyva gang, which is allied with one of two rival factions in the powerful Sinaloa cartel, Mexico’s military said.

He was captured alongside his number two in the group and another man identified as a financial operator.

They were all transported by a Mexican Air Force aircraft to Mexico City “to be placed at the disposal of the competent prosecutorial authorities,” the military said.

Chapo Isidro faces criminal charges in both Mexico and the United States.

The FBI had placed him on its list of 10 most wanted fugitives and offered a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest.

Giving his name as Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, the FBI bulletin says his group is responsible for importing “large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl, and marijuana into the United States.”

World.title: Maritime agency says 2 tankers struck in Hormuz, as Iran says ship on fire
World.content:
DUBAI: Two tankers were attacked on Saturday in the Strait of Hormuz, at the heart of the conflict between Iran and the United States, British maritime agency UKMTO said, as Iran said a ship was on fire.

“A tanker transiting outbound in the Strait of Hormuz has been hit on the stern by an unknown projectile. There are no reported casualties at this time,” the agency said, adding that another tanker was struck in its engine room.

Since US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February launched the Middle East war, Tehran has sought to restrict passage through the strategic waterway, and regularly targets ships that transit without its authorization.

Iran’s army on Saturday said a ship was on fire after hitting a mine in the strait.

“Before noon today, a violating oil tanker that had entered a restricted zone east of the Strait of Hormuz caught fire after striking a naval mine,” Iran’s Army naval forces said in a statement carried by state TV.

The tanker “had its identification and navigation systems switched off, in defiance of issued warnings and maritime transit regulations,” it added.

In recent weeks, Tehran has made multiple announcements saying ships have caught fire in the strait, often claiming they struck mines.

But the US military recently said it had cleared all mines from the main routes through the waterway.

Washington has responded to Iran’s chokehold on the strait with a blockade of Iranian ports, and its navy has been escorting tankers through the waterway.

US Central Command, which oversees US military operations in the region, said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.

Iran said on Saturday it shot down a US drone over Qeshm Island in the strait, according to state TV.

American fighter jets struck an Iranian missile site on Qeshm last Tuesday, according to a US military official.

Before the onset of the Middle East war, one fifth of the world’s oil and natural gas passed through the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Iraq qualifies for 2027 AFC U-17 Asian Cup in Uzbekistan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has officially confirmed the final 16-team lineup for the 2027 AFC U-17 Asian Cup, including Iraq, which topped Group B during the qualifiers in Thailand with 10 points—putting the young Lions of Mesopotamia just three group-stage matches away from securing a berth at the 2027 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar.

Under head coach Salam Shaker, Iraq clinched first place in Group B after defeating tournament hosts Thailand 2–1 in their decisive final qualifier in Buriram on Friday, November 20, ending a nine-year continental qualification drought for the national under-17 side.

The finals are scheduled to take place in the Uzbek capital of Tashkent from May 13 to 29, 2027, following the official tournament draw on February 18, 2027.

Per AFC competition regulations, the top eight finishers at the tournament in Uzbekistan—specifically the eight teams that advance out of the group stage into the quarterfinals—will automatically qualify for the 2027 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar.

Reaching the World Cup also carries a secondary continental incentive: under AFC rules, all Asian nations that qualify for the global finals earn direct entry into the 2028 AFC U-17 Asian Cup without having to contest the preliminary qualifying rounds.

The 16 participating nations in Tashkent comprise the seven qualifying group winners alongside the nine AFC representatives from the 2026 FIFA U-17 World Cup who received automatic entry:

Qualification Route Qualified Nations Qualifying Group Winners Iraq (Group B), Indonesia (Group A), Syria (Group C), Iran (Group D), India (Group E), Yemen (Group F), Lebanon (Group G) Automatic Qualifiers Uzbekistan (Hosts), Australia, China PR, Japan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, Tajikistan, Vietnam

Coach Salam Shaker and his squad now shift their focus toward preparing for February’s draw, aiming to replicate the historic success of Iraq’s 2016 U-16 championship generation and re-establish Iraqi youth football on both the Asian and global stages.

World.title: Japanese cyclist killed in highway collision in southern Iraq’s Muthanna Governorate
World.content:
Samawah (IraqiNews.com) – A Japanese bicycle traveler died on Friday, November 20, 2026, following a traffic collision along the Rumaitha–Samawah highway in southern Iraq’s Muthanna Governorate.

According to a security source, the tourist was riding a bicycle along the highway when he collided with a Dodge Charger sedan.

The impact proved fatal for the cyclist and also injured a passenger riding inside the vehicle, identified as a security officer.

Traffic police and forensic investigators conducted an on-site inspection of the crash scene following the incident. Based on their preliminary field assessment, authorities determined that the Japanese cyclist was at fault for the collision.

World.title: Iraqi Energy Police establish 12 checkpoints along Jurf Al Sakhar oil pipelines
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Interior’s Directorate General of Energy Police continued field operations on Saturday, November 21, 2026, to secure vital oil pipeline corridors across the Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr) subdistrict in northern Babylon Governorate.

Marking the second consecutive day since Baghdad formally inaugurated its new joint command center in the area, Energy Police units established full operational control along a pipeline stretch exceeding five kilometers.

In an official statement, Ministry of Interior Head of Relations and Media Major General Miqdad Miri confirmed that the deployment is being directed on the ground by Energy Police Director-General Lieutenant General Hamid Abdullah Ibrahim.

Executing the mission with a regiment from the Commando Brigade (Liwa al-Maghawir), engineering teams deployed specialized heavy machinery to carve a dedicated patrol road parallel to the pipeline bundles through rugged terrain, enabling rapid troop mobility and sustained field surveillance.

To lock down the corridor against illicit tampering, Energy Police established 12 new security checkpoints spaced roughly every 500 meters along the route, alongside a permanent regimental headquarters.

Major General Miri emphasized that these preventive measures are designed to elevate field command, safeguard crude transport infrastructure, and protect national wealth.

The deployment represents the first concrete operational phase following the expiration of Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi’s Friday ultimatum to Kata’ib Hezbollah.

On Friday, November 20, federal authorities inaugurated the joint control headquarters (Al-Musaytir)—commanded under the Federal Police and uniting Army, Federal Police, Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), and Energy Police formations—initiating a permanent security reorganization in Jurf al-Sakhar that includes securing pipeline networks and reopening closed transit arteries to civilian traffic.

World.title: US dollar steadies near 170,000 dinars across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged slightly lower across major domestic parallel markets on Saturday morning, November 21, 2026, hovering right at the 170,000-dinar threshold for retail sales while buying bids settled below that mark across key commercial hubs.

According to morning monitoring figures, physical banknote rates opened across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra as follows:

In Baghdad, currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 170,000 IQD against buying offers of 169,500 IQD per $100.

In Erbil, currency desks quoted retail selling rates slightly higher at 170,050 IQD alongside purchasing bids holding at 170,000 IQD per $100.

In Basra, foreign exchange offices matched Baghdad’s selling quote at 170,000 IQD, with buying offers dipping to 169,250 IQD per $100.

Despite the downward drift at the start of the trading week, parallel cash rates maintain a spread of roughly 18,000 dinars above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar).

World.title: Gulf alternatives may save Excelerate Energy’s LNG project in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Iraq is witnessing rapid on-site progress amid efforts to overcome geopolitical challenges and navigation risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz.

According to project updates, the field team and the materials required for constructing the marine jetty and terminal infrastructure have arrived in Iraq, Attaqa News reported.

US-based Excelerate Energy, which is carrying out the project, expects the pace of work to accelerate over the coming weeks, with construction activities progressing at the marine terminal and the facility’s infrastructure.

The firm aims to complete and commission the project during the second quarter of 2027, following a delay in 2026 caused by the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

Once Iraq begins imports, it will become the sixth Arab nation in history to import LNG—joining Kuwait, Egypt, the UAE, Jordan, and Bahrain.

The consequences of the Iranian conflict have caused delays for Iraq’s LNG project, which had originally planned to open in the third quarter of 2026. As a result, Excelerate Energy has moved the Excelerate Acadia, its floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), to Jordan for nine months.

To overcome disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the company plans to utilize an FSRU already stationed within the region, eliminating the need to traverse the strategic waterway.

The company is likely to utilize the FSRU currently stationed in the UAE, known as Express.

The US firm indicated that it is working to arrange the import of LNG from countries within the Gulf region, a statement that strongly suggests Qatar or the UAE.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Iraq’s parallel market
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced a slight increase on Thursday in both Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,706.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,706 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,710 Iraqi dinars and 1,700 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also increased, fluctuating between 1,709.5 and 1,708.5 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following the cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Iraqi PM orders reopening of closed roads in Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, ordered on Thursday to expedite the reopening of all closed roads in the Jurf al-Sakhar district in the central province of Babil.

During his meeting with security officials, al-Zaidi emphasized that the army and security forces would uphold the authority of the state across all Iraqi territory, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister emphasized that the enforcement of state authority would be carried out in accordance with the constitution and the law. He affirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the lives and interests of citizens across the country and to preventing any violations or assaults on public and private properties.

According to al-Zaidi, the security forces operate as a unified entity, with their numerous branches and units cooperating with one another.

These directives come ahead of the deadline set by the government for Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed militant faction, to withdraw from Jurf al-Sakhar—a deadline expiring on Friday—paving the way for security forces to enter and redeploy in the area.

The deadline for the withdrawal from Jurf al-Sakhar, also known as Jurf al-Nasr, follows an investigation by a government committee, which Baghdad stated uncovered evidence of oil smuggling operations in the area.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Iraq’s trade exchange with China drops to $19.8 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Chinese Ambassador to Iraq, Xiang Bo, said on Thursday that the decline in trade exchange with Iraq—which fell to $19.8 billion—is due to the escalating security tensions in the region.

During a press conference in Baghdad, Bo projected that trade between the two countries would recover, reaching $26 billion by the end of 2026 or early 2027.

According to Bo, China is a trusted partner to Iraq. He noted that the two countries share deep historical and cultural ties, dating back thousands of years.

Bo emphasized that bilateral relations have seen significant development, with Iraq serving as a key trade partner. Trade volume between the two countries reached $51 billion in 2025, reflecting the strength of their mutual commitments and relationship.

Bo mentioned earlier that major Chinese firms are involved in the construction and development of several industries in Iraq, such as oil, energy, and infrastructure.

The Chinese diplomat expressed his hope that this collaboration will continue and grow into other sectors, contributing to the development of a complete partnership between Iraq and China.

Chinese companies have been heavily involved in the oil industry and in significant infrastructure projects, such as the construction of major bridges and schools, with more than 600 schools completed in several Iraqi provinces.

World.title: 'Don't dislike BJP': Shehzad Poonawalla on quitting politics; calls rift with brother ideological
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former

spokesperson and Rise & Fall Season 2 winner Shehzad Poonawalla has said that his decision to quit active politics was not driven by any dislike for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

He also described his political differences with brother Tehseen Poonawalla as a "battle of principles" rather than a personal conflict.

In an interview with news agency ANI, Shehzad reaffirmed his support for Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath and Union home minister Amit Shah. He said he continued to hold the BJP in high regard and pointed to his choice of clothing as a sign of his association with the party.



"Why did I leave politics? It wasn't because I dislike the BJP; if I disliked them, I wouldn't be walking around wearing their T-shirt," he said.

Speaking about his differences with his brother, Shehzad alleged that the issues raised by Tehseen were not in the nation's interest. He also claimed that his brother was aligned with Congress leader

's team.

"I'm just glad these people weren't around during the time of the Mahabharata; otherwise, they would have claimed that the conflict between the Pandavas and the Kauravas was also just a publicity stunt! Our conflict isn't a personal one; it's a battle over principles.





I feel that the issues he raises aren't actually in the nation's interest. In a way, it seems like he's part of Rahul Gandhi's teamâmuch like how Arvind Kejriwal pushed Abhijeet Dipke to the forefront because his own credibility had hit zero," he said.

He further contrasted his political loyalties with those of his brother, calling Tehseen a representative of the Congress and describing himself as an open supporter of the BJP's top leadership.

"Tehseen Poonawalla acts as 'Hamza Mazari' for the Congress. As for me, I'm an openly declared supporter of Modi, Yogi, and Amit Shah. For Uttar Pradesh, the combination of Modi and Yogi is only 'useful.' Yes, I have worked both with Rahul Gandhi and Modijiâand that's precisely why I can say, with my eyes closed, that this country won't see another Prime Minister like Modi-ji for the next 100 years," he said.

Why Shehzad Poonawalla left active politics

Explaining his political journey, Shehzad said he had initially planned to remain with the BJP until the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

However, he continued working with the party through several subsequent state elections before deciding to return to the media.

"I left the Congress and joined the media, where I earned a very good salary as an anchor. Then, in 2021, I joined the BJP, with the intention of staying for about three to four years, until the 2024 elections. Then, there were crucial elections in Haryana, Maharashtra, and Bihar, and by the time those concluded, along with the Bengal elections, two years had passed; I moved on.

After that, I decided to step away from politics and return to the media," he said.

Shehzad also shared his views on Hindu identity and Hindutva, arguing that everyone living in India should identify as Hindu. He referred to the country as Bharat and Hindustan while explaining his position.

"Every person in this country is a Hindu, and everyone ought to be a 'Hindutva-vadi'. What else is this country called, besides Bharat? It is also known as Hindustan.

And what does that imply? It means that anyone who lives here is a Hindu," he said.

What Shehzad said about Rise & Fall Season 2 win\

Reflecting on his victory in reality show Rise & Fall Season 2, Shehzad said winning the trophy was not his idea of a true political rise. He said he would consider it a bigger achievement if Yogi Adityanath secured another electoral victory in 2027 and Modi returned to power in 2029.

World.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to reach Delhi on Sunday for his first foreign bilateral trip - what's on agenda
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

Balendra Shah will begin a two-day state visit to India on Sunday, his first overseas bilateral state visit since taking office in March.

"The visit will serve as an important opportunity to review our wide-ranging cooperative partnership with a forward-looking perspective, maximising mutual benefits for the peoples of both countries," Nepal's foreign ministry said in a statement.

Shah, an ex-Kathmandu mayor and a former rapper, will be accompanied by a 34-member delegation comprising finance minister Swarnim Wagle, foreign affairs minister Shishir Khanal, his chief advisor Kumar Byanjankar, and other senior government officials.

Balendra Shah's itinerary in New Delhi

Shah is scheduled to hold delegation-level talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday, after which they will jointly inaugurate several energy-related projects.



The two sides will also sign and exchange bilateral agreements covering various areas of cooperation.

The two prime ministers will address a joint press conference, followed by a luncheon hosted by PM Modi in honour of the visiting Nepali leader.

During his visit, Shah will also call on President Droupadi Murmu and pay tributes at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial at Rajghat.

He is also scheduled to attend the Nepal-India Business Forum, which aims to strengthen trade and economic ties between the two countries.





What's likely to be discussed

According to ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, India and Nepal are expected to discuss issues including development cooperation and people-to-people ties.

"All these issues will be discussed: development cooperation, people-to-people ties, energy ties, connectivity, and some of the newer areas of cooperation such as startups, technology, innovation, and sports. Cricket links have also become an important connection between India and Nepal.

This is a very important visit for us," Jaiswal told reporters at a weekly news briefing in New Delhi on Friday.

Shah is also expected to discuss Indian assistance for the reconstruction of areas affected by the devastating floods in August, Reuters reported, citing Nepalese officials.

The August 26 floods killed 1,500 people, left more than 5,200 missing and destroyed roads, bridges, power plants, farms and homes.

Nepal is also likely to discuss with India an additional route for commercial flights from the west to Bhairahawa, near Lumbini, the birthplace of Gautam Buddha, and the tourist city of Pokhara.

World.title: 'Goondaism isn't a bug': BJP, BRS attack Congress over Meta office vandalism
World.content:

and BRS on Saturday accused the ruling

of damaging Hyderabad's business-friendly image after Youth Congress workers vandalised the Meta office in the city on November 20, alleging that the incident had hurt 'Brand Hyderabad' and raised questions about the safety of companies operating in Telangana.

"Goondaism isn't a bug" in Congress culture but a "feature", he said.

World.title: 'Modi ji should apologise': Congress alleges PM's Lucknow event led to cancellation of four weddings
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former Uttar Pradesh

chief

on Saturday demanded an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, alleging that his event in Lucknow led to the cancellation of four weddings scheduled at Indira Gandhi Pratishthan.

Speaking to ANI, Rai said the venue had been booked months in advance by four families for their children's weddings, but the arrangements were disrupted after the Prime Minister's programme was scheduled at the same location.

World.title: N-safety regulator AERB grants criticality nod to Rajasthan’s N-plant unit-8, reactor moves closer to power generation
World.content:
In a big milestone in the domestic nuclear sector, Indiaâs nuclear safety regulator Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) has granted permission for the first approach to criticality of Rajasthan atomic power project unit-8 (RAPP-8) at Rawatbhata in Chittorgarh following satisfactory completion of safety reviews.

The AERB clearance on Nov 19 marks a significant step towards bringing the indigenously developed 700 MWe pressurised heavy water reactor (PHWR) closer to commercial electricity generation subject to satisfactory completion of prescribed tests and regulatory permissions. The first approach to criticality (FAC) represents the stage when a nuclear reactor starts a controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction for the first time at low power.



The reactor had commenced fuel loading at the 700 MW unit-8 in Sept.

AERB's permission follows a comprehensive safety review of the reactor's design, construction, commissioning test results and operational preparedness. The regulatory review process included detailed assessments by AERB and its safety review committees, complemented by regulatory inspections, and deliberations by the Board of AERB, govt said on Friday.





RAPP-8 is the fourth unit of India's indigenously designed and constructed 700 MWe PHWR series. The other three units of this design are Kakrapar atomic power station units 3 and 4 in Gujarat and RAPP unit-7 in Rajasthan. This site currently has eight NPP units.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

India's PHWR series forms the backbone of the first stage of the country's three-stage nuclear power programme, using heavy water as both moderator and coolant with natural uranium oxide fuel.

Designed by Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) and operated by Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL), the indigenous series has scaled up from 220 MWe to 540 MWe and 700 MWe units.

Currently there are 19 units of various types operational at various locations in India (14 IPHWR-220, 2 IPHWR - 540 and 3 IPHWR-700) and 13 more IPHWR-700 reactors planned or under construction.

India currently has 8.78 GW of installed nuclear power capacity across 24 operating reactors, contributing roughly 3.1% of total electricity generation in 2025â26. It plans to reach 100 GW by 2047 under its Nuclear Energy Mission. Nine reactor units (7.5 GW combined capacity), including 500 MWe indigenous Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR), which achieved first criticality in April this year, are under construction.

Ten additional reactors are in the pipeline.

World.title: 'Working to suppress India’s rise': US panel report flags China's support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor
World.content:
The US panel report says China is using military, maritime and economic pressure to constrain India's rise, while strengthening its support for Pakistan

What report said on China suppressing India's rise

China-Pakistan military partnership

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Chinaâs military support to Pakistan during the May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict added to New Delhiâs security challenges and raised concerns about a possible two-front threat, a US congressional commission report has said. The report said Beijing has been working across military, economic and maritime domains to constrain Indiaâs rise as a strategic power.The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, in its report on Chinaâs efforts to expand global power and influence, said the conflict following Operation Sindoor highlighted how Beijing could strengthen Pakistan during a crisis without directly entering the fighting.According to the report, Pakistan used advanced weaponry procured from China during the fighting. It also said China reportedly increased pressure on India by deploying a survey vessel with advanced sensors around waters within India's exclusive economic zone (EEZ) as tensions escalated.The report further noted that military officials in India had claimed after the conflict that Pakistan may have received real-time satellite imagery or other intelligence support from Beijing.China neither confirmed nor overtly denied the claim, it said.In May 2026, China's state-run CCTV aired an interview with Zhang Heng, an engineer from the Aviation Industry Corporation (AVIC) of China's Chengdu Aircraft Design and Research Institute, a key developer of fighter aircraft and uncrewed autonomous vehicles. Zhang confirmed that he and other Chinese AVIC personnel provided onsite technical support in Pakistan during the May 2025 conflict, the report said.The report said Indiaâs size, military strength and strategic location make it a significant factor in the long-term competition with China. It noted that India is the worldâs most populous country and largest democracy, and shares a 2,100-mile contested border with China. Its position along key sea lanes in the Indian Ocean also gives it strategic importance.âChina understands this, and it is actively working to suppress Indiaâs rise across multiple domains,â the report said.It said Beijing was continuing its military buildup, asserting sovereignty claims along the disputed border, deepening military support for Pakistan and expanding its naval and surveillance presence in the Indian Ocean.The report described China's economic leverage as its âsharpest toolâ. It said Beijing was âusing its control over critical industrial inputs, technology, and expertise to preserve its manufacturing advantages and make it harder for India to build competing capacityâ.Citing examples, the report said China had ârestricted exports of key inputs and products to India to exert economic pressureâ, ârecalled engineers and withheld equipment to slow Indiaâs electronics manufacturingâ, and âslashed pharmaceutical input prices to undercut new Indian plantsâ. It also said Beijing had imposed export controls on battery technology to impede the development of India's clean energy industry.The report further flagged China's move in 2025 to require Indian firms to certify that certain Chinese-supplied inputs would not be re-exported to the US. While Beijing suspended the requirement as part of the broader Trump-Xi trade dÃ©tente, the report said it remained âa lever that can turn Indiaâs dependence on China into a weapon aimed at U.S. supply chainsâ.The report said China's growing military partnership with Pakistan has made the possibility of a two-front contingency an increasingly critical concern for India. Beijing has deepened its ties with Islamabad since the 1962 Sino-Indian war, with cooperation spanning defence, infrastructure and economic sectors."Chinaâs evolving military partnership with Pakistan has made a two-front contingency an increasingly critical concern for India. The May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict demonstrated how China could strengthen Pakistan during a crisis without Beijing entering the fighting directly, adding to Indiaâs concerns about how a future conflict with Pakistan could develop," it said.China is Pakistan's main defence supplier, accounting for 81% of its arms imports between 2020 and 2024, the report said.It added that China's military support to Pakistan has magnified the strategic challenges India faces in its longstanding rivalry with Islamabad, raising concerns that a conflict with one could escalate into a challenge involving both.

World.title: 'When you promote rakshasas': BJP MP Nishikant Dubey takes swipe at Meta amid youth Congress protests
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

MP Nishikant Dubey on Saturday took a swipe at Meta, saying the social media giant should now realise the consequences of promoting "demons and monsters".

His remarks came after the Indian Youth Congress (IYC), the Congress' youth wing, staged a protest outside Meta's offices in India, alleging that the accounts of its leaders had been suspended at the behest of the ruling BJP.

Dubey, however, claimed that Meta had designed its algorithms to favour the Congress.

"There is a lesson here for Meta. The algorithm they have designed is tailored in favour of the Congress," PTI quoted the BJP MP as saying.

"When you promote 'rakshas' (demons) and 'danav' (monsters), what else do you expect the outcome to be? Meta, including X and Facebook, needs to understand this," he added.

Meanwhile, the IYC issued a seven-day "ultimatum" to Meta, demanding that it restore restricted accounts and posts within the deadline.



The IYC's warning came amid allegations that Meta, which owns Instagram, had suspended or restricted accounts and removed posts belonging to key party functionaries, including national president Uday Bhanu Chib and national in-charge Manish Sharma.

On Friday, Telangana Youth Congress workers protested at Meta's Hyderabad office, accusing the company of "censorship." Around 20 protesters were taken into preventive custody and released after approximately three hours.

World.title: 'Voices carry no weight': Wangchuk warns Ladakh's alienation could hurt national security during war
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Climate activist

on Saturday accused the

of treating the Union Territory "like a colony", alleging that decisions were being imposed on people without their consent.

Addressing a press conference along with Leh Apex Body chairman Chering Dorje Lakruk, Wangchuk warned that the continued alienation of the strategically sensitive border region could have serious consequences for national security.

"Ladakh has effectively become a colony where the voices of local people carry no weight and decisions are simply imposed on them. How can such a system continue?" Wangchuk asked.



"Ladakh has stood with the country during previous wars, and it should continue to do so. Why are such loyal and patriotic people being repeatedly subjected to this treatment?" he said.

Warning against alienating people in a strategically sensitive border region, Wangchuk said the consequences of imposing decisions on them might not be immediately apparent during peacetime but could become significant during a conflict.





"They may not be able to do much in peacetime, but there could be differences in times of war," he said, urging the Centre to ensure that people in Ladakh enjoy the same democratic rights as citizens elsewhere in the country.

According to news agency PTI, Wangchuk also urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi and defence minister Rajnath Singh to intervene, saying the issue should be examined from a national security perspective rather than being left solely to the lieutenant governor's administration or the ministry of home affairs.

He also called for an inquiry commission under the Union home ministry to examine the grievances of local government employees and officers and assess their views on the administration's functioning.

Wangchuk claimed that even employees belonging to Ladakh were deeply unhappy with the manner in which decisions were being taken.

His remarks came amid continuing protests over Ladakh's political and constitutional demands and the ongoing electoral process.

Earlier, Wangchuk, a prominent member of the Leh Apex Body (LAB), alleged that around 20-25 police and paramilitary personnel had been stationed outside his residence, restricting his movement.

In a video message posted on his social media accounts, including X and Facebook, the activist claimed that security personnel, vehicles and tents had been positioned around his house, with armed personnel deployed on all sides.

He alleged that the restrictions were imposed while he and other members of the LAB and the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) were preparing to stage a sit-in protest over various demands concerning Ladakh.

The proposed demonstration was also linked to concerns over the timing of the upcoming elections to the Autonomous Hill Development Councils, scheduled for December 4.

The police, however, denied that Wangchuk had been placed under house arrest.

The clarification came after the activist alleged that he had been confined to his residence after being taken away from a protest site and escorted home on November 11.

"Police arrangements which (were) placed to ensure compliance with prohibitory order have been withdrawn," Leh district police said in a post on X.

The police further stated that the prohibitory order had been issued by the Additional District Magistrate (ADM) of Leh and denied claims that Wangchuk was under house arrest.

"ADM Leh has passed a prohibitory order against Shri Sonam Wangchuk. It is clarified that he was not put under any house arrest as has been claimed," the statement said.

World.title: Skywalk, flyover planned at Konanakunte Cross
World.content:
The State government is planning both a skywalk and a flyover at the busy Konanakunte Cross, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said. “Pedestrian movement has increased with the metro station and the traffic has also shot up,” he said, directing officials to plan a skywalk at the junction to ensure safe and convenient connectivity for pedestrians. He also asked them to ensure that it did not affect or obstruct the proposed flyover construction.

Flyover at the junction

Earlier this year, the special purpose vehicle, Bengaluru Smart Infrastructure Limited (B-SMILE), obtained government approval to construct a flyover at the junction, citing increasing traffic volumes that had led to congestion even on connecting roads.

Mr. Gowda said the tendering process for the project is currently underway. He made the announcement after inaugurating the third phase of the Ward One Campaign at Konanakunte Cross on Saturday.

“B-SMILE has prepared a plan to construct a split-type flyover, with elevated stretches of approximately 600 metres on either side of the junction.
